Show two months side by side when the user frequently selects dates that span a month boundary.

For a custom month view, use useCalendarNavigation and useCalendarDays from @astryxdesign/core/Calendar. To show another calendar system, pass the same calendar to both and feed visibleCalendarMonths into useCalendarDays. The hooks default to gregory and never read the InternationalizationProvider calendar.
Use a calendar for dates far in the past or future like a birth date. A text input is faster for open-ended entry.
Disable large blocks of dates without context. The user should understand why dates are unavailable.

anatomy.name: Calendar root
anatomy.description: The container that holds the month header and the day grid.

anatomy.name: Month header
anatomy.description: The month name and year with navigation arrows to move between months. The arrows mirror automatically under dir="rtl".

anatomy.name: Day grid
anatomy.description: A 7-column grid of days with column headers for the day names.

anatomy.name: Day button
anatomy.description: One day in the grid; the control a date is picked with.

anatomy.name: Range band
anatomy.description: The band behind the days of a selected range, rounded at its first and last day.

anatomy.name: Range preview band
anatomy.description: The band behind the days a hover would select, before the range is picked.

anatomy.name: Selected day
anatomy.description: The currently selected date, highlighted. In range mode, the start and end dates plus the days between them.

anatomy.name: Today marker
anatomy.description: A subtle indicator on the current date for orientation.

components.name: Card
components.description: Card is a bordered, elevated container for discrete, self-contained items: things you could reorder, remove, or interact with independently. Cards are NOT the default layout tool. Most content groups don't need a container at all; spacing and alignment create visual grouping naturally. Only reach for a Card when items need clear interaction boundaries or visual comparison in a grid.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the card (number = pixels, string = used as-is). In a flex row or grid track this is the preferred width: the card shrinks below it when the row is narrower. To hold the width in a flex row, wrap the card in StackItem (static by default) and let the row wrap or scroll. In Grid, set a consumer minWidth on the Card and size the track accordingly.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the card (number = pixels, string = used as-is).

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: Maximum width of the card.

props.name: minHeight
props.description: Minimum height of the card.

props.name: children
props.description: Content to render inside the card: one discrete item; a page’s people, principles or contacts are page content, so set them under headings with Dividers or in one List, not a Card each, on a phone too.

props.name: padding
props.defaultValue: the theme's card padding (spacing step 4 with no theme)
props.description: Internal padding using the spacing scale. Omit it and the card takes the theme's card padding rather than a step, so passing a step is a decision to override the theme, not a way to restate the default.

props.name: variant
props.description: Background color variant. `default` uses the standard card background. `transparent` drops the background entirely. `muted` uses the muted background for de-emphasised cards. The non-semantic variants use the corresponding `--color-background-<name>` token.

props.name: elevation
props.description: Resting shadow depth. `none` is flat; `low`/`med`/`high` map to the shadow token scale. Raise a card only when it needs to float above surrounding content.

bestPractices.text: Ask "could I reorder or remove this independently?" If yes, it's a card. If no, it's just a section of the page: use a heading + Stack or Section.
Use cards for discrete items: a single user profile, a single notification, a single metric, a product in a grid. Each card represents one "thing" with clear interaction boundaries.
Spacing and alignment alone create visual grouping. Not everything needs a container; try removing the card and see if the grouping is still clear from whitespace and typography.
Keep padding consistent across sibling cards so they align visually in a grid or list.
Pair a card with Layout when you need a structured header, scrollable content, and footer with actions.

Let cards share a row or grid on a phone: a card shrinks to fit its track and clips content that cannot wrap at its edge. Truncate long IDs, hashes, and URLs with Text maxLines={1} (the full value shows in a tooltip), and give wide content its own scroll region: Table scrolls by itself; put code or other wide content in a ScrollableArea.
Default to cards for visual grouping. A heading + Stack with proper spacing creates hierarchy without adding borders everywhere. Cards should be the exception, not the default.
Wrap page sections in cards. "General Settings", "Notification Preferences", form groups: these are page regions, use Section or heading + stack.
Create identical card grids (icon + heading + text, repeated). Vary the layout or question whether cards are needed at all.
Nest cards inside other cards; flatten the hierarchy or use spacing and dividers instead.
Use color variants for status; use Banner or Badge for that. Color cards are for categorization.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: The outer box with border, background, border-radius, and padding.

anatomy.name: Content
anatomy.description: Any children rendered inside the card. Often a stack of heading, text, and actions.

components.name: Carousel
components.description: Carousel scrolls a row of items horizontally when they overflow the available width. Use it for card grids, image galleries, product lists, or any set of items that should be browsable without taking up the full page.

props.name: children
props.description: Carousel items rendered in a horizontal scroll container.

props.name: gap
props.description: Gap between items using the spacing token scale.

props.name: hasButtons
props.description: Show prev/next navigation buttons when content is scrollable.

props.name: hasEdgeFade
props.description: Show a gradient edge-fade mask when content overflows, signalling that more items exist off-screen.

props.name: hasLoop
props.description: Wrap-around scrolling: next at the end scrolls to the start, prev at the start scrolls to the end. Buttons stay visible at both edges. Only engages when content overflows.

props.name: hasSnap
props.description: Snap each child to the start edge. hasSnap uses native CSS scroll snap. hasSnap={useSnapPaging()} adds iOS paging under a finger and on a trackpad swipe, on the same stops: a flick moves one view, or one item with useSnapPaging({pages: 'item'}). Only that value loads the paging code.

props.name: padding
props.description: Inline padding inside the scroll container, with matching scroll-padding so snap points align to the content edge.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible label for the carousel region.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the root element.

props.name: handleRef
props.description: Imperative handle exposing scrollNext(), scrollPrev(), scrollTo(index), canScrollNext(), and canScrollPrev() for programmatic scroll control.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the root element. Prefer xstyle.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

bestPractices.text: Enable scroll-snap when each item should land precisely at the start edge, like a gallery or product list.

For iOS paging under a finger and on a trackpad swipe, pass hasSnap={useSnapPaging()} from @astryxdesign/core/SnapPaging. A flick moves one view, or one item with useSnapPaging({pages: 'item'}). A mouse wheel keeps native snapping. Only a carousel given it loads the paging code.
Reach for hasLoop on small, cyclable sets like a photo gallery, where wrapping past the last item back to the first feels natural.
Always provide an aria-label that describes what the carousel contains, like "Featured products" or "Team members".

Carousel implements the WAI-ARIA APG carousel pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/carousel/) without auto-rotation: the region is labelled and carries aria-roledescription="carousel", each item is a group named "Slide N of M", and the scroll container is a tab stop while its content overflows, so keyboard users can pan it with the arrow keys; while everything fits it stays out of the tab order.
Use a consistent gap and item width so the carousel looks intentional, not like content overflowing by accident.
Trust the built-in navigation: trackpad users can swipe horizontally, and mouse users can hold Shift while scrolling the wheel to move through items.
Use a carousel for content every user must see. Not everyone scrolls horizontally, so put critical content above the fold.
Auto-advance items. Let the user scroll at their own pace.
Nest carousels. A carousel inside a carousel is confusing and breaks keyboard navigation.

anatomy.name: Scroll container
anatomy.description: The horizontal overflow area that holds all items.

anatomy.name: Items
anatomy.description: The children rendered in a row inside the scroll container. With hasSnap, each item snaps to the start edge.

anatomy.name: Fade edges
anatomy.description: Gradient fades on the left and right edges that indicate more content is available. Enabled by default, disable with hasEdgeFade={false}.

anatomy.name: Navigation buttons
anatomy.description: Prev/next buttons that appear when the content can scroll in that direction. Enabled by default, disable with hasButtons={false}.

components.name: Center
components.description: Center aligns content to the middle of its container. Use it for empty states, loading screens, login forms, or any content that should sit in the center of the available space.

props.name: axis
props.description: Which Center mode to use. In horizontal writing, "horizontal" centers the flex main/inline axis and "vertical" centers the cross/block axis. In vertical writing, current single-axis behavior follows those logical flex axes rather than the physical names; "both" still centers both axes.

props.name: width
props.description: Container width (px or CSS value).

props.name: height
props.description: Container height (px or CSS value).

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: Maximum container width (px or CSS value).

props.name: minHeight
props.description: Minimum container height (px or CSS value).

props.name: padding
props.description: Inner padding on all sides, using the spacing scale (0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10). Matches the padding prop on Stack, Card, LayoutContent, and LayoutPanel. Pass as a JSX number expression e.g. padding={3}.

props.name: paddingInline
props.description: Logical inline-axis padding, using the spacing scale. Overrides padding on the inline axis when both are set.

props.name: paddingInlineStart
props.description: Logical inline-start padding, using the spacing scale. Its resolved physical edge depends on writing mode and direction. Overrides paddingInline and padding on that edge only.

props.name: paddingInlineEnd
props.description: Logical inline-end padding, using the spacing scale. Its resolved physical edge depends on writing mode and direction. Overrides paddingInline and padding on that edge only.

props.name: paddingBlock
props.description: Logical block-axis padding, using the spacing scale. Overrides padding on the block axis when both are set.

props.name: paddingBlockStart
props.description: Logical block-start padding, using the spacing scale. Its resolved physical edge depends on writing mode. Overrides paddingBlock and padding on that edge only.

props.name: paddingBlockEnd
props.description: Logical block-end padding, using the spacing scale. Its resolved physical edge depends on writing mode. Overrides paddingBlock and padding on that edge only.

props.name: isInline
props.description: Use inline-flex (useful for text/icons).

props.name: children
props.description: Content to center.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

bestPractices.text: Use a single-axis value only in horizontal writing, or after verifying the active writing mode. In vertical writing, the current implementation follows flex main/cross axes rather than the physical prop names.
In horizontal writing, give Center height when using axis="vertical"; centering needs available space on the selected flex axis.
Use isInline to center small elements like icons or badges within a line of text without breaking the text flow.
Keep semantic structure and accessible names on the content. Center is a layout-only container and does not add a role or label.
Wrap large page sections in Center. Use Layout or AppShell for page-level structure.
Use Center for horizontal lists of items. Use Stack with hAlign="center" instead.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: A flexbox wrapper that aligns its children to the center along the chosen axis.

anatomy.name: Content
anatomy.description: Any children passed to Center. Typically a card, form, spinner, or empty state message.

components.name: Chat
components.description: Chat is a family of composable primitives for building AI and human chat experiences. Combine ChatLayout, ChatMessageList, ChatMessage, bubbles, system messages, tool calls, tokenized text, and ChatComposer to assemble complete conversations without reimplementing sender-aware layout, density, scrolling, or composer behavior.

bestPractices.text: Compose messages using MessageList > Message > Bubble for consistent sender-aware styling and density.
Set the density prop to control spacing globally: compact for sidebars, balanced for most views, spacious for long-form reading. Individual messages can override.
Use gap when top-level rows are independent (for example, LLM tool events or streamed blocks) and list spacing needs to be tuned separately from density.
Use the group prop on bubbles (first, middle, last) when a single sender sends multiple consecutive messages; it tightens corner radius to visually connect them.
Use ChatSystemMessage with variant="divider" for date separators and default for inline status notices like joins, leaves, or topic changes.
Put name on the first bubble and metadata on the last bubble in a message so they align with the bubble's inline padding.

Wrap custom in-message content (cards, attachments, citations) in a ghost bubble so it aligns with the bubble text column; add width="100%" when it should span the full message column instead of the default bubble width cap.
Provide an emptyState prop so new users see a clear prompt to start a conversation instead of a blank screen.
Use the ghost bubble variant for AI-style responses that show rich content like code blocks or markdown without a visible boundary.
Don't use ChatSystemMessage for sender content; it has no avatar, alignment, or bubble. Use ChatMessage with a sender role instead.
Don't put long or multi-line content in a system message; keep it to a single short sentence. If you need more, use a bubble or a card.
Don't nest ChatMessage inside another ChatMessage; each message is a standalone article element with its own sender context.

anatomy.name: Message area
anatomy.description: Scrollable region for messages. Renders children (typically ChatMessageList) in a flex column that pushes content to the bottom when the list is short.

anatomy.name: Frosted glass dock
anatomy.description: Sticky or fixed container at the bottom with a backdrop-blur layer. Houses the scroll button and composer.

anatomy.name: Scroll-to-bottom button
anatomy.description: Appears when the user scrolls up or new messages arrive. Defaults to ChatLayoutScrollButton; pass null to hide or a custom element to override.

anatomy.name: Composer
anatomy.description: The input area for sending messages, typically ChatComposer. Docked at the bottom inside the frosted glass layer.

anatomy.name: Empty state
anatomy.description: Centered placeholder shown when no messages exist. Use EmptyState for a consistent look.

anatomy.name: Avatar
anatomy.description: A sender avatar rendered beside the message. Typically Avatar with size="md". Hidden for system messages.

anatomy.name: Name
anatomy.description: Sender name above the message body. Place on the bubble when using bubbles, or on the message wrapper for raw content.

anatomy.name: Content
anatomy.description: The message body: one or more ChatMessageBubble elements, or any free-form ReactNode like images or tool calls. Wrap non-bubble content in a ghost bubble to align it with the bubble text column.

anatomy.name: Metadata
anatomy.description: Timestamp, delivery status, and footer actions below the message. Place on the last bubble or on the message wrapper.

components.name: ChatComposer
components.description: ChatComposer is the message-entry shell for a chat surface. It coordinates a controlled or uncontrolled draft, provides a default token-capable input and send/stop action, and arranges optional drawer, header, footer, and status content. Custom inputs and send controls can join the same value, submission, disabled, stop, and focus contract through useChatComposerContext().

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Called when the user submits a message.

props.name: onStop
props.description: Called when the user requests to stop generation.

props.name: isStopShown
props.description: Whether the stop button is shown instead of the send button.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled input value.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Change handler for controlled mode.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when the input is empty.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the composer.

props.name: density
props.description: Visual density.

props.name: elevation
props.description: Resting elevation of the composer body. `low` (the default) keeps today's raised look: low at rest, bumping to med on hover / focus. `none` flattens it and draws a border. Keyboard focus in the editor adds the shared focus ring in either presentation; pointer focus does not add that ring.

props.name: drawer
props.description: Slot: collapsible drawer above the input: attachments, context chips, etc. Use ChatComposerDrawer.

props.name: headerActions
props.description: Slot: left-aligned header actions (attach, mention buttons). Use icon-only size="sm" buttons.

props.name: headerContext
props.description: Slot: right-aligned contextual info in the header (context window usage, ProgressBar, supporting text).

props.name: input
props.description: Slot: custom input element. Replaces the default input. Use ChatComposerInput for trigger menus/tokens, or wire any input (plain textarea, rich editor) to the composition contract via useChatComposerContext(): read value/onChange/onSubmit/canSend and register a focus control on inputControlRef so body-click-to-focus works.

props.name: footerActions
props.description: Slot: left-aligned footer actions (model selector, etc).

props.name: sendActions
props.description: Slot: actions to the left of the send button.

props.name: sendButton
props.description: Slot: custom send button. Replaces the default send/stop button.

props.name: status
props.description: Status message rendered below (or above) the composer.

props.name: statusPosition
props.description: Where to render the status.

anatomy.name: Composer frame
anatomy.description: Outer composition root that groups the body with an optional status message above or below it.

anatomy.name: Composer body
anatomy.description: Rounded, elevated surface containing the header, input, and footer.

anatomy.name: Drawer
anatomy.description: Content before the body for attachments or other expandable context, typically ChatComposerDrawer.

anatomy.name: Header
anatomy.description: Row for start-aligned actions and end-aligned contextual information.

anatomy.name: Input
anatomy.description: Default ChatComposerInput or a custom editor connected through useChatComposerContext().

anatomy.name: Footer
anatomy.description: Row for caller-supplied footer and send actions plus the primary action.

anatomy.name: Send or stop action
anatomy.description: Default ChatSendButton or a custom sendButton; it submits the current draft or requests interruption.

anatomy.name: Status message
anatomy.description: Error or warning feedback rendered before or after the composer body.

components.name: ChatComposerDrawer
components.description: Use ChatComposerDrawer in the ChatComposer drawer slot for supplementary content such as attachments, context chips, or previews. Provide count only when people should be able to collapse that content.

props.name: children
props.description: Content to render inside the drawer: tokens, chips, previews, or any React elements.

props.name: count
props.description: Total item count shown in the collapsed badge. When provided, the drawer gains a collapse/expand toggle.

props.name: label
props.description: Label shown next to the count in the default collapsed summary and used to name the expand/collapse action.

props.name: collapsedSummary
props.description: Visual content for the complete Collapsed summary anatomy part. When count enables collapse, this replaces the default neutral Badge and label while the component retains disclosure behavior and accessible naming.

props.name: isCollapsed
props.description: Controlled collapsed state. Use with `onCollapsedChange` for external control.

props.name: defaultIsCollapsed
props.description: Initial collapsed state for uncontrolled usage.

props.name: onCollapsedChange
props.description: Callback fired when the user toggles the drawer.

bestPractices.text: Give label a concrete plural noun such as "Attachments" so the expand and collapse actions have a useful accessible name.
Use controlled isCollapsed with onCollapsedChange when another part of the page owns drawer state; otherwise use defaultIsCollapsed.
Put primary composer actions in the drawer; use ChatComposer footer or send-action slots so those controls remain available when the drawer is collapsed.

anatomy.name: Root surface
anatomy.description: The drawer surface that composes above the ChatComposer body.

anatomy.name: Disclosure toggle
anatomy.description: The keyboard- and pointer-operable collapse control rendered when count is provided.

anatomy.name: Collapsed summary
anatomy.description: The default count Badge and label, or caller-provided visual content, presented while the drawer is collapsed.

anatomy.name: Content area
anatomy.description: The caller-provided supplementary content; collapsed descendants are unavailable to keyboard and assistive technology.

components.name: ChatComposerInput
components.description: Pass ChatComposerInput to ChatComposer's input slot when the draft needs trigger menus, inline tokens, history recall, dictation insertion, or file intake.

props.name: handleRef
props.description: Imperative handle for programmatic control: insertToken, expandToken, insertText, focus, and getValue.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled input value. Pair with onChange for two-way binding.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when the input value changes. The serialized string includes token placeholders.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when the input is empty.

props.name: maxRows
props.description: Maximum visible rows before the input scrolls. Use a lower value in compact layouts.

props.name: triggers
props.description: Trigger definitions for typeahead menus. Each trigger specifies a character (@ or /), a search source, and an onSelect handler that returns the token to insert. Set hasMultiWordQuery: true when suggestions contain spaces (people, topics): the query then runs to a line break or about 64 characters instead of ending at the first space. Per-trigger emptySearchText (ReactNode) is the message when the query matched nothing.

props.name: debounceMs
props.description: Debounce delay for async search sources to avoid excessive network requests.

props.name: hasHistory
props.description: Enable ArrowUp/Down to recall previously submitted messages.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label announced by screen readers.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the input. Use during streaming or when a prerequisite is unmet.

props.name: onPaste
props.description: Called when plain text is pasted. Return true after handling the text yourself; otherwise ChatComposerInput inserts it or applies paste-as-token behavior.

props.name: pasteAsToken
props.description: Paste-as-token behavior. By default, plain-text pastes over 200 characters become expandable tokens. Pass false to keep every text paste inline, or provide useChatPasteAsToken() to customize the conversion.

props.name: onFiles
props.description: Called when files are pasted or dropped onto the input. Use to handle attachments.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Called when the user presses Enter without Shift. The serialized value includes token placeholders.

props.name: onKeyDown
props.description: Key-down handler invoked before the built-in Enter/history behavior (after any open trigger menu). The seam for platform-specific keys: call event.preventDefault() to suppress the default submit (e.g. newline on a touch keyboard), or act on the event yourself to add behavior (e.g. submit on Cmd/Ctrl+Enter). IME composition is always respected; Enter never submits mid-composition.

props.name: enterKeyHint
props.description: What the Return key of a touch keyboard says (the native enterkeyhint). Enter sends the message, so it defaults to send and iOS shows its Send key. When onKeyDown makes Enter insert a line break on touch keyboards, pass enter so the key shows Return again.

bestPractices.text: Use handleRef for programmatic text or token insertion; inserted text follows the same onChange pipeline as typing.
Use onFiles for files pasted or dropped onto the editor, and keep file validation and upload progress in the product layer.
Use custom token rendering for ordinary mentions or commands; prefer the structured badge form so tokens remain predictable and themeable.

anatomy.name: Input root
anatomy.description: The themed container that forwards the root ref and BaseProps styling seams.

anatomy.name: Editable surface
anatomy.description: The labeled contenteditable textbox or combobox that owns text, selection, keyboard, paste, and drop behavior.

anatomy.name: Placeholder
anatomy.description: Visual guidance shown only while the serialized draft is empty.

anatomy.name: Trigger menu
anatomy.description: The suggestion popup rendered while a configured trigger is active.

anatomy.name: Inline token
anatomy.description: A non-editable badge or custom rendering with a stable serialized value.

components.name: ChatComposerTokenElement
components.description: Renders a single token chip outside the contentEditable input. Wraps a badge config or custom render function in the correct data-astryx-token span so the token serializes properly and stays visually consistent with tokens inside the composer.

props.name: token
props.description: The token to render. Pass a badge config ({ value, label, variant?, icon? }) for the common case, or a custom render ({ value, render }) for full control.

components.name: ChatDictationButton
components.description: ChatDictationButton is a toggle button that starts and stops voice dictation inside a chat composer. It pairs with useChatDictation to show a microphone icon when idle and animated frequency bars when listening. Place it in the sendActions slot of ChatComposer.

props.name: dictation
props.description: The return value from useChatDictation or useSpeechRecognition. Controls all button state: listening, volume, bands, and toggle.

props.name: size
props.description: Button size. Matches ChatComposer density.

props.name: isHiddenWhenUnsupported
props.description: When true, renders nothing if the browser does not support SpeechRecognition. When false, keeps the button visible but disabled.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label override. Defaults to "Start dictation" or "Stop dictation" based on state.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

bestPractices.text: Place the dictation button in the sendActions slot of ChatComposer so it sits next to the send button where users expect voice input controls.
Pass an inputRef to useChatDictation so interim transcripts appear as ghost text in the composer input while the user speaks.
Enable hasSounds on useChatDictation to give users audio feedback when dictation starts and stops. This is especially helpful when the button's visual change is subtle.
Don't use the dictation button outside a chat composer context. It's designed for the composer's send-action layout, not as a standalone recording control.
Don't forget to handle the unsupported case. The button hides itself by default when the browser lacks SpeechRecognition, but you should still design the composer to work without it.

anatomy.name: Microphone icon
anatomy.description: Shown in the idle state. Indicates that tapping will start voice input.

anatomy.name: Frequency bars
anatomy.description: Animated equalizer bars that replace the icon during listening. React to real microphone volume.

anatomy.name: Ghost button
anatomy.description: The underlying Button with ghost variant and isIconOnly, providing the hit target and focus ring.

components.name: ChatLayout
components.description: ChatLayout is the layout shell for full-page chat interfaces. It renders messages in normal page flow and docks the composer to the bottom with a frosted glass blur layer. Set the density prop to control spacing; it defaults to balanced. Use it to wrap ChatMessageList and ChatComposer for a complete chat experience with built-in auto-scroll and a scroll-to-bottom button.

props.name: children
props.description: Message content: typically ChatMessageList. Flows naturally in the page and scrolls with the container.

props.name: composer
props.description: Composer element: typically ChatComposer. Fixed to the bottom with a frosted glass dock.

props.name: emptyState
props.description: Content shown when children is empty. Centered vertically in the message area.

props.name: scrollButton
props.description: Scroll-to-bottom button rendered above the composer. Defaults to ChatLayoutScrollButton with auto-scroll integration. Pass null to hide.

props.name: scrollRef
props.description: External scroll container ref. When provided, auto-scroll and scroll-to-bottom target this element instead of the layout root. Use when the chat is embedded in a page where a parent element or the document body scrolls.

props.name: density
props.description: Visual density: controls dock padding, message-area max-width and inline padding, and the height of the frosted glass blur layer.

bestPractices.text: Pass ChatMessageList as children and ChatComposer as the composer prop for a complete chat interface.
Provide an emptyState so new conversations show a prompt instead of a blank screen.
Use scrollRef when the chat is embedded in a page where a parent element handles scrolling.

Give a full-page ChatLayout a container 100dvh tall, not 100vh: where a phone browser's toolbar collapses, 100vh is the viewport with the toolbar hidden, so the composer would start below the screen's edge.
Markdown prose keeps its 680px measure, while code blocks and tables span the message column. To give a reply one right edge, pass contentWidth="100%" to its Markdown.
Don't apply a fixed height on the layout; let it fill its container with flex: 1.
Don't render multiple ChatLayout instances in the same scroll container; each expects to own its scroll context.

anatomy.name: Message area
anatomy.description: Scrollable region for messages. Renders children (typically ChatMessageList) in a flex column that pushes content to the bottom when the list is short.

anatomy.name: Frosted glass dock
anatomy.description: Sticky or fixed container at the bottom with a backdrop-blur layer. Houses the scroll button and composer. While a software keyboard is up it sits on top of the keyboard, and the message area gets room to scroll above it.

anatomy.name: Scroll-to-bottom button
anatomy.description: Appears when the user scrolls up or new messages arrive. Defaults to ChatLayoutScrollButton; pass null to hide or a custom element to override.

anatomy.name: Composer
anatomy.description: The input area for sending messages, typically ChatComposer. Docked at the bottom inside the frosted glass layer. In a top-level page on a touch screen, its wrapper (without the scroll button) is a group with no name. When the keyboard’s Done ends typing, focus rests on that group (it is no tab stop), so the next tap or Tab starts from the composer. It shows the focus ring after keyboard input only. Under a mouse or inside an iframe, the wrapper is a plain container.

anatomy.name: Empty state
anatomy.description: Centered placeholder shown when no messages exist. Use EmptyState for a consistent look.

components.name: ChatLayoutScrollButton
components.description: Floating scroll-to-bottom button that appears when the user scrolls away from the latest messages. It fades in as a compact icon button and expands to show a label when new messages arrive. ChatLayout renders this by default: pass a custom element to the scrollButton prop to override, or null to hide it entirely.

props.name: isVisible
props.description: Whether the button is visible. Bind to a scroll-position check so the button only appears when the user has scrolled up.

props.name: label
props.description: Optional label that expands the button (e.g. "New messages"). Use to signal unread content below the fold.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler: typically scrolls to bottom and dismisses the new message indicator.

components.name: ChatMessage
components.description: Sender context wrapper: handles avatar, name, metadata, and alignment based on sender role.

props.name: sender
props.description: Who sent this message: controls alignment and layout.

props.name: children
props.description: Free-form content: bubbles, asset lists, tool calls, images. Custom (non-bubble) children render flush with the message edge; wrap them in a ghost ChatMessageBubble to align them with the bubble text column.

props.name: avatar
props.description: Avatar element rendered beside the message. Typically Avatar. `null`, booleans, and empty strings create no slot; any other content that renders nothing collapses its slot.

props.name: name
props.description: Sender name rendered above the message body; it labels the message. `null`, booleans, and empty strings create no slot, and any other content that renders nothing collapses its slot; either way the message is labelled by the translated sender fallback. Use when the first child is raw content (not a bubble). If the first child is a bubble, put the name on the bubble's `name` prop instead.

props.name: metadata
props.description: Metadata rendered below the message body. `null`, booleans, and empty strings create no slot; any other content that renders nothing collapses its slot. Use when the last child is raw content (not a bubble). If the last child is a bubble, put metadata on the bubble's `metadata` prop instead.

props.name: density
props.description: Visual density. Inherited from list context if not set.

components.name: ChatMessageBubble
components.description: Styled content container for the chat "bubble." Reads sender from parent ChatMessage context to auto-style the background. Use filled for standard messages and ghost when content needs alignment without a visible boundary. Supports name/metadata slots aligned with bubble padding, and multi-bubble grouping via the group prop for consecutive messages from the same sender.

props.name: children
props.description: Bubble content: text, Markdown, or any ReactNode.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual variant. 'filled' renders sender-colored background (default). 'ghost' renders transparent background but keeps padding for alignment.

props.name: name
props.description: Sender name rendered above the bubble, aligned with bubble text padding. Use on the first bubble in a message. Non-rendering scalar values (null, undefined, booleans, and the empty string) omit the aligned wrapper; numeric 0 remains aligned. If the first content is raw (no bubble), use ChatMessage's `name` prop instead.

props.name: metadata
props.description: Metadata content rendered below the bubble, aligned with bubble text padding. Use on the last bubble in a message. Non-rendering scalar values (null, undefined, booleans, and the empty string) omit the aligned wrapper; numeric 0 remains aligned. If the last content is raw (no bubble), use ChatMessage's `metadata` prop instead.

props.name: group
props.description: Position within a multi-bubble group. Controls corner radius reduction on the sender side. Leave unset for standalone bubbles (full radius).

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the bubble (number = pixels, string = used as-is). When set, replaces the default max(80%, 280px) width cap. Combine with variant="ghost" to let custom content (an artifact card, attachments) span the full message column.

components.name: ChatMessageList
components.description: Presentational message container with density context and infinite scroll support. Provides role="log" with aria-live="polite" for accessibility. A flex spacer pushes messages to the bottom when the list isn't full; set align="top" to start messages at the top instead.

props.name: children
props.description: Message elements: typically ChatMessage or ChatSystemMessage.

props.name: emptyState
props.description: Content shown when the list has no messages.

props.name: scrollToTopAction
props.description: Async action fired when user scrolls to top. Use for loading older messages. Wrapped in useTransition: shows a spinner at the top while pending.

props.name: density
props.description: Visual density: flows to child messages via context.

props.name: gap
props.description: Gap between top-level message rows. Defaults to the selected density; override for LLM event streams or independent rows that need different spacing from density.

props.name: align
props.description: Vertical alignment when the list is shorter than its container. 'bottom' fills free space with a spacer so short conversations sit above the composer; 'top' omits the spacer so messages start at the top. Only affects a non-full list; overflowing lists scroll identically, preserving auto-scroll-to-bottom.

props.name: isStreaming
props.description: Whether an assistant message is actively streaming. Marks the log aria-busy so screen readers wait and announce the completed message once instead of re-announcing partial text on every token.

components.name: ChatMessageMetadata
components.description: Place ChatMessageMetadata below a message or in the last ChatMessageBubble metadata slot to show a timestamp, footer content, and optional delivery status. Non-rendering scalar slots (booleans and empty strings) create no separator; numeric zero remains visible. Composite React content remains caller-owned.

props.name: timestamp
props.description: Timestamp content: a string or Timestamp component.

props.name: footer
props.description: Footer content: model info, reaction buttons, copy button.

props.name: status
props.description: Message delivery status. Shows icon + label.

bestPractices.text: Put metadata in the last bubble metadata slot when the message uses bubbles, so it follows the bubble content.
Pass timestamp and footer content independently; separators are omitted for non-rendering scalar slots. Composite React nodes are used as supplied.
Do not supply footer actions without their own accessible names and interaction behavior; the metadata row does not own those controls.
Do not put the same metadata on both a bubble and its enclosing message.

anatomy.name: Metadata row
anatomy.description: Sender-aware line containing the visible metadata items.

anatomy.name: Timestamp
anatomy.description: Caller-supplied time content at the start of the logical sequence.

anatomy.name: Footer
anatomy.description: Caller-supplied information or actions between time and status.

anatomy.name: Status
anatomy.description: Localized delivery icon and text when a status is supplied.

components.name: ChatSendButton
components.description: Use ChatSendButton as ChatComposer’s send control when the action should switch between sending and stopping. Inside ChatComposer it reads readiness, streaming state, and action callbacks from context; standalone usage supplies those values explicitly.

props.name: isStopShown
props.description: Whether the stop button is shown. Defaults to context value.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the send button is disabled. Defaults to !canSend from context.

props.name: onSend
props.description: Called when the user clicks send. Defaults to context onSubmit.

props.name: onStop
props.description: Called when the user clicks stop during streaming. Defaults to context onStop.

props.name: sendIcon
props.description: Custom icon for the send state. Defaults to the arrowUp icon (theme icons, else a registered or built-in drawing).

props.name: stopIcon
props.description: Custom icon for the stop state. Defaults to the stop icon (theme icons, else a registered or built-in drawing).

props.name: size
props.description: Button size.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

bestPractices.text: Place ChatSendButton inside ChatComposer when its readiness and send or stop lifecycle should follow composer context.
For standalone use, provide the state and matching onSend or onStop callback explicitly.
Keep the translated Send or Stop accessible name intact when supplying custom icon artwork; the icon is decorative and must not be the only name source.
Do not render the stop state without a working onStop callback from props or ChatComposer context.
Do not expect isDisabled to disable the stop action; it applies only to the send state.

anatomy.name: Action button
anatomy.description: Circular icon-only Button that exposes the translated Send or Stop name and carries the chat-send-button theme target.

components.name: ChatSystemMessage
components.description: Use ChatSystemMessage for concise, non-sender content inside a chat transcript. Choose the default variant for factual status notices and the divider variant for date or section breaks. Long default content wraps within the available width. It carries no live role: inside a ChatMessageList, the log announces new notices. The divider branch includes a labelled separator.

props.name: children
props.description: System message content: factual text or React content such as a date, join/leave notice, or status change. Long default content wraps within the available width.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual variant. 'default' renders centered text. 'divider' adds horizontal lines on each side via Divider: use for date separators and section breaks.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional caller-provided icon content. Rendered before the message in the default variant; the divider variant currently does not render it. Wrap in Icon for consistent sizing.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

bestPractices.text: Keep the visible message concise and self-contained so it remains understandable without an icon.
Use the divider variant for temporal or section boundaries and the default variant for factual status notices.
Use ChatSystemMessage for sender-authored content; use ChatMessage and ChatMessageBubble instead.
Use caller-provided icon artwork as the only source of meaning; the visible message must carry the same information.

anatomy.name: System message
anatomy.description: The noninteractive status row that carries the chat-system-message theme target.

anatomy.name: Content
anatomy.description: The concise caller-provided message or divider label.

anatomy.name: Icon content
anatomy.description: Rendered before the message in the default variant; the divider variant currently does not render it.

anatomy.name: Divider
anatomy.description: A labelled horizontal Divider rendered by the divider variant.

components.name: ChatTokenizedText
components.description: Use ChatTokenizedText inside a chat message when stored plain text contains serialized token values that should be projected as inline badges or caller-rendered token content. Unmatched text is preserved exactly and empty token values are ignored so rendering always finishes.

props.name: children
props.description: The plain text message containing serialized token values. Patterns matching a token's value are replaced with inline token content.

props.name: tokens
props.description: Token definitions using the same type as composer input. Each non-empty value is matched literally. Empty values are ignored. Structured tokens render a Badge, while custom tokens render caller content.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the root text wrapper. Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

bestPractices.text: Reuse the same token definitions for composer insertion and message rendering so serialized values and visible labels stay aligned.
Use non-empty, stable serialized values so every definition identifies real message text.
Use token labels as a substitute for the surrounding message text; the complete message must remain understandable in reading order.
Put component-owned interaction or accessibility behavior inside a custom token renderer; custom token content remains caller owned.

anatomy.name: Tokenized text
anatomy.description: The inline root that preserves unmatched text and carries the chat-tokenized-text theme target.

anatomy.name: Rendered token
anatomy.description: Inline token content rendered by Badge for structured tokens or by the caller for custom tokens.

components.name: ChatToolCalls
components.description: ChatToolCalls displays tool or function call invocations from an LLM response. Pass an array of calls and the component handles the rest: a single call renders inline, while multiple calls collapse into a summary with the latest call visible at the surface. Use it anywhere an AI agent shows what actions it took.

props.name: calls
props.description: Array of tool call data. Each item has name, status, target, duration, node, additions, deletions, stats, errorMessage, resultDetail, key, and data. status is one of 'pending', 'running', 'complete', or 'error' (defaults to 'complete').

props.name: label
props.description: Custom summary label shown for an expanded group. The translated call count is used when omitted.

props.name: isExpanded
props.description: Controlled expanded state for the group.

props.name: defaultIsExpanded
props.description: Default expanded state when uncontrolled.

props.name: onExpandedChange
props.description: Callback fired when the expanded state changes.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

bestPractices.text: Include a target string on every call so the user can see what the tool acted on: a file path, a shell command, or a search query.
Show a duration on completed calls so users can judge which tools are slow and understand why a response took time.
Provide a group label when the automatic count does not explain what the calls represent.
Provide resultDetail with a code block for calls that produce output (diffs for edits, terminal output for shell commands) so users can inspect results inline.
Set a unique key on each call item when streaming so React can animate additions without re-mounting completed rows.
Don't omit the status field. Without it the call defaults to complete, which is misleading for calls that are still running or have failed.
Don't display tool calls outside a chat message context; they are designed to sit inside an assistant message, not as standalone UI.
Don't use custom wrappers around individual calls; the component handles single vs. grouped layout automatically based on the array length.

anatomy.name: Status icon
anatomy.description: The success or error icon (theme icons, else a registered or built-in drawing), or a spinner while the call is pending or running.

anatomy.name: Tool name
anatomy.description: The function or tool name displayed in monospace: bash, edit, read, web_search, etc.

anatomy.name: Node badge
anatomy.description: A neutral pill badge showing which sandbox or environment ran the tool, like cli:remote-server or workspace.

anatomy.name: Target label
anatomy.description: The target of the action (a file path, command, or search query) shown after the tool name.

anatomy.name: Diff stats
anatomy.description: Green additions and red deletions counts for edit operations, displayed inline after the target.

anatomy.name: Duration
anatomy.description: Execution time shown on the trailing edge for completed calls.

anatomy.name: Group header
anatomy.description: A wrench icon with a call count, shown when multiple calls are present. Clicking toggles between the summary and the full list.

components.name: CheckboxInput
components.description: CheckboxInput toggles a single on/off value. Use it for settings like "Enable notifications", terms acceptance, or opt-in choices. For multiple checkboxes in a group, use CheckboxList instead.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the underlying <input> element.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the checkbox (always rendered for accessibility).

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Whether to visually hide the label (still accessible to screen readers).

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed below the label.

props.name: value
props.description: Whether the checkbox is checked, unchecked, or indeterminate.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the checkbox state changes.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action on change. Fires after onChange if not prevented. Shows loading spinner while pending.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Whether the checkbox is in a loading state. Shows spinner and prevents interaction.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the checkbox is disabled.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: The HTML name attribute for the underlying checkbox input, useful for form submissions (submits "on" when checked).

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the checkbox is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the checkbox focusable via aria-disabled (toggling stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled CheckboxInput in Tooltip. Disabled controls swallow the hover events an external Tooltip needs.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: Whether the checkbox is read-only. Displays the current state at full opacity but prevents interaction. Unlike `isDisabled`, read-only checkboxes are not visually dimmed.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Whether the field is optional. Mutually exclusive with isRequired.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Whether the checkbox is required. Mutually exclusive with isOptional.

props.name: size
props.description: The size of the checkbox. sm for compact layouts, md for default. Under a coarse pointer a labelled checkbox’s target grows toward 44 px through an invisible hit area. It never shrinks below the row and stops at half the gap to a closer neighbour; nothing changes size.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Callback fired when the checkbox receives focus.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Callback fired when the checkbox loses focus.

props.name: labelIcon
props.description: Built-in meaning or custom content displayed before the label text. See `astryx docs icons` for the built-in meanings.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator. Displays a colored message box below the checkbox and sets aria-invalid for errors.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

bestPractices.text: Always provide a visible label so the user knows what they are toggling. Use isLabelHidden only when surrounding context makes it obvious.
Add a description for choices that need extra context, like explaining what "Share usage data" actually shares.
Use the indeterminate state for "select all" checkboxes when only some items in a group are selected.
Use a checkbox for mutually exclusive choices; use RadioList when only one option can be selected.
Use a checkbox for actions that take effect immediately; use a toggle switch or button instead.
Wrap a disabled checkbox in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

accessibility.name: Checkbox box
accessibility.description: The box edge (unchecked) and fill (checked) must have at least 3:1 contrast with the surface behind them. For Hover and Pointer down, measure the final colors after the tint and the pressed overlay are applied.

anatomy.name: Checkbox
anatomy.description: The check box itself: unchecked, checked, or indeterminate.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Text describing what the checkbox controls. Always present for accessibility.

anatomy.name: Description
anatomy.description: Helper text below the label with additional context.

anatomy.name: Status message
anatomy.description: An error, warning, or success message below the checkbox.

components.name: CheckboxList
components.description: CheckboxList shows a small group of checkboxes so users can turn several options on or off at once. Place it in settings pages, filter panels, or forms where every choice should be visible without scrolling. For a single standalone checkbox (like "I agree to the terms"), use CheckboxInput instead. If only one option can be picked, use RadioList. If the list is long enough to need searching or scrolling, use MultiSelector instead.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the checkbox group (always rendered for accessibility).

props.name: children
props.description: CheckboxListItem elements.

props.name: value
props.description: The currently selected values (collection mode).

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the selected values change.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action on change with optimistic updates. While the promise is pending, the toggled item shows a spinner inside its checkbox and is marked aria-busy.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Whether to visually hide the label.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed below the label.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Whether the group is optional. Shows the optional indicator after the group label, unless a surrounding FormLayout already makes fields optional by default.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Whether the group needs at least one checked box. Shows the required indicator after the group label by the same rules as every input field. While no box is checked, the browser blocks submit and moves focus to the first box that is neither disabled nor read-only, with its own message. A disabled or read-only group requires nothing. Show your own error text through status. Mutually exclusive with isOptional.

props.name: density
props.description: Spacing density for list items.

props.name: hasDividers
props.description: Whether to show dividers between items.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether all checkbox items are disabled.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the group is disabled. Applies to the whole-group disabled state (isDisabled), not per item. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the checkboxes focusable via aria-disabled (toggling stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled CheckboxList in Tooltip. Disabled controls swallow the hover events an external Tooltip needs.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: Whether all checkbox items are read-only. Displays the current state at full opacity but prevents interaction. Unlike isDisabled, read-only checkboxes are not visually dimmed.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator ({ type, message }).

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the element that paints the border and background and holds icons and end controls. Never the native input.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Class name for the visual control box.

props.name: controlStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the visual control box.

bestPractices.text: Keep the list short: three to seven options is the sweet spot. Beyond that, switch to MultiSelector which adds search and scrolling.
Turn on dividers (hasDividers) when items have helper text underneath; without them the labels and descriptions blur together.

Pass an option description that is longer than one line as a node: description={<Text type="supporting">…</Text>}. A string description shows on one line, and the row cuts the remaining text with an ellipsis.
Write a group label that says what the choices represent: "Export formats" tells users more than "Options".
Show a CheckboxList when the user can only pick one thing; that is what RadioList is for.
Put buttons or links inside the trailing slot (endContent); the whole row is already tappable, so a nested button creates two competing click targets.
Wrap a disabled CheckboxList in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

anatomy.name: Group
anatomy.description: Container for the labeled checkbox group.

anatomy.name: Group label
anatomy.description: Text identifying what the checkbox options represent.

anatomy.name: Description
anatomy.description: Helper text below the group label.

anatomy.name: Options list
anatomy.description: List containing the available checkbox options.

anatomy.name: Option row
anatomy.description: Selectable row containing one option.

anatomy.name: Checkbox
anatomy.description: Selection indicator for an option.

anatomy.name: Option label
anatomy.description: Primary content identifying an option.

anatomy.name: Option description
anatomy.description: Secondary text below an option label.

anatomy.name: End content
anatomy.description: Caller-provided content at the end of an option row.

anatomy.name: Spinner
anatomy.description: Loading indicator shown inside the pending checkbox.

components.name: CheckboxListItem
components.description: Individual checkbox item with label, description, and end content slot. Works in collection mode (inside a CheckboxList with a value array) or standalone mode (inside List, or inside a CheckboxList without value, such as a select-all item). On a touch screen (a coarse primary pointer), a toggleable row is one press target: a touch on the label, the description or the box itself shows the pressed state on the row and its checkbox together. Where the primary pointer is fine, the box keeps its own press.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary text label for the item. Rich labels may contain links or buttons, which keep their own behavior without toggling the item. A ReactNode label names the checkbox from its visible text; pass aria-label only when that text is absent, or include all visible label words in the override.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Plain-text accessible name for the checkbox, replacing the one derived from label. Applied to the checkbox control. Use it when a rich label has no visible text; otherwise the value must retain every visible label word.

props.name: value
props.description: Identity key. Required when the parent CheckboxList has a value array; the item throws without it there.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary content below the label: a string shows on one line and the row cuts long text with an ellipsis, so for full text pass a node, for example description={<Text type="supporting">…</Text>}. String or ReactNode. The description is the checkbox's accessible description through aria-describedby, so assistive technology can tell it is the explanation for that choice.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content rendered after the label area.

props.name: align
props.description: Vertical alignment of the start and end content against the label, passed through to Item unchanged. `first-line` keeps a small mark (a checkbox) level with the first line of a wrapped label. See Item.align.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether this individual item is disabled.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Whether this item is loading. Shows a spinner inside the checkbox and blocks interaction on this item. In collection mode, the toggled item also shows this automatically while the parent changeAction is pending.

props.name: isChecked
props.description: Direct checked state in standalone mode: inside List, or inside a CheckboxList without value (for example, a select-all item). Ignored when the parent CheckboxList has a value array.

props.name: onCheck
props.description: Direct check handler in standalone mode: inside List, or inside a CheckboxList without value. Ignored when the parent CheckboxList has a value array; that list's onChange receives the change.

components.name: Citation
components.description: Citations display inline references to external sources. Use them to attribute information within AI-generated responses, articles, or anywhere provenance and source links are needed.

props.name: source
props.description: The citation source object containing title, url, an optional image src, and an optional icon node. The url follows the shared navigation rule described on the Link `href` prop; rejected destinations leave the citation visible without navigation. Image src uses separate resource handling.

props.name: number
props.description: The display index for this citation.

props.name: variant
props.description: Display style: a label chip showing the source title or a compact numbered badge.

bestPractices.text: Use the label variant when the source title adds meaningful context for the reader.
Use the number variant for compact inline references within body text, like footnotes.
Mix label and number variants in the same paragraph. Pick one style per context for visual consistency.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: The root wrapper. Accepted source URLs render an anchor; missing or rejected URLs render an inert span.

anatomy.name: Icon
anatomy.description: An optional source icon shown before the label text. Accepts a favicon/logo image URL (via source.src) or a React node such as an Astryx <Icon>. Only available in the label variant.

anatomy.name: Label text
anatomy.description: The source title, truncated with ellipsis when it exceeds the max width. Shown in the label variant.

anatomy.name: Number
anatomy.description: The citation index displayed as a superscript badge. Shown in the number variant.

components.name: ClickableCard
components.description: An interactive card for navigation or action targets. Nested interactive elements work independently.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessibility label.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler: fires on card surface only.

props.name: href
props.description: Navigation URL. Plain, new-tab, Cmd/Ctrl-click, and middle-click activation all follow the shared navigation rule described on the Link `href` prop.

props.name: target
props.description: Link target.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the card and removes a link destination; the card keeps its tab stop and is announced as disabled.

props.name: children
props.description: Card content.

props.name: padding
props.description: Inner padding.

props.name: variant
props.description: Background color variant.

props.name: elevation
props.description: Resting shadow depth. Often raised to signal the whole card is clickable.

props.name: width
props.description: Card width.

props.name: height
props.description: Card height.

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: Maximum card width.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

bestPractices.text: Use for cards that navigate to a detail page or trigger a single action.
Nest buttons or links freely inside; they handle their own events.
Use for toggling selection; use SelectableCard for that.

Use with a transparent variant and no padding only to borrow the press model for a surface that owns its own box. Compose the chrome-free recipe in the useClickableContainer docs instead: it adds no Card styles to the page.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: Interactive div with hover/focus/active states.

anatomy.name: Content
anatomy.description: Children, which may include nested interactive elements.

components.name: Code
components.description: Code marks short inline references such as function names, variables, file paths, and command-line flags. Use CodeBlock for standalone or multi-line snippets.

props.name: children
props.description: The inline code content.

props.name: color
props.description: Text color. Use 'inherit' to take the surrounding text color.

props.name: size
props.description: Set to 'inherit' to take the surrounding font size and line height. Omit it to use the code type-scale size.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the semantic code element.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the root element. Prefer xstyle for StyleX-optimized styling.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

bestPractices.text: Use Code for short technical terms inside prose, such as a function name, prop, file path, or command-line flag.
Set size to 'inherit' when inline code should match the surrounding text size and line height.
Use Code for multi-line or standalone snippets. Use CodeBlock instead so readers get appropriate block formatting and syntax support.
Use Code as an interactive copy or navigation control. Pair it with the appropriate Button or Link when an action is required.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: The semantic code element that contains the inline code content and paints the background, typography, padding, and radius.

components.name: CodeBlock
components.description: CodeBlock renders syntax-highlighted code with line numbers, a copy button, and optional collapsible sections. Use CodeBlock for multi-line snippets like source files, terminal commands, and configuration examples. Use Code for inline references to function names, variables, or CLI flags within body text.

props.name: code
props.description: The code string to display.

props.name: language
props.description: Language for syntax highlighting. A string selects a built-in: ts, js, tsx, jsx, json, html, xml, svg, css, scss, less, python, bash/sh/zsh/shell, php, hack, yaml, markdown, c, cpp (c++, cc, cxx, hpp, hh), sql, rust, kotlin, swift, go. Any other language is a value you import on its own and pass here: graphql, java, thrift, objectiveC, toml, powershell, ruby, lua, dockerfile from @astryxdesign/core/CodeBlock/languages/<path> (e.g. languages/graphql, languages/objective-c), or your own made with createCodeLanguage({name, identifiers, tokenize}). A value labels with its name and reflects its first identifier as data-language. Use "plaintext" to disable.

props.name: title
props.description: Filename or label shown in the header bar.

props.name: hasLanguageLabel
props.description: Show the language name in the header bar. Hidden when language is "plaintext".

props.name: hasLineNumbers
props.description: Show a line number gutter.

props.name: startLineNumber
props.description: First line number shown in the gutter. The gutter shows file coordinates (startLineNumber + index) so a code excerpt reads with its real line numbers. highlightLines uses the same file coordinates. Values below 1 clamp to 1.

props.name: highlightLines
props.description: 1-indexed line numbers to highlight, in the same file coordinates as the gutter (see startLineNumber). Out-of-range entries render no highlight.

props.name: isDiff
props.description: Render the code as a unified diff over `language`: lines starting with + are added, - removed, @@ is a hunk header (a `--- `/`+++ ` file-header pair directly before one is a header too), anything else is context. The language label reads `diff` or `<language> diff`. The glyph sits in its own column and the rest of each line keeps syntax highlighting; copy returns the exact source. Markdown ```diff and ```diff-<lang> fences set this.

props.name: hasCopyButton
props.description: Show a copy-to-clipboard button.

props.name: onCopy
props.description: Callback after the code is copied.

props.name: onCopyError
props.description: Called once with the rejection when the clipboard write fails. The copy button shows a cross and is named and announced as "Failed to copy value to clipboard."; the error is not shown.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Your own controls, shown just before Copy: in the header when the block has one, otherwise beside the code in the top inline-end corner, never over it. It never creates a header and never collapses the block. Ghost sm IconButtons match Copy’s size and variant.

props.name: isWrapped
props.description: Wrap long lines instead of enabling horizontal scroll.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Max height before the block scrolls vertically.

props.name: size
props.description: Text size variant.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the code block. Any CSS width value. 'fit-content' (default) shrinks to longest line. '100%' fills parent width.

props.name: container
props.description: Container presentation style. 'card' (default): border and radius with the muted syntax background for a standalone card look. 'section': no border or radius and a transparent background so the block blends into the card or panel it's embedded in.

props.name: tokenizer
props.type: (code: string, language: string) => Array<{type: string; start: number; end: number}>
props.description: Deprecated: pass language={createCodeLanguage({name, identifiers, tokenize})} with this same function instead. Still works exactly as released and wins over the language; astryx upgrade rewrites static uses.

props.name: syntaxTheme
props.description: Per-instance syntax theme override. Shorthand for wrapping the block in <SyntaxTheme theme={...}>. Accepts a preset from @astryxdesign/core/theme/syntax or a theme created with defineSyntaxTheme(). Defaults to the nearest SyntaxTheme ancestor or the theme-level syntax colors.

props.name: highlightMode
props.description: Syntax highlighting rendering mode.

props.name: isCollapsible
props.description: Allow collapsing the code body into just the header bar. Starts expanded; a visible header becomes clickable when the code exceeds collapsibleThreshold lines. Headerless blocks never collapse, and removing the header expands a previously collapsed block.

props.name: collapsibleThreshold
props.description: Minimum number of lines before the collapse toggle appears. Below this threshold the code block renders normally even when isCollapsible is true.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the root code-block element.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles. Prefer xstyle for StyleX-optimized styling.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

bestPractices.text: Set the language prop to match the code content so syntax highlighting is accurate. Use "plaintext" when the language is unknown.
Add a title when the code represents a file. It gives readers context and appears in the header bar alongside the copy button.
Use Code for short inline references like function names or CLI flags, and CodeBlock for standalone multi-line snippets.
Enable line numbers on short snippets (under 5 lines) where they add clutter without helping navigation.
Nest a code block inside a scrollable container. Use the maxHeight prop instead, which handles overflow natively.

anatomy.name: Header Bar
anatomy.description: Shows the title, visible language label, endContent, and copy button when a header is present. A title or visible language label creates the header at every line count. With no title and hasLanguageLabel={false}, endContent and the copy button sit in their own column beside the code, centred on the first line, and never cover it; a one-line block then reads as a single row.

anatomy.name: Header Title
anatomy.description: Groups the optional title, visible language label, and collapsible chevron inside the header bar.

anatomy.name: Line Numbers
anatomy.description: Numbered gutter along the left edge. Enable with hasLineNumbers.

anatomy.name: Code Body
anatomy.description: The syntax-highlighted code content.

anatomy.name: Highlighted Lines
anatomy.description: Background accent on specific lines to draw attention.

anatomy.name: Copy Button
anatomy.description: Copies the code string to the clipboard. Shown by default.

components.name: Collapsible
components.description: Collapsible hides and reveals content behind a trigger button. Use it in settings panels, FAQ pages, or detail views to keep the page scannable while letting users drill into sections they care about. Wrap multiple collapsibles in CollapsibleGroup for accordion behavior. For custom collapsible components, use the `useCollapsible` hook directly (`astryx hook useCollapsible`).

props.name: trigger
props.description: Content shown in the trigger area (always visible).

props.name: children
props.description: Content that collapses and expands.

props.name: defaultIsOpen
props.description: Default open state for standalone uncontrolled usage. Ignored when value binds the item to a surrounding CollapsibleGroup.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Controlled open state for standalone usage. Ignored when value binds the item to a surrounding CollapsibleGroup.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disable the item so its trigger can't be toggled (dimmed, aria-disabled, and out of the tab order). Doesn't collapse an already-open item.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback invoked when standalone open state changes. A surrounding CollapsibleGroup owns grouped state and calls its onChange instead.

props.name: chevronPosition
props.description: Logical position of Collapsible's disclosure chevron. `end` (default) follows the label, pointing down when collapsed and up when expanded. `start` precedes the label, pointing inward toward content when collapsed (mirrored under RTL) and down when expanded. Inside a CollapsibleGroup this defaults to the group's chevronPosition.

props.name: value
props.description: Identifier used for group coordination. When set inside a CollapsibleGroup, the group owns open state and its onChange is the notification callback.

props.name: animatedLayout
props.description: The handle from useAnimatedLayout({containerRef}). With it, opening and closing glides the content after this Collapsible, up to that container, on one shared motion role instead of jumping, and the revealed content and the chevron move on the same motion. Without it, the content after it takes its place at once.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the root collapsible element.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles. Prefer xstyle for StyleX-optimized styling.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

bestPractices.text: Give every trigger a meaningful accessible name. Visible text usually supplies it; custom trigger content should include VisuallyHidden text when its visuals do not.
Use hasDividers on CollapsibleGroup for FAQ-style lists: built-in row hairlines with themed border tokens, no hand-rolled borders.
Wrap each Collapsible in an Card for visual separation in accordion layouts, or use CollapsibleGroup's hasDividers for flat lists; don't combine both.
Use CollapsibleGroup with type="single" for settings or FAQ pages where only one section should be open at a time.
Use type="multiple" when users need to compare content across sections, like feature lists or pricing tiers.
Start sections open (defaultIsOpen) when the content is likely needed on first view; don't make users click to see essential info.
Hide critical or required content behind a collapsible; users may not discover it.
Nest collapsibles more than two levels deep; it makes content hard to find and navigate.
