Use a collapsible for a single short paragraph; just show the text directly instead.

accessibility.name: Trigger label
accessibility.description: The trigger text must have at least 4.5:1 contrast with the surface behind it. For Pointer down, measure against the pressed overlay the trigger row paints while it is pressed.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: The root that contains one trigger and its controlled content and, in a divided group, paints the item divider.

anatomy.name: Trigger
anatomy.description: The always-visible button that toggles the content. Shows a label and a chevron indicator.

anatomy.name: Chevron
anatomy.description: Animated disclosure arrow. It follows the label by default; chevronPosition="start" moves it ahead of the label, points inward when collapsed (mirrored under RTL), and turns down when expanded.

anatomy.name: Content
anatomy.description: The area that hides or reveals when the trigger is clicked.

anatomy.name: Group container
anatomy.description: The CollapsibleGroup wrapper rendered when dividers are enabled. It contains the coordinated items and carries their density.

components.name: CollapsibleGroup
components.description: Coordinates multiple Collapsible instances so only one (single mode) or any number (multiple mode) can be open at a time. Renders no wrapper DOM element unless dividers are enabled.

props.name: type
props.description: Whether one or many items can be open simultaneously.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Default open item(s) for uncontrolled usage. Use a string for single mode and an array for multiple mode.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled open item(s).

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback invoked when the set of open items changes.

props.name: hasDividers
props.description: Whether to draw hairline dividers between the group's items. When set, the group renders a wrapper div and items default to 'balanced' density. Pair with bare Collapsible children; Card-wrapped items provide their own separation.

props.name: density
props.description: Row density controlling trigger and content block padding on the group's items. Defaults to 'balanced' when dividers are shown; otherwise items keep their default unpadded look.

props.name: chevronPosition
props.description: Logical position shared by the group's direct Collapsible items. `end` is the default trailing indicator; `start` is a leading disclosure arrow that points inward when collapsed (mirrored under RTL) and down when expanded. An individual Collapsible can still override it.

props.name: children
props.description: Collapsible instances to coordinate.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the group wrapper when hasDividers renders one.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the group wrapper when hasDividers renders one. Must be a stylex.create() value.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name for the group wrapper when hasDividers renders one. Prefer xstyle for styling.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the group wrapper when hasDividers renders one. Prefer xstyle for StyleX-optimized styling.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector forwarded to the group wrapper when hasDividers renders one.

components.name: CommandPalette
components.description: CommandPalette is a searchable dialog for quick access to commands, navigation, and actions. Use it as a keyboard-driven launcher powered by SearchSource for filtering and selection.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Whether the command palette dialog is visible.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the palette visibility changes.

props.name: searchSource
props.description: Search source providing items via search(query) and bootstrap(). Use createStaticSource for static lists.

props.name: input
props.description: Input slot. Defaults to CommandPaletteInput with standard behavior.

props.name: footer
props.description: Footer slot. Defaults to CommandPaletteFooter showing keyboard hints.

props.name: renderItem
props.description: Per-item render function for non-interactive presentation content such as labels, icons, descriptions, and shortcut hints. Do not return buttons or links inside the option. Auto-grouping by auxiliaryData.group is preserved. When omitted, renders label text.

props.name: emptySearchText
props.description: Content shown when a search query returns no results.

props.name: emptyBootstrapText
props.description: Content shown when there is no search query and bootstrap() returns nothing.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled selected value for picker mode.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called when the selected value changes in picker mode.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the command palette dialog.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the dialog.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Maximum height of the dialog.

props.name: isInline
props.description: Renders command palette content inline without modal behavior. Automatically disables input auto-focus and initial highlighted-item auto-scroll. For documentation previews and showcases only.

bestPractices.text: Provide a searchSource with bootstrap results so users see useful options before typing.
Use auxiliaryData.group on items to automatically organize results into labeled sections.
Provide a specific label when more than one command palette can appear in the same product surface.
Keep renderItem content non-interactive; each rendered row is one option, so buttons and links cannot be nested inside it.
Intercept query-field keyboard events without preserving active IME composition and native Home/End caret movement.
Use CommandPalette for simple dropdowns or menus; use Menu or Selector for inline selections.
Add too many groups or items; curate results to keep the palette fast and scannable.

anatomy.name: Dialog
anatomy.description: Modal surface that contains the command palette.

anatomy.name: Input
anatomy.description: Search region containing the query field and its supporting visuals.

anatomy.name: Search glyph
anatomy.description: Search symbol rendered by Icon in the default Input.

anatomy.name: Query field
anatomy.description: Native text field used to enter a search query.

anatomy.name: Loading spinner
anatomy.description: Spinner shown in the default Input while a search is pending.

anatomy.name: List
anatomy.description: Scrollable results container: a listbox while selectable results exist, otherwise the Empty state as plain content.

anatomy.name: Item
anatomy.description: Selectable command result rendered inside the List.

anatomy.name: Group
anatomy.description: Optional collection of Items that share a heading.

anatomy.name: Group heading
anatomy.description: Visible heading rendered for a Group.

anatomy.name: Empty
anatomy.description: Message shown when the current result set is empty.

components.name: CommandPaletteEmpty
components.description: Empty state display for the results area. CommandPalette renders it automatically when a search returns no results, or when there is no query and bootstrap() returns nothing.

props.name: children
props.description: Message or content to display.

components.name: CommandPaletteFooter
components.description: CommandPalette renders CommandPaletteFooter automatically. Pass a CommandPaletteFooter to the footer slot only when replacing the default guidance.

props.name: children
props.description: Custom footer content. When omitted, renders default keyboard hints via Kbd.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

anatomy.name: Footer
anatomy.description: Supporting region that presents default guidance or caller-provided footer content.

anatomy.name: Keyboard shortcut
anatomy.description: Default Kbd badges for navigation, selection, and dismissal.

components.name: CommandPaletteGroup
components.description: Visual grouping with a heading label. Place inside CommandPaletteList.

props.name: heading
props.description: Group heading text.

props.name: children
props.description: CommandPaletteItem children.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

components.name: CommandPaletteInput
components.description: Use CommandPaletteInput inside CommandPalette for a popup-backed command query, or as an independent search field when no result popup is present.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text for the input.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the query field, announced by screen readers. Defaults to the translated "Search commands"; the placeholder is never used as the name.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Auto-focus the input when mounted. Automatically disabled when inside an inline command palette.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content rendered at the trailing end of the input, after the spinner. Use for clear buttons or keyboard shortcut hints.

props.name: value
props.description: Search value. When omitted inside CommandPalette, reads from context.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called when search value changes. When omitted inside CommandPalette, writes to context.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

bestPractices.text: Pass a concise label that identifies what can be searched when "Search commands" does not describe it; the placeholder is never the field's name.
Use endContent for short supporting controls or shortcut hints at the trailing edge.
Override combobox role or popup state. CommandPaletteInput owns those semantics when connected to CommandPalette.

anatomy.name: Input
anatomy.description: The surrounding inline layout for the search glyph, query field, and trailing content.

anatomy.name: Search glyph
anatomy.description: A decorative search icon before the query field.

anatomy.name: Query field
anatomy.description: The native text field. It is a searchbox when standalone without popup attributes and a combobox when popup relationships are supplied or CommandPalette context is present.

anatomy.name: Loading spinner
anatomy.description: A delayed pending indicator shown before trailing content while search is busy.

anatomy.name: Trailing content
anatomy.description: Caller-provided supporting content such as a clear control or shortcut hint.

components.name: CommandPaletteItem
components.description: Use CommandPaletteItem for one non-interactive result row inside CommandPaletteList or CommandPaletteGroup. CommandPalette owns the composite keyboard model; standalone items expose only their explicit visual state and pointer activation.

props.name: value
props.description: Unique value used for item identity, highlight lookup, and selection.

props.name: children
props.description: Non-interactive item content such as a label, icon, description, or keyboard shortcut.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called after this item is activated by pointer. Keyboard selection in CommandPalette reports through CommandPalette onValueChange.

props.name: isHighlighted
props.description: Whether this item is the active keyboard result. Derived from context when omitted inside CommandPalette.

props.name: isSelected
props.description: Whether this item represents the selected value in picker mode. Derived from the CommandPalette value when omitted inside CommandPalette.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the item is unavailable and suppresses pointer activation.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

bestPractices.text: Keep each value unique within the result list so highlight, active-descendant identity, and selection resolve to the same item.

Inside CommandPalette, each item is an option in the listbox popup of the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern: keyboard focus stays in the query field, arrow keys move the highlight through aria-activedescendant, and Enter selects the highlighted item.

Nest buttons, links, or other interactive controls inside an item. Option semantics make descendants presentational, so use non-interactive content such as icons, descriptions, and shortcut hints, and activate the option itself.
Treat isHighlighted as selection. Highlight is the active keyboard result; isSelected represents the chosen value.

anatomy.name: Item
anatomy.description: The option root that carries selection, disabled, item identity, interaction, and theme state.

anatomy.name: Content
anatomy.description: Caller-provided non-interactive label and supporting presentation.

components.name: CommandPaletteList
components.description: Scrollable results container. Renders as a listbox standalone, and inside CommandPalette while selectable results exist. Contains CommandPaletteItem and CommandPaletteGroup children.

props.name: children
props.description: Items, groups, and empty states.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the listbox.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

components.name: ComplexSelector
components.description: Use ComplexSelector when a selection needs richer custom content than a Selector option row. It is intentionally one component: ComplexSelector owns the field, trigger, popover, focus restore, and changeAction flow, while the content render prop owns the selector-specific accessible structure.

bestPractices.text: Use variant="secondary" beside secondary buttons, or variant="ghost" beside ghost buttons; add a startIcon when it helps identify the trigger. Use alignment="end" when a wide surface should align its end edge to the trigger.
For staged editors, keep draft state in the composed content and call the provided onChange helper only from Apply. Cancel or dismiss without committing.

Compose the dialog content from the appropriate accessible structure for the job: RadioList for a simple choice, Calendar/date inputs for date picking, TreeList or a searchable list for hierarchy, or a custom grid when two-dimensional arrow navigation is useful.
Use the provided onChange helper from children; it already calls both onChange and changeAction and updates optimistic busy state.
Call close() from custom content when a selection should dismiss the popup. Keep it open for multi-step content or freeform entry flows.
Use Astryx focus hooks for custom content: useGridFocus for two-dimensional grids, useTreeFocus through TreeList for hierarchies, and useListFocus for custom linear collections.

Evaluate custom content against WCAG 2.2: keyboard operation, focus visible/not obscured, names and roles, labels/instructions, target size, and contrast/non-text contrast are especially relevant for selector popovers.
Do not rebuild trigger ARIA, popover focus management, or changeAction handling in product code.
Do not use ComplexSelector for a plain single-column text list; use Selector instead.
Wrap a disabled ComplexSelector in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; the text would not describe the trigger. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

anatomy.name: Field
anatomy.description: Field shell that provides the label and optional supporting field content.

anatomy.name: Trigger
anatomy.description: Control that displays the current value or placeholder and opens the popup.

anatomy.name: Icon-rendered start icon
anatomy.description: Optional leading icon, by built-in meaning or icon component, rendered through Icon.

anatomy.name: Caller-rendered start content
anatomy.description: Optional arbitrary React content rendered directly at the start of the trigger.

anatomy.name: Indicator icon
anatomy.description: Trailing chevron shown when status presentation does not replace it; rotates to reflect whether the popup is open.

anatomy.name: Popup
anatomy.description: Mounted dialog surface that is painted and shown while open and hidden while closed.

components.name: ContextMenu
components.description: A right-click context menu that appears at the cursor position. Use to provide contextual actions for specific elements or regions without cluttering the UI with visible buttons.

props.name: children
props.description: The trigger area: right-click on this content to open the menu.

props.name: items
props.description: Data-driven menu entries. Pass exactly one of `items` or `menuContent`. Each entry is one of: an action item `{label, onClick?, icon?, isDisabled?, variant?, items?}` (nested `items` open a flyout in popover presentation and drill into a new view in bottom-sheet presentation; variant `"destructive"` renders it in the error color), a divider `{type: "divider"}`, or a section `{type: "section", title?, items: [...action items]}`.

props.name: menuContent
props.description: Custom JSX menu content for compound mode. Pass exactly one of `menuContent` or `items`.

props.name: menuWidth
props.description: Custom menu width.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of menu items: controls padding density.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the menu surface, announced when it opens.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback fired when the menu opens or closes.

props.name: presentation
props.description: Presentation policy. `popover` opens at the pointer position, `bottom-sheet` always uses an action sheet, and `adaptive` uses the BottomSheet on a compact touch screen: a coarse primary pointer, and a viewport narrower than the theme `md` breakpoint (768px by default) or shorter than 500px.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: When true, right-click shows the native browser context menu instead.

props.name: triggerXstyle
props.description: Styles applied to the trigger wrapper. Accepts `stylex.create()` values, not inline style objects.

props.name: triggerAs
props.description: The element the trigger wrapper renders as. 'div' is a block; 'span' an inline wrapper, so a reference inside prose can own a context menu without breaking the text flow.

bestPractices.text: Keep menu items concise and action-oriented; users expect quick access to contextual actions.
Use sections and dividers to group related actions when the menu has many items.
Use `presentation="adaptive"` when right-click should remain cursor-positioned on desktop while long-press opens a reachable BottomSheet on compact touch devices.
Ensure all context menu actions are also accessible via other UI elements for keyboard-only users.
Keep a visible MoreMenu or equivalent trigger for important mobile actions; long-press must not be the only route.
Use a ContextMenu as the only way to access important actions; not all users know to right-click.
Place more than 10–12 items in a single menu without grouping them into sections.

anatomy.name: Trigger area
anatomy.description: Caller-provided region that accepts right-click, keyboard context-menu, and long-press input.

anatomy.name: Pointer menu surface
anatomy.description: Cursor-positioned menu panel used by the pointer presentation.

anatomy.name: Pointer action row
anatomy.description: DropdownMenu-owned action, selectable option, or submenu row in the pointer presentation.

anatomy.name: Touch sheet frame
anatomy.description: BottomSheet panel, content area, handle, and optional scrim that host touch actions.

anatomy.name: Touch menu surface
anatomy.description: ContextMenu-owned content panel rendered inside the touch sheet frame.

anatomy.name: Touch action list
anatomy.description: Spacious List that groups data-driven touch actions.

anatomy.name: Touch action row
anatomy.description: ListItem button used for a data-driven action or drill-in entry in the touch presentation.

components.name: ContextMenuItem
components.description: Menu item component for compound mode. Re-exported from DropdownMenuItem for discoverability.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon to display before the label; pass a built-in meaning such as 'search' (see `astryx docs icons`), an icon component, or an icon element.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary label text.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary description text displayed below the label.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Callback when the item is selected. A keyboard activation arrives as a synthesized click carrying the key's modifiers. On a row with `href` it runs before the browser navigates and is skipped for a modified click (⌘, Ctrl, Shift, Alt, middle button), which is left to the browser.

props.name: href
props.description: Address the row navigates to. The row then renders as a real anchor with role="menuitem" (through LinkProvider), so a modified click or a middle click keeps the browser's meaning — a new tab — instead of running onClick.

props.name: target
props.description: Link target. Only used with href.

props.name: rel
props.description: Link relationship. noopener noreferrer is added for target="_blank". Only used with href.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the row is unavailable. Disabled rows expose aria-disabled, remove link destinations, and suppress activation.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Additional content rendered after the label and description.

props.name: hasCloseOnSelect
props.description: Whether activating the item closes the menu. Set false for an action that reports its result on the item itself.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual variant. 'destructive' renders the label, description, and icon in the error color for dangerous actions (e.g. Delete).

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the row root, the element carrying role="menuitem". Register the row with an element-keyed observer or overlay.

components.name: createAnimator
components.description: Animates one element with the motion Astryx's own components use, without React. `animate` springs an element to new values on the state-change motion, `decay` flings it with the momentum of a released scroll view, and `set` moves it directly, so a card can follow a finger, snap back and be thrown away. Use the `useAnimator` hook in React. To animate an area's layout as its items change, use `useAnimatedLayout`; for what a component already animates, such as a sheet's detents or a carousel's snapping, use the component's own props.

bestPractices.text: Start every `animate` that follows a drag with the release velocity, so the element carries on as it was thrown.
Reach every state an animation shows without the animation too: a key, a button or a menu item that calls the same code.
`await` the promise before removing an element you animate out, and call `destroy` once it is gone.
Read the element’s position from layout while it moves: `get` gives the value on screen, wherever the motion runs.

accessibility.name: Keyboard and assistive technology
accessibility.description: An animator moves an element; it adds no way to act. Give every action an animation stands for a control a keyboard and a screen reader can reach, such as a button that discards a card, and have it call `animate`, which Reduce Motion turns into a fade in place. Keep `decay` for a throw the person made: Reduce Motion keeps the momentum of a coast, as it continues that throw. Keep focus on an element that stays on screen: move it before you fling its element away.

accessibility.name: Reduce Motion
accessibility.description: When the person asks for reduced motion, every call is planned for them. On a touch screen a move or a scale becomes a short opacity cross-fade: the element fades out where it was and fades back in where it lands. With a mouse it lands at once. A decay of `x` and `y` keeps its momentum, as it continues the throw the person made; a decay of `scale`, `rotate` or `opacity` is planned like a move. No option turns this off.

components.name: createDragToSnapPoints
components.description: Lets a drag move an element along one axis and settles it on snap points when the finger lifts, the way an iOS sheet settles on its detents: on the nearest snap point to where it is, on the next one in its direction after a quick flick, and back where it started when the finger was moving back. The settle continues the release's velocity. For a bottom sheet, use BottomSheet's `snapPoints`; for a scrolling row, Carousel's `hasSnap`. Use the `useDragToSnapPoints` hook in React.

bestPractices.text: Offer the same positions without a drag: buttons or keys that call `settleTo`.
Keep the snap points few and far apart, so a release clearly picks one.
Use it for a sheet or a carousel: their own props already settle the way people expect.

accessibility.name: Keyboard and assistive technology
accessibility.description: A drag is one way in, never the only one. Give each snap point a control a keyboard and a screen reader can reach, such as Expand and Collapse buttons, and call `settleTo` from it. When a position changes what the element shows, announce the change.

accessibility.name: Reduce Motion
accessibility.description: When the person asks for reduced motion, the settle after a touch drag becomes a short cross-fade into the snap point, as does any settle on a device whose primary pointer is coarse, such as a tablet; after a mouse or pen drag elsewhere it lands at once. `settleTo` fades on such a device and lands at once with a fine primary pointer. While the finger is down, the element still follows it.

components.name: createPanGesture
components.description: Reports a drag on an element as values, without React, for a surface the product moves itself: a card that follows the finger, a drawer pulled by its handle. A finger, a mouse and a pen all drive it. A mouse or pen drag that starts on selectable text selects that text, and the pan reports nothing. Give that text `user-select: none`. The drag claims its touch at UIKit’s 10 pt, as `UIPanGestureRecognizer` does, so a tap stays a tap and a press or a long press is never reported as a pan. Use the `usePanGesture` hook in React. Where a component already offers the behavior, use its prop instead: BottomSheet's `snapPoints`, Carousel's `hasSnap`. Its example is on the usePanGesture page: one draggable box, made once with the hook and once with createPanGesture.

bestPractices.text: Move the element from `translation` added to where it was when the drag began, so it moves with the finger from the moment the drag claims it.
At `ended`, hand `velocity` to the animation that settles the element, so a flick carries on at the speed it was released.
Call `destroy` when the element leaves the page, so no listener outlives it.
Read the element’s layout on every `changed` event to place it; `translation` already says where the finger is.

accessibility.name: Keyboard and assistive technology
accessibility.description: A drag has no keyboard or assistive-technology path of its own: whatever the drag does needs another way to do it, such as buttons, arrow keys or a menu.

accessibility.name: Reduce Motion
accessibility.description: The pan moves nothing itself, so Reduce Motion applies to the motion you drive from it: a settle or a throw goes to its end without travel when the person asks for reduced motion.

components.name: createReorderable
components.description: Makes a collection's rows reorderable. On a touch screen a finger held still on a row's handle for a moment picks it up (a flick on the handle still scrolls): the row stays in its place, dimmed, while a copy of it follows the finger and an accent line marks where it would land; the other rows stay still, the page scrolls near its edges, and on release the rows rearrange. A pen held still on a handle where the primary pointer is coarse picks the row up as a finger does. A mouse, or a pen where the primary pointer is fine, drags a handle at once the same way, and the rows take their places without motion; a cancelled drag puts everything back at once. Without a drag, the handle toggles reorder mode for its row (a click, Space or Enter): each arrow key moves the row a place at once, and Escape or another activation ends the mode, keeping the moves; screen readers hear each move with the row's place and neighbours, and a hint shows the moves and Done as buttons, for taps alone. The reorder code ships with this function: a collection without the prop loads none of it.

bestPractices.text: Give each row a stable key from your data, a string or a number (`itemKey={item.id}`), and apply each move by rendering the items in their new order in the same task.
Use `isReorderable` for rows that must stay put, such as a pinned first row.
Offer reorder mode from your own UI too, such as a row's context menu, with `reorderable.start(item.id)`.
Use React's `key` as the reorder key, or index-based keys: a move changes every index after it.

components.name: createSwipe
components.description: Gives a list row the verbs a sideways swipe uncovers, the way a mail row reveals Archive and Delete on a phone: `const mail = createSwipe({trailing: [{id: 'archive', label: 'Archive', onActivate: ({itemKey}) => archive(itemKey)}]})`, then `<ListItem label="Inbox" itemKey={message.id} swipe={mail} />`. A finger, a pen or a trackpad’s two-finger swipe drags the row; a mouse never does. A plain function, not a hook, pure and cheap: define the swipe once at module scope, where each handler reads the row from `itemKey`, or in `useMemo` when its handlers need component state. A new value with the same ids neither closes an open row nor restarts its settle, and it does no DOM work. The swipe’s code comes with this function, so a row given `swipe` is swipeable at its first paint and an app that never imports it ships none of it.

bestPractices.text: Give every swipe action a second home in the row, such as a menu or a button in endContent: a verb reachable only by swipe is unreachable by keyboard and by mouse.
Put the rows in a List, which clips them in the inline axis; any other container sets overflow-inline: clip once.
Give a `commit` side more than one entry: it fires none of them.

accessibility.name: Keyboard and assistive technology
accessibility.description: The swipe is a touch accelerator. A closed row’s panels are out of the accessibility tree and the tab order; an open row’s entries are real buttons under `reveal`, named by their labels, and Escape closes the row. Every verb must also be reachable through the row’s own content.

accessibility.name: Reduce Motion
accessibility.description: When the person asks for reduced motion, the row reaches its resting place with no travel or spring and cross-fades when a finger started the swipe.

components.name: DateInput
components.description: DateInput lets the user type or pick a date from a calendar popover. Use it for scheduling, deadlines, booking dates, or any form field that needs a specific calendar date.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hide the label.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text displayed below the label.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Show an "(optional)" indicator next to the label.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Mark the field as required.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disable the input and calendar. The field stays focusable and exposes `aria-disabled`; typing and opening are blocked.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the input is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus (activation stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled DateInput in Tooltip.

props.name: value
props.description: Selected date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback invoked when the selected date changes.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action fired after onChange. Drives optimistic UI updates via useTransition.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Whether the input is in a loading state. The field stays focusable and exposes `aria-busy` with a spinner; typing, picking, and clearing are blocked until loading ends.

props.name: min
props.description: Minimum selectable date (YYYY-MM-DD).

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum selectable date (YYYY-MM-DD).

props.name: dateConstraints
props.description: Array of custom constraint functions that disable specific dates.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown in the text input. A caller placeholder replaces the calendar format hint.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the input control.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator object for error, warning, or success states with a message. For a date the field rejects, typed or picked in the native control, and for unreadable or unfinished text that Enter or blur keeps, the field shows its own error message instead; with onEntryErrorChange, an error status with a message shows in place of that message. A warning or success never replaces a rejection.

props.name: onEntryErrorChange
props.type: (error: {kind: 'unreadable' | 'incomplete' | 'nonexistent' | 'outOfRange' | 'unavailable', text: string, date?: ISODateString} | null) => void
props.description: Called each time the field's rejection of typed text changes, and with null when the rejection ends. kind is 'unreadable', 'incomplete' (part of a date that Enter or blur cannot finish), 'nonexistent' (a date the calendar does not have), 'outOfRange' (before min or after max), or 'unavailable' (a day dateConstraints rules out); text is the typed text; date is the Gregorian ISO date the text names, for 'outOfRange' and 'unavailable'. It also runs when a new min, max, dateConstraints, or value, a calendar pick, disabling the field, or Enter or blur changes the rejection, and never twice for the same rejection; it reports null when the typed field leaves while its rejection stands, as when a presentation or pointer change shows the native or touch picker. With it, an error status with a message replaces the field's own message, and a rejection that starts under an unchanged error message announces that message once. The native and touch pickers take no typed text, so it never reports a rejection there.

props.name: entryErrorBehavior
props.description: When the field shows its own entry error: a typed date it rejects, as onEntryErrorChange reports it. It sets when the error shows, not when validation runs, so it is not React Aria's validationBehavior (native versus ARIA validation), and it never changes a caller status. 'complete' shows a date the calendar does not have, or one outside min, max, or dateConstraints, as soon as the typed date is complete, and unreadable or unfinished text at Enter or blur. 'blur-or-enter' holds every rejection until Enter or blur: the message, aria-invalid, the invalid styling, the announcement, and the onEntryErrorChange report then appear together. Under both values, an edit that makes the text a date or empties it clears the error at once; under 'blur-or-enter', an edit that leaves the text wrong keeps the shown error until the next Enter or blur. A date the native control refuses shows at Enter or blur under both values. The field's own value wins over the nearest FormLayout's defaultEntryErrorBehavior.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip hides the message box and surfaces it in a tooltip on the status icon.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text displayed via an info icon at the end of the label.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Shows a clear (×) button when a date value is set. Clicking it clears the value and returns focus to the input.

props.name: numberOfMonths
props.description: Number of months displayed simultaneously in the calendar popover.

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.description: First day of week in Astryx calendar surfaces. A number (0 = Sunday to 6 = Saturday) or a three-letter day name; native pickers remain browser/OS-owned.

props.name: format
props.description: How the committed date value is displayed. Named values are reused from Timestamp's format vocabulary: 'date' shows 'Mar 21, 2026', 'date_long' shows 'March 21, 2026', 'date_weekday' shows 'Wed, Mar 21, 2026', 'system_date' shows '2026-03-21'. 'date', 'date_long', and 'date_weekday' write the date in the field's calendar; 'system_date' stays the Gregorian ISO date. A function receives the ISO value and returns a custom string; the field cannot re-commit text it cannot read back. Applies only to the committed value, never to text being typed.

props.name: calendar
props.description: The calendar the text field reads and writes dates in, and the calendar its popover and bottom sheet show. value, onChange, min, and max stay Gregorian ISO dates. People type a date the way the locale writes it in this calendar, in any decimal digits; the field reports a date only once it is complete, and names a date the calendar does not have. Years are years of this calendar: a Buddhist field reads 2026 as Buddhist year 2026, so set min and max on Buddhist and Minguo calendar fields to catch a Gregorian year typed by mistake. Calendars other than gregory, iso8601, buddhist, roc, and japanese need Temporal, native or a polyfill the application loads; without it the field shows Gregorian dates. With a calendar other than gregory or iso8601, a presentation that would show the native date control shows the popover on a fine pointer and the bottom sheet on a coarse pointer, because the native control is Gregorian; the bottom sheet shows the months, leap months, and era years of the calendar. A year in which the era changes is labeled with the era of the shown month, such as 平成31 in January 2019 and 令和元 in July.

props.name: presentation
props.description: Which surface draws the date picker. 'adaptive-native' (the default) uses Astryx's calendar popover on a fine pointer and the browser/OS picker (input type=date) on a coarse pointer, keeping Astryx fallbacks where a native control cannot express the value; 'native' always uses the browser/OS picker with no fallback; 'adaptive-bottom-sheet' uses the popover on a fine pointer and Astryx's bottom-sheet picker on a coarse pointer; 'popover' and 'bottom-sheet' force that Astryx surface on every pointer. Every value opens a picker; a typed-only field is TimeInput's alone. Use a non-native presentation for a field that needs weekStartsOn, numberOfMonths or dateConstraints, none of which a native picker can express. With a calendar other than gregory or iso8601, 'native' and 'adaptive-native' use the popover on a fine pointer and the bottom sheet on a coarse pointer, and an explicit 'native' warns in development.

props.name: nativePicker
props.description: Deprecated: use presentation ('touch' = 'adaptive-native', 'always' = 'native', 'never' = 'adaptive-bottom-sheet'). Still works exactly as released; presentation wins when both are set. With a calendar other than gregory or iso8601, 'touch' and 'always' use the popover on a fine pointer and the bottom sheet on a coarse pointer.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the Field box around the label, control, and status. containerClassName and containerStyle take a class name and inline styles for the same box. No effect (development warning) where no Field box renders: inside InputGroup (style the group) and in a horizontal-labels FormLayout.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the Field box. Same targeting as containerXstyle.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the Field box. Same targeting as containerXstyle.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the bordered element that holds the text, icons, and end controls, never the native input. controlClassName and controlStyle take a class name and inline styles for the same box. Replaces root xstyle, className, and style, which this component does not accept.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Class name for the visual control box. Same targeting as controlXstyle.

props.name: controlStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the visual control box. Same targeting as controlXstyle.

bestPractices.text: Base props such as ref, id, data-*, aria-*, and DOM event handlers go to the date input, the element that is focused and announced. A DOM handler runs after DateInput's own handler for the same event and still receives events it handled (including ones it called preventDefault on), so it cannot cancel built-in behavior.
Provide clear labels and descriptions so users understand what date is expected.
Use min, max, and dateConstraints to restrict selectable dates to valid ranges.
Set min and max on a Buddhist or Minguo calendar field, so a Gregorian year typed by mistake shows an error instead of a date centuries away.
Use hasClear when the date is optional so the user can reset it.
Show a loading state with changeAction when the date triggers a server-side save.

On a fine pointer the field follows the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern with a dialog popup, as in the APG date picker combobox: ArrowDown or Alt+ArrowDown opens the calendar, and Escape closes it and returns focus to the field.
Use DateInput inside InputGroup when adding a short static prefix or suffix, such as a due-date hint.
Use a DateInput for free-form text that does not represent a calendar date.
Hide the label without surrounding context that makes the field purpose obvious.
Rely on the calendar alone; the text input lets users type dates directly, which is faster for known dates.
Wrap a disabled DateInput in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop instead, which ties the reason to the field.

anatomy.name: Text input
anatomy.description: A field where the user can type a date directly, written the way the locale writes it in the field's calendar.

anatomy.name: Calendar icon
anatomy.description: A button that opens the calendar popover for visual date picking.

anatomy.name: Calendar popover
anatomy.description: A month grid that appears when the icon or the input is clicked, or when ArrowDown is pressed in the input.

anatomy.name: Clear button
anatomy.description: A × button that resets the date value. Shown when hasClear is true and a date is set.

anatomy.name: Status message
anatomy.description: An error, warning, or success message below the input.

components.name: DateRangeInput
components.description: DateRangeInput lets users select a start and end date from a dual-month calendar popover. Use it for filtering data by time period, report generation, analytics dashboards, and booking flows.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hide the label.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text displayed below the label.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Show an "(optional)" indicator.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Mark the field as required.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disable the trigger and picker. The trigger stays focusable and exposes `aria-disabled`; opening is blocked.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the input is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and describes the trigger (activation stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled DateRangeInput in Tooltip.

props.name: value
props.description: Selected date range or null. Import the `DateRange` type from `@astryxdesign/core/DateRangeInput`; it is `{start: ISODateString, end: ISODateString}`. Do NOT redeclare your own DateRange type; use the exported one so TypeScript structurally matches.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback when the range changes. Called with null on clear.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action fired after onChange. Drives optimistic UI updates via useTransition.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Whether the input is in a loading state. Disables interaction and shows a spinner.

props.name: min
props.description: Minimum selectable date. `ISODateString` is a template literal type (`\`${number}${number}${number}${number}-${number}${number}-${number}${number}\``). Pass a string literal like `"2026-01-28"`, not a runtime string variable. Import it from `@astryxdesign/core/Calendar` or use `as ISODateString` if computing the value dynamically.

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum selectable date. Same template literal type as `min`: use a YYYY-MM-DD string literal or cast with `as ISODateString`.

props.name: dateConstraints
props.description: Custom constraint functions to disable specific dates.

props.name: maxRangeSpan
props.description: Maximum days a selected range may span, counting both endpoints (`7` = a 7-day window, start + 6). Once a start is picked, days beyond this distance are disabled so the range cannot stretch past the cap. Rolling window relative to the start; for fixed calendar bounds use `min`/`max`. Constrains selection only; it never rewrites a `value` already wider than the cap (flag that with `status`).

props.name: minRangeSpan
props.description: Minimum days a selected range must span, counting both endpoints (`2` forbids a single-day range). Once a start is picked, days closer than this are disabled. Clicking the start again commits a one-day range when allowed, or cancels the in-progress selection when the minimum is longer. Defaults to 1 (same-day start and end allowed).

props.name: presets
props.description: Preset ranges shown as quick-select options beside the calendar, or above it when the two do not fit side by side. A preset is disabled when either endpoint violates min, max, or dateConstraints, or when its span violates minRangeSpan or maxRangeSpan.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Shows a clear button when a range is selected.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text when no range is selected.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the trigger.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator for error, warning, or success states.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip hides the message box and surfaces it in a tooltip on the status icon.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text via info icon at label end.

props.name: numberOfMonths
props.description: Number of months in the calendar.

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.description: First day of week in the calendar. A number (0 = Sunday to 6 = Saturday) or a three-letter day name.

props.name: calendar
props.description: The calendar the trigger text and the popover calendar show, such as persian, hebrew, or buddhist. value, onChange, min, max, and presets stay Gregorian ISO dates. The field has no typed entry. Calendars other than gregory, iso8601, buddhist, roc, and japanese need Temporal, native or a polyfill the application loads; without it the field shows Gregorian dates and warns in development. Month starts in the Chinese and Dangi calendars come from the runtime's Temporal; when you render on the server, load the same Temporal implementation on the server and in the browser.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the Field box around the label, control, and status. containerClassName and containerStyle take a class name and inline styles for the same box. No effect (development warning) where no Field box renders: inside InputGroup (style the group) and in a horizontal-labels FormLayout.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the bordered element that holds the text, icons, and end controls, never the native input. controlClassName and controlStyle take a class name and inline styles for the same box. Replaces root xstyle, className, and style, which this component does not accept.

bestPractices.text: Base props such as ref, id, data-*, aria-*, and DOM event handlers go to the range trigger, the element that is focused and announced. A DOM handler runs after DateRangeInput's own handler for the same event and still receives events it handled (including ones it called preventDefault on), so it cannot cancel built-in behavior.
Use presets for common ranges like "Last 7 days" to speed up selection.
Use min/max to constrain selectable dates to valid ranges.
Keep hasClear enabled (default) so users can reset the filter.
Provide clear labels and descriptions so users understand what the range controls.
Use DateRangeInput when only a single date is needed; use DateInput instead.
Hide the label without surrounding context that makes the purpose obvious.
Wrap a disabled DateRangeInput in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop instead, which ties the reason to the field.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Text above the trigger describing what date range is expected.

anatomy.name: Field surface
anatomy.description: Bordered control containing the calendar toggle, range trigger, and end affordances.

anatomy.name: Trigger button
anatomy.description: A button showing the formatted range or placeholder. Clicking opens the popover.

anatomy.name: Calendar icon
anatomy.description: A trailing icon that also opens the popover.

anatomy.name: Calendar popover
anatomy.description: A dual-month calendar grid with range selection and hover preview.

anatomy.name: Preset sidebar
anatomy.description: A list of preset range options beside the calendar, or above it when the two do not fit side by side.

anatomy.name: Preset button
anatomy.description: A quick-select action for one preset range, reflecting current and disabled states.

anatomy.name: Clear button
anatomy.description: A × button that resets the range to null.

anatomy.name: Status message
anatomy.description: An error, warning, or success message below the trigger.

components.name: DateTimeInput
components.description: DateTimeInput combines date and time selection in one field. With presentation="adaptive-native" (the default), mouse/trackpad devices use Astryx typed fields and popovers, while coarse-pointer devices use browser/OS date and time controls in the same two-segment field. presentation="native" uses both native controls on every pointer; presentation="adaptive-bottom-sheet" keeps Astryx's own surfaces — pointer fields on fine pointers and the coordinated Date/Time bottom sheet on coarse pointers; "popover" and "bottom-sheet" force one Astryx surface on every pointer. The closed segments stay side by side when at least 400px is available and wrap into full-width rows below 400px, independent of viewport width. Use it for scheduling, event creation, deadline setting, or any form field that needs a specific datetime.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hide the label.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text displayed below the label.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Show an "(optional)" indicator next to the label.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Mark the field as required.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disable the input and picker. The fields stay focusable and expose `aria-disabled`; typing and opening are blocked.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the input is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and describes the fields (activation stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled DateTimeInput in Tooltip.

props.name: value
props.description: Selected datetime in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS).

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback invoked when the selected datetime changes.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action fired after onChange. Drives optimistic UI updates via useTransition.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Whether the input is in a loading state. Disables interaction and shows a spinner.

props.name: min
props.description: Minimum selectable datetime. Constrains both date and time selection.

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum selectable datetime. Constrains both date and time selection.

props.name: dateConstraints
props.description: Array of custom constraint functions that disable specific dates.

props.name: hasSeconds
props.description: Include seconds in the time portion. Keeps Astryx's time field even when nativePicker selects native surfaces, because iOS has no seconds wheel.

props.name: hourFormat
props.description: Hour display format. '12h' shows the locale's day period; '24h' uses 24-hour notation. When unset, follows the InternationalizationProvider locale's hour cycle (en-US 12-hour, en-GB 24-hour); a person's own preference rides on the locale tag (e.g. 'en-US-u-hc-h23').

props.name: timeIncrement
props.description: Minute step for arrow keys in Astryx's typed time field. A non-default value keeps the Astryx time field in nativePicker modes because iOS treats native step as validation, not picker cadence. Ignored by the Astryx touch sheet, which uses wheels.

props.name: timeOptionInterval
props.description: Minute cadence for the preset-time combobox on Astryx's fine-pointer time field. Setting it keeps that Astryx time field even in nativePicker modes because the OS picker has no equivalent preset list. The Astryx touch sheet uses wheels.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Shows a clear button when a datetime value is set.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown in the date portion when no date is selected. A caller placeholder replaces the calendar format hint.

props.name: calendar
props.description: The calendar the date segment reads and writes typed dates in, and the calendar its popover and bottom sheet show. value, onChange, min, and max stay Gregorian ISO datetimes. People type a date the way the locale writes it in this calendar, in any decimal digits; the field reports a date only once it is complete, and names a date the calendar does not have. Years are years of this calendar, so set min and max on Buddhist and Minguo calendar fields to catch a Gregorian year typed by mistake. Calendars other than gregory, iso8601, buddhist, roc, and japanese need Temporal, native or a polyfill the application loads; without it the field shows Gregorian dates. With a calendar other than gregory or iso8601, a presentation that would show native controls shows the popovers on a fine pointer and the bottom sheet on a coarse pointer, because the native date control is Gregorian; the Date panel of the bottom sheet shows the months, leap months, and era years of the calendar. A year in which the era changes is labeled with the era of the shown month, such as 平成31 in January 2019 and 令和元 in July.

props.name: timePlaceholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown in the time portion when no time is selected. On touch, this appears in the closed time segment before a time is chosen.

props.name: timeLabel
props.description: Accessible label for the time portion. Defaults to "{label} time" so it is tied to the field label and localizable.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the input control.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator object for error, warning, or success states with a message. For a date the field rejects, typed or picked in the native control, and for unreadable or unfinished text that Enter or blur keeps, the field shows its own error message instead; with onEntryErrorChange, an error status with a message shows in place of that message. A warning or success never replaces a rejection. A typed time the time segment rejects shows once it is complete, or at Enter or blur, and stays in the field; its own error message shows unless the date segment shows its message or an error status with a message shows in its place.

props.name: onEntryErrorChange
props.type: (error: {kind: 'unreadable' | 'incomplete' | 'nonexistent' | 'outOfRange' | 'unavailable', text: string, date?: ISODateString} | null) => void
props.description: Called each time the date segment's rejection of typed text changes, and with null when the rejection ends. kind is 'unreadable', 'incomplete' (part of a date that Enter or blur cannot finish), 'nonexistent' (a date the calendar does not have), 'outOfRange' (before the date of min or after the date of max), or 'unavailable' (a day dateConstraints rules out); text is the typed text; date is the Gregorian ISO date the text names, for 'outOfRange' and 'unavailable'. It also runs when a new min, max, dateConstraints, or value, a calendar pick, disabling the field, or Enter or blur changes the rejection, and never twice for the same rejection; it reports null when the typed field leaves while its rejection stands, as when a presentation or pointer change shows the native or touch picker. With it, an error status with a message replaces the field's own message, and a rejection that starts under an unchanged error message announces that message once. The native and touch pickers take no typed text, so it never reports a rejection there.

props.name: entryErrorBehavior
props.description: When both segments show their own entry errors: a typed date or time the field rejects. It sets when the error shows, not when validation runs, so it is not React Aria's validationBehavior (native versus ARIA validation), and it never changes a caller status. 'complete' shows a complete typed date the calendar does not have or that is out of range, a complete typed time outside the range, and a time the native control reports outside the range at once, and other rejected text at Enter or blur. 'blur-or-enter' holds every rejection until Enter or blur in its segment: the message, aria-invalid, the invalid styling, the announcement, and the date segment's onEntryErrorChange report then appear together. Under both values, an edit the field accepts or that empties the segment clears the error at once; under 'blur-or-enter', an edit that leaves the entry wrong keeps the shown error until the next Enter or blur. A date the native control refuses shows at Enter or blur under both values. The field's own value wins over the nearest FormLayout's defaultEntryErrorBehavior.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text displayed via an info icon at the end of the label.

props.name: numberOfMonths
props.description: Number of months displayed simultaneously in Astryx's pointer calendar popover. Ignored by native date controls and the mobile touch sheet, whose Date panel always shows one swipe-paged month at a time.

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.description: First day of week in Astryx calendars. A number (0 = Sunday to 6 = Saturday) or a three-letter day name. Ignored by native date controls.

props.name: presentation
props.description: Which surfaces draw the date and time pickers. 'adaptive-native' (the default) uses Astryx's typed fields and popovers on a fine pointer and browser/OS controls on a coarse pointer — with per-segment Astryx fallbacks: hasSeconds, non-default timeIncrement, or timeOptionInterval retain Astryx's time field because iOS cannot express them faithfully; 'native' always uses both browser/OS controls with no fallback; 'adaptive-bottom-sheet' uses popovers on a fine pointer and Astryx's coordinated bottom sheet on a coarse pointer; 'popover' and 'bottom-sheet' force that Astryx surface on every pointer. Every value opens pickers; typed-only fields are TimeInput's alone. Use a non-native presentation when numberOfMonths, weekStartsOn, or visible dateConstraints behavior matters. Constraints are enforced on commit; min/max are forwarded as hints. hourFormat formats the closed time, while the OS picker follows the user's locale. With a calendar other than gregory or iso8601, 'native' and 'adaptive-native' use the popovers on a fine pointer and the bottom sheet on a coarse pointer, and an explicit 'native' warns in development.

props.name: nativePicker
props.description: Deprecated: use presentation ('touch' = 'adaptive-native', 'always' = 'native', 'never' = 'adaptive-bottom-sheet'). Still works exactly as released; presentation wins when both are set. With a calendar other than gregory or iso8601, 'touch' and 'always' use the popovers on a fine pointer and the bottom sheet on a coarse pointer.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the Field box around the label, control, and status. containerClassName and containerStyle take a class name and inline styles for the same box. No effect (development warning) where no Field box renders: inside InputGroup (style the group) and in a horizontal-labels FormLayout.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the row that holds the bordered date and time segments with their icons and end controls, never a native input. controlClassName and controlStyle take a class name and inline styles for the same box. Replaces root xstyle, className, and style, which this component does not accept.

bestPractices.text: Base props such as ref, id, data-*, aria-*, and DOM event handlers go to the date input, the element that is focused and announced. A DOM handler runs after DateTimeInput's own handler for the same event and still receives events it handled (including ones it called preventDefault on), so it cannot cancel built-in behavior.
Provide clear labels and descriptions so users understand what datetime is expected.
Use min and max to restrict selectable datetimes to valid ranges.
Set min and max on a Buddhist or Minguo calendar field, so a Gregorian year typed by mistake shows an error instead of a date centuries away.
Use hasClear when the datetime is optional so the user can reset it.

Leave hourFormat unset so the field follows the InternationalizationProvider locale's hour cycle (12-hour in en-US, 24-hour in en-GB or de-DE). Set it only when the field itself needs a fixed format, and carry a person's own 12/24-hour preference on the provider locale (e.g. 'en-US-u-hc-h23') rather than on each field.
Use DateTimeInput when only a date is needed; use DateInput instead.
Use DateTimeInput when only a time is needed; use TimeInput instead.
Hide the label without surrounding context that makes the field purpose obvious.
Wrap a disabled DateTimeInput in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop instead, which ties the reason to the field.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Text above the input describing what datetime is expected.

anatomy.name: Segment row
anatomy.description: The unbordered layout row that holds the two bordered segments and wraps them when its container is narrow.

anatomy.name: Date input
anatomy.description: A typed date field with calendar popover on the fine-pointer Astryx surface, a real input type=date in native modes, or a read-only segment opening the Astryx touch sheet under presentation="adaptive-bottom-sheet" on a coarse pointer.

anatomy.name: Calendar icon
anatomy.description: A button that opens the active date surface: the platform picker, Astryx calendar popover, or Astryx touch sheet.

anatomy.name: Date picker
anatomy.description: The browser/OS picker in native modes, an Astryx month-grid popover on a fine pointer, or the Date panel of the Astryx bottom sheet on a coarse pointer with presentation="adaptive-bottom-sheet".

anatomy.name: Time input
anatomy.description: A real input type=time for the default minute-precision native mode, a text/combobox time field when seconds, custom increments, or preset options are requested, or a read-only segment opening accessible time wheels under presentation="adaptive-bottom-sheet" on a coarse pointer.

anatomy.name: Clock icon
anatomy.description: The time glyph shown as a leading identifier on the Astryx pointer field and as the picker affordance in native and touch-sheet time segments.

anatomy.name: Time options popover
anatomy.description: A list of preset times at the timeOptionInterval cadence. Setting the prop retains Astryx's text/combobox time field even when nativePicker otherwise selects native controls; the Astryx touch sheet uses wheels instead.

anatomy.name: Time option
anatomy.description: One selectable preset time in the optional time-options popover.

anatomy.name: Clear button
anatomy.description: A × button that resets the datetime value.

components.name: Dialog
components.description: Dialog displays a modal overlay that blocks interaction with the page until the user responds. Use it for delete confirmations, edit forms, terms acceptance, or any decision that should not be skipped. For cases where you want to show a dialog without managing open state, use the `useImperativeDialog` hook: call `dialog.show(content)` and render `dialog.element` in your tree.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Whether the dialog is open.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback when dialog visibility changes.

props.name: children
props.description: Dialog content.

props.name: width
props.description: Preferred width of the dialog in pixels or any CSS value. Standard dialogs clamp to their container and the dynamic viewport with spacing-token gutters so narrow viewports keep content on screen.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Maximum height of the dialog. Defaults to a dynamic viewport value so browser UI changes are reflected where supported.

props.name: position
props.description: Static position for the dialog; centered by default when omitted. Use logical `start`/`end` for inline offsets so positioned dialogs mirror correctly under RTL.

props.name: variant
props.description: Dialog variant: fullscreen expands to fill the entire viewport.

props.name: purpose
props.description: Controls dismissal behavior: required disables Escape and backdrop click; form disables backdrop click after interaction; info allows both.

props.name: padding
props.description: Internal padding of the dialog using the spacing scale step.

props.name: isInline
props.description: Renders dialog content inline without the <dialog> element, backdrop, or modal behavior. For documentation previews and showcases only.

bestPractices.text: Don't add your own focus return or try to turn it off. When the dialog closes, focus goes back to the opener, or to the nearest control that stands in for it (a dialog opened from a menu row returns focus to the menu's trigger), never to the page. To send focus somewhere specific, focus that element after the dialog has closed: in an effect that runs once isOpen is false. The page outside an open dialog is inert, so a focus call in onOpenChange does nothing.
Choose the right purpose: info for dismissable content, form to prevent accidental backdrop dismissal, required when the user must respond.
Include a clear title in the header so users immediately understand what the dialog is asking.
Use purpose="form" for dialogs with inputs so the user can't accidentally lose data by clicking the backdrop.
Keep dialogs focused on a single task; if the content grows beyond what fits, consider a full page instead.
Use a dialog for simple messages that could be shown inline or as a toast notification.

Nest dialogs inside other dialogs; restructure the flow into steps within a single dialog instead. The one exception is an AlertDialog that confirms a destructive action: it asks one question, and Escape closes only the alert.
Use the fullscreen variant for simple confirmations; it is meant for complex content like editors or long forms.

anatomy.name: Header
anatomy.description: Title, optional subtitle, and close button. The title receives focus on open and labels the dialog via aria-labelledby.

anatomy.name: Body
anatomy.description: The main content area: text, forms, lists, or any layout.

anatomy.name: Footer
anatomy.description: Action buttons like Save/Cancel or Accept/Decline, aligned to the end.

anatomy.name: Backdrop
anatomy.description: Semi-transparent overlay behind the dialog that blocks page interaction.

components.name: DialogHeader
components.description: Use DialogHeader to give a dialog a labelled title area and optional close control.

props.name: title
props.description: Dialog title, rendered inside the focusable h2 (receives focus on open; its text content labels the dialog via aria-labelledby unless the Dialog has an explicit aria-label/aria-labelledby). Keep it inline, non-interactive, and non-empty.

props.name: subtitle
props.description: Subtitle below the title. Accepts inline content such as a Link; avoid block elements.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Close button callback (no button if omitted).

props.name: startContent
props.description: Content before the title (e.g., a back button).

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content after the title, before close button.

props.name: endContentEdgeCompensation
props.description: Selects compensation axes for the end-content slot. Omit to preserve automatic close-action compensation.

props.name: hasDivider
props.description: Adds border at the bottom edge.

anatomy.name: Header row
anatomy.description: Arranges the title block, optional start/end content, and close control.

anatomy.name: Start content
anatomy.description: Wraps optional leading content.

anatomy.name: Title block
anatomy.description: Groups the title and optional subtitle.

anatomy.name: End content
anatomy.description: Groups optional trailing content with the optional close control.

anatomy.name: Close icon
anatomy.description: Visual close glyph inside the close button.

components.name: Divider
components.description: A visual separator that divides content into distinct sections. Use to create clear boundaries between groups of related content, or to demarcate interactive regions within a layout.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Orientation of the divider.

props.name: label
props.description: Optional label centered on the divider. Numeric zero is preserved; null, booleans, and empty strings render no label.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual weight of the divider line.

props.name: isFullBleed
props.description: Extend the divider to container edges with negative margins.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

bestPractices.text: Use subtle dividers between related content sections and strong dividers for high-contrast boundaries.
Add a label to the divider when sections need a visible category heading.
Overuse dividers; rely on spacing and layout to separate content when possible.

anatomy.name: Divider group
anatomy.description: Separator group that arranges one or two rules around an optional label.

anatomy.name: Rule
anatomy.description: Painted line segment; a second segment renders when a label is present.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Optional content displayed between two rule segments.

components.name: Drawer
components.description: A side panel that floats above page content for inspectors and detail views: the "click a table row, see its details" pattern. Unlike a docked panel it overlays the layout instead of reflowing it. Works on desktop and touch: the width budget applies on desktop and the panel preserves a 56px page reveal below 640px without exceeding the width budget. Escape closes the drawer (unless purpose is required) and focus returns to the element that opened it. Entry/exit slide animation respects prefers-reduced-motion. On a phone or tablet (a coarse primary pointer), a tap or a drag that lands while the drawer is still sliding in reaches nothing (for a drawer without a scrim, only one on the panel: the page stays live), and the drawer finishes sliding in; keys and assistive technology stay live, and a mouse or a trackpad still clicks: at once when it was the last pointer used, otherwise once it moves. Stacking contract: sibling drawers stack last-opened on top, Escape closes only the topmost, and closing peels innermost-first; render them as siblings, never nested. Like Dialog, the drawer is a container: its content area is inset by --spacing-4 (16px) by default, by the padding prop, or by a theme's padding on drawer. Compose the header, body, and footer the way Dialog does, with a Layout: DrawerHeader in the header slot (it shows a close button when you pass it onOpenChange, like DialogHeader), the body in LayoutContent, and actions in LayoutFooter. The Layout redistributes the inset to those regions so they line up on one content line, and the header is not inset twice. A lone Section child also escapes the inset. Drawer renders no close button of its own, so give every drawer a visible way to close, especially a non-modal one, which has no scrim to click. Put data-autofocus on the control that should receive focus on open. Choosing a surface: use Dialog for a centered decision or short form, Drawer for full-height side detail that keeps the page in sight, BottomSheet for block-axis sheets on touch, and a docked panel (a layout column) when content should reflow the page instead of floating over it. Theming: the panel is the single stable target (astryx-drawer, with data-side reflecting side), and the scrim is the panel's native ::backdrop. DrawerHeader exposes astryx-drawer-header targets for its row, slots, and close icon.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Whether the drawer is open. Fully controlled; pair with onOpenChange.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the drawer requests an open-state change. Escape and a scrim click call it with false as purpose allows; a DrawerHeader given the same callback calls it from its close button. The caller owns the open state. With sibling drawers open, Escape only closes the last-opened one.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the drawer. Required; the drawer has no built-in heading to derive a name from.

props.name: children
props.description: Drawer content, rendered inside a full-height scrollable area. Compose your own header/body/footer; an element with data-autofocus is focused on open. Children stay mounted during the exit animation; keep the last-selected item rendered instead of nulling content on close.

props.name: side
props.description: Edge the drawer slides from: 'end' is right in LTR (the inspector convention), 'start' is left. Inline axis only; for a bottom sheet use BottomSheet.

props.name: width
props.description: Desktop width budget. A number is pixels; a string is any CSS length ('50%', '32rem'). Below the 640px mobile breakpoint this remains the maximum while the drawer preserves a 56px reveal of the page behind.

props.name: experimental
props.description: Experimental options: anything in this object may change or be removed in a patch release, and omitting it keeps the stable behavior. isFullWidthOnMobile (default false) covers the full viewport width below the 640px mobile breakpoint instead of preserving the default 56px reveal of the page behind, which makes the drawer read as an overlay, not a navigation.

props.name: hasScrim
props.description: Modal scrim behind the drawer. true uses showModal() (top layer, focus trap, scroll lock; clicking the scrim closes unless purpose prevents it; modal only); false uses the manual Popover API for a non-modal top-layer overlay that does NOT trap focus and keeps the page behind interactive.

props.name: purpose
props.description: Configures implicit dismissal, matching Dialog. info: Escape and a scrim click close. form: Escape closes, a scrim click does not. required: neither closes (Escape is consumed) and a modal drawer is exposed as an alertdialog, so give its content a way out. A non-modal drawer has no scrim, so form and info behave the same.

props.name: padding
props.description: Internal padding of the drawer content using the spacing scale, matching Dialog. When omitted, uses the theme default for drawers: --spacing-4 (16px) unless the theme sets padding on drawer. Pass 0 for a full-bleed content area. A lone Section child escapes the padding, bleed children such as Table and Divider compensate against it, and a Layout picks it up for its regions. The content area's block-end edge adds the home-indicator safe area on top in every mode.

bestPractices.text: Use for contextual detail views (row inspectors, entity details) where the user should keep the underlying list in sight.
Keep the caller as the source of truth: derive isOpen from selection state and clear the selection in onOpenChange.
Use hasScrim={false} for master-detail flows; non-modal drawers do not trap focus and the page behind stays interactive.
Keep the last-selected item rendered on close: children stay mounted during the exit animation, so nulling content mid-close blanks the panel while it slides out.
Give every drawer a visible close action, usually DrawerHeader with onOpenChange; a non-modal drawer has no scrim to click.
Use purpose="form" when a stray scrim click would discard unsaved input.
Use a Drawer for short confirmations or small forms; use Dialog or AlertDialog instead.
Reach for a Drawer when the content should push the page aside; a Drawer floats over content, so use a docked panel or layout column instead.
Use a Drawer as a bottom or top sheet; it is inline-axis only, so use BottomSheet for block-axis sheets.
Nest a Drawer inside another Drawer; render drawers as siblings; the last-opened stacks on top and Escape closes it first.

anatomy.name: Panel
anatomy.description: The root <dialog> element: a full-height surface anchored to the inline start or end edge, flush with three viewport edges (square corners).

anatomy.name: Content area
anatomy.description: Scrollable container that receives children; compose the header, body, and footer inside it with a Layout, as in Dialog. Inset by --spacing-4 (16px) by default; the padding prop or a theme sets a different container inset.

anatomy.name: Header
anatomy.description: DrawerHeader, composed in a Layout header slot as DialogHeader is in Dialog: a title row with optional subtitle and start/end content. Pass it onOpenChange to show a close button, as with DialogHeader.

anatomy.name: Scrim
anatomy.description: Backdrop that dims and blocks the page behind a modal drawer (hasScrim, the default); a non-modal drawer renders none.

components.name: DrawerHeader
components.description: Compose DrawerHeader in the header slot of a Layout inside the Drawer, as DialogHeader is composed in Dialog, for a title row and, when you pass onOpenChange, a close button.
