The Layout keeps the header on the drawer inset instead of padding it twice. Drawer renders no close button of its own. Unlike DialogHeader it does not take focus on open (Drawer uses data-autofocus) and does not name the drawer (Drawer label does).

props.name: title
props.description: Drawer title, rendered as an h2. Keep it inline and non-interactive. It does not name the drawer; pass Drawer a label.

props.name: subtitle
props.description: Subtitle below the title. Accepts inline content such as a Link; avoid block elements.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Close button callback, called with false (no button if omitted). Pass the Drawer's own onOpenChange.

props.name: startContent
props.description: Content before the title (e.g., a back button).

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content after the title, before the close button.

props.name: endContentEdgeCompensation
props.description: Selects compensation axes for the end-content slot. Omit to preserve automatic close-action compensation.

props.name: hasDivider
props.description: Adds a border at the bottom edge. Defaults to the parent Layout's defaultHasDividers.

anatomy.name: Header row
anatomy.description: Arranges the title block, optional start/end content, and close control.

anatomy.name: Start content
anatomy.description: Wraps optional leading content.

anatomy.name: Title block
anatomy.description: Groups the title and optional subtitle.

anatomy.name: End content
anatomy.description: Groups optional trailing content with the optional close control.

anatomy.name: Close icon
anatomy.description: Visual close glyph inside the close button.

components.name: DropdownMenu
components.description: A dropdown menu that displays a list of actionable items in a popup triggered by a button. Use to present action options as a next step in a process, or to offer contextual actions without cluttering the interface. Like the menus of macOS and iOS, the row under the pointer when it is released is the row that acts, the highlight follows a held mouse or finger, a mouse opens it on press and can drag straight into it, and a finger held on the trigger opens it with the finger down.

props.name: button
props.description: Props for the trigger button (Button props except onClick). Mutually exclusive with `renderTrigger`.

props.name: renderTrigger
props.description: Render the control the menu hangs off — an IconButton, a chip, an avatar, a list row — instead of the built-in Button. Spread the given props onto it: they carry the press model (a mouse opens on press-down, a finger or a pen opens as it presses), the keyboard opens, the toggle click, and `aria-haspopup`/`aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`/`id`; the menu is then named by that control through `aria-labelledby`. Mutually exclusive with `button`.

props.name: items
props.description: Array of menu entries. Each entry is one of: an action item `{label, onClick?, href?, target?, rel?, icon?, description?, endContent?, isDisabled?, variant?, hasCloseOnSelect?, id?}` (`href` makes the row a real link, so a modified click keeps the browser's meaning; variant `"destructive"` renders it in the error color; `endContent` holds trailing content such as a keyboard-shortcut hint; `id` is the row's stable React key, needed only when the array reorders or filters), a divider `{type: "divider"}`, or a section `{type: "section", title?, id?, items: [...action items]}`.

props.name: presentation
props.description: Presentation surface for data-driven items. 'popover' stays anchored, 'bottom-sheet' always renders the actions in a modal BottomSheet, and 'adaptive' uses a BottomSheet on compact coarse-pointer layouts while remaining anchored elsewhere. Compound children currently support popover only. Omitted, the menu is anchored, and under a finger or a pen, on every device, its trigger opens as it is pressed (inside a scroll view, after the 150 ms content-touch delay), and the opening finger picks after moving 10 px. Pass 'popover' to keep the pointer behavior on every device, a 500 ms hold included.

props.name: isMenuOpen
props.description: Controlled open state for the menu. Mounting with true renders the menu open without moving focus into it; focus moves to the first item only when the menu opens after mount.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback fired when the open state changes.

props.name: menuWidth
props.description: Minimum width for the popover presentation. Length values may grow for content; intrinsic and CSS-wide keywords select the preferred inline size. Every form is capped to the available viewport space. Defaults to matching the trigger width up to that cap.

props.name: menuMaxHeight
props.description: Maximum height in pixels for the popover presentation, for a menu that must fit its rows. Lifts the default 300px cap; the viewport still bounds it.

props.name: header
props.description: Content above the rows and outside the menu itself — a filter field, a toggle. A menu holds only its rows, so a control that is not a row goes here or in `footer`, never among the rows. It keeps its own keys and presses. With a header or footer the popover is a modal dialog around the menu: Tab and Shift+Tab move through the header, the menu and the footer and wrap at either end, and Escape closes. The bottom sheet shows it above the actions.

props.name: footer
props.description: Content below the rows and outside the menu itself — a "Create" button. Tab from the menu moves into it, and Tab past its last control wraps to the start of the dialog (see `header`). The bottom sheet shows it below the actions.

props.name: placement
props.description: Popover placement relative to the trigger. Ignored by the bottom-sheet presentation. Logical: start/end resolve against the menu's own inherited direction (RTL mirrors).

props.name: alignment
props.description: Popover alignment along the placement axis. Ignored by the bottom-sheet presentation. Logical: start/end follow the menu's own inherited direction (RTL mirrors).

props.name: onClick
props.description: Callback fired for accepted trigger activation. The trailing click from the same press that light-dismissed the menu is ignored.

props.name: hasChevron
props.description: Whether to show a chevron icon on the trigger button. Set to false for icon-only triggers.

props.name: children
props.description: Compound-mode menu content: DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuDivider, DropdownMenuSubMenu (a flyout on a laptop, a drilled-in view with a Back row on a phone), and the selectable items. Mutually exclusive with `items`.

bestPractices.text: Keep menu items concise and action-oriented so users can scan options quickly.

Let the menu return focus on close: to its trigger, or to a stand-in when the trigger is gone (a BottomSheet presentation keeps the sheet return). There is no option to turn this off; to send focus elsewhere, focus that element in onOpenChange.
Use sections and dividers to group related actions when the menu has many items.
For a short, flat action set, use presentation="bottom-sheet" when product policy calls for a modal touch surface.
Use presentation="adaptive" when the same short action set should remain anchored on pointer layouts and become a BottomSheet on compact coarse-pointer layouts.
For a hierarchy that cannot fit as adjacent flyouts on a compact touch surface, a product may explicitly use a drill-in interaction with a Back action.
Choose presentation explicitly in product code. A compact, coarse-pointer, hover-free media query is one useful policy, but DropdownMenu does not impose a universal device breakpoint.
When the content is no longer a short list of immediate actions, reevaluate the interaction and choose a component that matches the actual task; content traits alone do not determine the component.
Use a DropdownMenu for navigation; use a navigation component instead.
Place more than 10–12 items in a single menu without grouping them into sections.

anatomy.name: Trigger button
anatomy.description: Button that opens and closes the selected menu presentation.

anatomy.name: Trigger indicator icon
anatomy.description: Optional trailing chevron shown by a labeled trigger when hasChevron is enabled.

anatomy.name: Pointer menu surface
anatomy.description: Anchored top-level or nested menu panel used by the pointer presentation.

anatomy.name: Pointer action row
anatomy.description: Action, selectable option, or submenu trigger row in an anchored menu.

anatomy.name: Icon-rendered item icon
anatomy.description: Optional built-in meaning or icon component rendered through Icon at the start of an action row.

anatomy.name: Caller-rendered item start content
anatomy.description: Optional arbitrary React content rendered directly at the start of an action row.

anatomy.name: Checkbox indicator
anatomy.description: Decorative shared checkbox indicator for a checkbox action row.

anatomy.name: Radio indicator
anatomy.description: Decorative shared radio indicator with an additional menu-owned target.

anatomy.name: Pointer section heading
anatomy.description: Heading that labels a group of rows in an anchored menu: a data-driven section or a compound DropdownMenuGroup.

anatomy.name: Pointer divider
anatomy.description: Divider between groups in an anchored menu.

components.name: DropdownMenuCheckboxItem
components.description: An independently checkable option inside DropdownMenu. The row owns menuitemcheckbox semantics while the shared Indicator supplies decorative checkbox paint.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary label text identifying the item.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary description text displayed below the label.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon to display before the label; pass a built-in meaning such as 'search' (see `astryx docs icons`), an icon component, or an icon element.

props.name: value
props.description: Whether the item is checked. Controlled; pair with onChange.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired with the next checked state when the item is toggled.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the item is disabled. A disabled item stays in the accessibility tree as disabled (aria-disabled), and the arrow keys and typeahead reach it so keyboard users find it. The pointer highlight skips it, and activation is blocked.

props.name: hasCloseOnSelect
props.description: Whether toggling the item closes the menu. Checkbox items default to staying open so several can be toggled in a single session.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the row root, the element carrying role="menuitemcheckbox". Register the row with an element-keyed observer or overlay.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content to render after the label and description, such as a keyboard shortcut hint or badge.

anatomy.name: Checkable row
anatomy.description: The menuitemcheckbox root that owns the accessible name, checked state, focus, and activation.

anatomy.name: Label/content
anatomy.description: Caller content laid out by Item: the required label plus optional description, icon, and end content.

anatomy.name: Checkbox marker
anatomy.description: Decorative shared Indicator chrome that visualizes checked and disabled state without adding a second control.

components.name: DropdownMenuDivider
components.description: A horizontal rule separating groups of rows in a compound menu. Renders role="separator", so it is never a stop in the arrow-key order. The data-driven equivalent is the `{type: "divider"}` entry in `items`; both modes render this component, so they look and theme identically. Host attributes and DOM handlers (id, data-*, aria-*) reach the separator; its role and orientation stay component-owned.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles applied after the menu spacing. Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

components.name: DropdownMenuGroup
components.description: Use DropdownMenuGroup to give related compound-menu rows one visible and programmatic name. Use an untitled group only when a separate name would not help people understand the rows.

props.name: title
props.description: Non-interactive heading content shown above the rows and used as the group's accessible name. Omit for an unnamed group; place controls in DropdownMenu header or footer.

props.name: children
props.description: The grouped rows: DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuCheckboxItem, DropdownMenuRadioGroup, or DropdownMenuSubMenu.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles applied to the role="group" wrapper. Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name applied to the role="group" wrapper.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles applied to the role="group" wrapper.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the role="group" wrapper.

bestPractices.text: Use short, descriptive title content that explains what the grouped rows have in common.
Keep the title non-interactive so every available action remains in the menu arrow-key order.
Place buttons, links, fields, or other controls in title. Put them in DropdownMenu header or footer instead.
Wrap rows that do not form a meaningful set; a group adds structure only when its relationship helps users.

anatomy.name: Group
anatomy.description: The role="group" wrapper containing the heading and menu rows.

anatomy.name: Heading
anatomy.description: Visible non-interactive title content that names the group and carries the dropdown-menu-section-heading theme target.

anatomy.name: Rows
anatomy.description: Menu items, selectable items, radio groups, or submenus owned by DropdownMenu.

components.name: DropdownMenuItem
components.description: Use DropdownMenuItem inside DropdownMenu compound mode for one action or destination. Keep label, description, icon, and endContent non-interactive; controls belong in separate rows or the menu header/footer.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon to display before the label; pass a built-in meaning such as 'search' (see `astryx docs icons`), an icon component, or an icon element.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary label text.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary description text displayed below the label.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Callback when the item is selected. A keyboard activation arrives as a synthesized click carrying the key's modifiers. On a row with `href` it runs before the browser navigates and is skipped for a modified click (⌘, Ctrl, Shift, Alt, middle button), which is left to the browser.

props.name: href
props.description: Address the row navigates to. The row then renders as a real anchor with role="menuitem" (through LinkProvider), so a modified click or a middle click keeps the browser's meaning — a new tab — instead of running onClick.

props.name: target
props.description: Link target. Only used with href.

props.name: rel
props.description: Link relationship. noopener noreferrer is added for target="_blank". Only used with href.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the row is unavailable. Disabled rows expose aria-disabled, remove link destinations, and suppress activation.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Non-interactive content rendered after the label and description.

props.name: hasCloseOnSelect
props.description: Whether activating the item closes the menu. Set false for an action that reports its result on the item itself.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual variant. 'destructive' renders the label, description, and icon in the error color for dangerous actions (e.g. Delete).

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the row root, the element carrying role="menuitem". Register the row with an element-keyed observer or overlay.

bestPractices.text: Use href for a destination so LinkProvider, modified clicks, middle clicks, and browser link affordances remain available.
Use hasCloseOnSelect=false only when activation reports a result in place on the same row.
Put buttons, links, or other focusable controls inside label, description, or endContent. Each menu row is one interactive target.

anatomy.name: Row
anatomy.description: The role="menuitem" root that owns activation, disabled state, destination behavior, and theme state.

anatomy.name: Content
anatomy.description: The non-interactive label plus optional icon, description, and end content.

components.name: DropdownMenuRadioGroup
components.description: Use DropdownMenuRadioGroup inside compound-mode DropdownMenu when several commands represent one mutually exclusive choice. Keep value in caller state, provide a concise accessible label, and render each choice as DropdownMenuRadioItem.

props.name: value
props.description: The currently selected value in the group. Pass undefined when nothing is selected yet.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the selected value changes.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the group, applied as aria-label so screen readers announce the radios as a named set, e.g. "Sort by". Required even when aria-labelledby (via base props) points to visible text; that visible reference becomes the computed name while label remains the fallback.

props.name: hasCloseOnSelect
props.description: Whether selecting a value closes the menu. Radio items default to closing on selection (a single-choice commit).

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the role="group" root.

props.name: children
props.description: The DropdownMenuRadioItems that make up the group.

bestPractices.text: Keep value controlled and update it from onChange so checked state follows caller data.
Provide a concise label even when aria-labelledby points to visible text; label remains required and supplies the aria-label fallback.
Set hasCloseOnSelect=false only when the menu must stay open to show another selection or an in-place result.
Place buttons, links, checkboxes, or arbitrary menu rows inside the radio group.
Add a second key handler or roving-focus model; DropdownMenu owns keyboard navigation.

anatomy.name: Group
anatomy.description: The role="group" root that owns the accessible name, controlled-selection context, close policy, root inputs, and inter-item gap.

anatomy.name: Radio items
anatomy.description: DropdownMenuRadioItem children; each child owns its menuitemradio role, checked state, content, and indicator paint.

components.name: DropdownMenuRadioItem
components.description: A single option in a DropdownMenuRadioGroup (role="menuitemradio"). Must be used inside a DropdownMenuRadioGroup.

props.name: value
props.description: The value this item represents within its group. The group's value matches against this to determine the checked state.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary label text identifying the option.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary description text displayed below the label.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon to display before the label; pass a built-in meaning such as 'search' (see `astryx docs icons`), an icon component, or an icon element.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether this individual radio item is disabled. A disabled item stays in the accessibility tree as disabled (aria-disabled), and the arrow keys and typeahead reach it so keyboard users find it. The pointer highlight skips it, and selection is blocked.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content to render after the label and description, such as a badge or metadata.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the row root, the element carrying role="menuitemradio". Register the row with an element-keyed observer or overlay.

components.name: DropdownMenuSubMenu
components.description: A single menu row that reveals a nested flyout of its own items. The row adopts DropdownMenuItem semantics (label / icon / description / isDisabled); its children become the flyout content. Opens inline-end with viewport auto-flip; Right/Enter/Space opens and focuses the first item, Left/Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger (Right/Left swap in RTL). On a phone (a coarse pointer, decided when the menu opened) the row drills in instead: its rows replace the menu's rows in the same box, led by a Back row named "Back to <parent>", and Back, Escape or ArrowLeft return to the row. Host attributes and DOM event handlers (aria-*, data-*, id) reach the trigger row, the element carrying role="menuitem" and aria-haspopup="menu"; a caller's handlers run after the row's own, except for the keys that open the flyout (the open arrow, Enter, Space) and a click on a disabled row. For data-driven menus, give a menu item a nested `items` array instead of using this component directly.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary label text for the trigger row.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon to display before the label; pass a built-in meaning such as 'search' (see `astryx docs icons`), an icon component, or an icon element.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary description text displayed below the label.

props.name: children
props.description: The flyout menu items: the same components used at the top level (DropdownMenuItem, nested DropdownMenuSubMenu, selectable items).

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: A disabled submenu renders its trigger row but never opens the flyout.

props.name: hasSpinner
props.description: Show a spinner in place of the caret, e.g. while a lazy submenu's children are loading.

props.name: menuWidth
props.description: Minimum flyout width. The flyout may grow for its content, but it is capped to the available viewport space. Defaults to intrinsic sizing (min 160px).

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the flyout opens or closes.

props.name: presentation
props.description: How the sub-menu shows its rows. 'flyout' opens them beside the row; 'drill-in' replaces the menu's rows with them and a Back row, in the same box; 'adaptive' drills in when a finger opened the menu (a coarse pointer, decided when the menu opened) and flies out otherwise.

props.name: delay
props.description: How long a hovering pointer waits before the flyout opens, in milliseconds. Keyboard focus and touch never wait.

props.name: hideDelay
props.description: How long the flyout stays open after the pointer leaves, in milliseconds.

props.name: header
props.description: Content above the sub-menu's rows and outside its menu, a field that filters them, say. It keeps its own keys and presses. With a header or footer the sub-menu's surface (the flyout, or the drilled-in view on a phone) is a modal dialog named by the row, beside the menu rather than inside it: the row says aria-haspopup="dialog", Tab and Shift+Tab move through the header, the rows and the footer and wrap, Escape returns to the row, and a pointer leaving the flyout closes it only once focus leaves too. A ContextMenu does not show it.

props.name: footer
props.description: Content below the sub-menu's rows and outside its menu, a door to where the options are managed, say. Same rules as header.

props.name: menuDataTestId
props.description: Test id for the sub-menu's own role="menu" element: the flyout, or the drilled-in list on a phone. The trigger row takes data-testid.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the trigger row. Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the trigger row, the element carrying role="menuitem" and aria-haspopup="menu" ("dialog" with a header or footer).

components.name: EmptyState
components.description: EmptyState shows a placeholder when a content area has no data. Use it for empty lists, zero search results, first-time setups, or cleared inboxes. Always include a title and a next step so the user is not stuck.

props.name: title
props.description: Primary message rendered as the configured heading level inside the empty state.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional secondary text providing additional context below the title.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon or illustration displayed above the title; rendered as decorative (aria-hidden="true").

props.name: actions
props.description: Optional action buttons displayed below the description, laid out horizontally by default and stacked vertically when isCompact is true.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Controls only the rendered HTML heading tag (h1-h6) so the title fits the document outline. This is a semantic change for accessibility and does not change the visual size of the title, which stays fixed regardless of level.

props.name: isCompact
props.description: Enables the compact variant with reduced spacing for constrained content areas.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

bestPractices.text: Include a clear title and a call-to-action button so users know how to proceed.
Use an illustration or icon that reinforces the context of the empty state.
Use the compact variant inside cards or sidebars where space is limited.
Leave an empty state without guidance; always explain what happened and what the user can do next.
Use a generic message like "No data"; be specific about what is empty and why.
Use an EmptyState for error messages that require immediate action; use a Banner instead.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: The centered root that owns spacing, reading order, and the compact layout variant.

anatomy.name: Icon
anatomy.description: A visual cue above the title that reinforces the context, like a search icon for no results.

anatomy.name: Title
anatomy.description: Primary message explaining what is empty: "No projects yet" not "No data".

anatomy.name: Description
anatomy.description: Additional context explaining why it is empty or what the user can do.

anatomy.name: Actions
anatomy.description: One or two buttons guiding the user to a next step, like "Create project" or "Clear filters".

components.name: Field
components.description: Field is a low-level wrapper for custom, native, or third-party controls that do not already provide field label, description, and status UI. Use it when you need the Field shell around a control you own; use styled Astryx inputs like TextInput, Typeahead, and Select directly when they already expose label, description, and validation props.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the field (always rendered for accessibility).

props.name: inputID
props.description: ID for the input element (used for the label htmlFor attribute).

props.name: labelID
props.description: ID applied to the label element itself for group accessibility.

props.name: isGroupLabel
props.description: Renders the label as a span for control groups (radiogroup, checkbox list).

props.name: children
props.description: The input or control to render.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hide the label (still accessible to screen readers).

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the associated input is disabled. Propagates disabled styling to the label.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed between the label and input.

props.name: descriptionID
props.description: ID for the description element (use for aria-describedby on the input).

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Whether the field is optional (mutually exclusive with isRequired).

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Whether the field is required (mutually exclusive with isOptional).

props.name: labelIcon
props.description: Icon to display before the label text; pass a built-in meaning such as 'search' (see `astryx docs icons`), an icon component, or an icon element.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Help text for an info button after the label, named "About {label}". Hover and keyboard focus preview it; a tap, click, Enter, or Space opens it and never focuses or toggles the control.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator with type and optional message. When message is set, displays a colored status box. messageID is for wiring aria-describedby on the input.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How status feedback is placed. Attached overlaps an eligible opaque, bordered, fixed-height control; detached renders a message below custom or non-bordered controls; tooltip leaves the visible affordance to the wrapped input and announces its message without a FieldStatus box.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned. Prefer this over setting width via xstyle/className/style, which only size the inner control box. Without a width, a row can shrink the whole field below the natural width of its control, so filter bars shrink instead of overflowing.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the root element.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name(s) appended to the root element. Prefer xstyle for StyleX deduplication.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles applied to the root element. Takes priority over StyleX inline styles.

bestPractices.text: Wrap custom controls, native inputs, or third-party widgets that need labeling, helper text, optional/required indicators, or validation status.
Always provide a label for accessibility, even if visually hidden with isLabelHidden.
Use inputID and descriptionID to connect the label and description to the inner control with htmlFor and aria-describedby.
Nest Field around styled inputs such as TextInput, Typeahead, Select, DateInput, or TextArea; those components already render their own Field shell.
Use attached status only when the wrapped control is opaque, bordered, and fixed-height; use detached for custom, tall, translucent, or non-bordered controls.
Set both isOptional and isRequired on the same field.
Hide the label without providing an alternative way for the user to understand the field purpose.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: Root field box that owns layout, width, and local stacking for the label, control, and status.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Text identifying the field. Always rendered for accessibility, optionally hidden visually.

anatomy.name: Ordinary description
anatomy.description: Helper text under the label in the ordinary field layout.

anatomy.name: Horizontal-label description
anatomy.description: Helper text in the control column when FormLayout owns horizontal labels.

anatomy.name: Control slot
anatomy.description: A custom, native, or third-party control that does not already render a field shell.

anatomy.name: Status message
anatomy.description: Inline validation feedback showing error, warning, or success with a message.

anatomy.name: Input status icon
anatomy.description: Shared status affordance used by Field-composed input controls.

anatomy.name: Input clear button
anatomy.description: Shared clear action used by Field-composed input controls.

anatomy.name: Input clear icon
anatomy.description: Glyph inside the shared input clear action.

anatomy.name: Optional/Required indicator
anatomy.description: Badge next to the label showing whether the field is optional or required.

components.name: FieldLabel
components.description: Standalone label group for one control or a caller-labelled group, with optional supporting text, optionality indicators, icon, and tooltip.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text, always rendered for accessibility.

props.name: inputID
props.description: ID of the input this label is for.

props.name: labelID
props.description: ID applied to the label element itself. Use it with `aria-labelledby` when `isGroupLabel` is true.

props.name: isGroupLabel
props.description: Render a span that can name a group instead of a native label for one control.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hide the label and description while keeping both available to assistive technology.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Use disabled label presentation for the associated control.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Show the localized optional indicator unless it matches FormLayout's default optionality.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Show the localized required indicator unless it matches FormLayout's default optionality.

props.name: labelIcon
props.description: Icon before the label text; pass a built-in meaning such as 'search' (see `astryx docs icons`), an icon component, or an icon element.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Help text for an info button after the label, named "About {label}". Hover and keyboard focus preview it; a tap, click, Enter, or Space opens it and never focuses or toggles the control.

props.name: description
props.description: Supporting content displayed below the label and kept separate from the control's accessible name.

props.name: descriptionID
props.description: ID applied to the supporting description for caller-owned `aria-describedby` wiring.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the label element. Group mode currently renders a span.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles applied to the label element after its base and state styles.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name appended to the label element.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles applied to the label element after StyleX inline styles.

components.name: FieldStatus
components.description: FieldStatus renders validation feedback for fields and field-like controls. Use it directly for custom controls that need the same error, warning, or success presentation as Field.

props.name: type
props.description: Status type.

props.name: message
props.description: Status message text.

props.name: id
props.description: ID for aria-describedby association.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual variant: attached overlaps the input, detached floats below.

bestPractices.text: Use attached status below bordered inputs when the message belongs to that input.
Use detached status for controls like checkboxes, switches, and custom controls where overlap would be visually awkward.
Use FieldStatus for general alerts or page-level notices; use Banner or Toast instead.

A field's status is announced when it first appears and when its message or type changes, not again when a repeated submit fails with the same errors. On such a repeated submit, with the errors unchanged, announce it once from the form with useAnnounce, for example announce(`${errors.length} errors. ${errors[0]}`, 'assertive'), and move focus to the first invalid field. On a first failed submit the fields announce their own errors, so the form adds no announcement.

anatomy.name: Message box
anatomy.description: Painted container for the validation feedback.

anatomy.name: Detached icon
anatomy.description: Leading status glyph shown only by the detached variant.

anatomy.name: Message text
anatomy.description: Text describing the validation status.

components.name: FileInput
components.description: FileInput provides file upload with optional drag-and-drop support. Use it for single or multiple file selection with built-in validation for file type, size, and count. Pair with validation status for upload feedback.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the file input.

props.name: value
props.description: Currently selected file(s). Controlled component.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when files are selected or removed.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async change action (React 19 transitions pattern). Use for immediate upload on file selection.

props.name: accept
props.description: Accepted file types. Uses the HTML accept attribute format (e.g. "image/*", ".pdf,.doc").

props.name: isMultiple
props.description: Whether multiple files can be selected. When true, value and onChange use File[] instead of File.

props.name: maxSize
props.description: Maximum file size in bytes. Files exceeding this are rejected with an error status.

props.name: maxFiles
props.description: Maximum number of files (only applies when isMultiple is true).

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible to screen readers.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed between the label and input.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Displays an "Optional" indicator next to the label. Mutually exclusive with isRequired.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Displays a "Required" indicator next to the label and adds a screen-reader-only "Required" description to the trigger (assistive tech does not reliably announce aria-required on the trigger). Mutually exclusive with isOptional.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the input, preventing interaction and dimming the element.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the input is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the trigger focusable via aria-disabled (opening the file picker stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled FileInput in Tooltip; disabled controls swallow the hover events an external Tooltip needs.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Puts the input in a loading state, showing a spinner and setting aria-busy.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when no file is selected.

props.name: mode
props.description: Visual mode. 'input' is a compact inline style; 'dropzone' is a larger area with drag-and-drop support.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status: applies a colored border. If message is provided, displays a floating message below the input. Error type also sets aria-invalid.

props.name: statusVariant
props.defaultValue: 'attached' in input mode; 'detached' in dropzone mode
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip hides the message box and surfaces it in a tooltip on the status icon. Dropzone mode does not support attached, so a dropzone defaults to detached; an explicit attached keeps its released rendering until the next minor release, which resolves it to detached.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text displayed in an info icon at the end of the label.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the element that paints the border and background and holds icons and end controls. Never the native input.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Class name for the visual control box.

props.name: controlStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the visual control box.

bestPractices.text: Always specify an accept prop to guide users toward valid file types.
Use maxSize and maxFiles to prevent oversized uploads; the component handles validation and error display automatically.
Add a description to communicate constraints like file size limits or accepted formats.
Use changeAction for immediate upload workflows that benefit from optimistic UI.
Don't use FileInput for directory or folder uploads; that is not supported in v1.
Don't avoid dropzone mode unless space is constrained; drag-and-drop is the expected interaction for file uploads.
Don't wrap a disabled FileInput in Tooltip to explain why it's disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Text that identifies the field. Always rendered for accessibility even when visually hidden.

anatomy.name: Description
anatomy.description: Helper text between the label and the drop zone explaining accepted formats or size limits.

anatomy.name: Drop zone
anatomy.description: The clickable area for file selection. In dropzone mode, also accepts dragged files.

anatomy.name: Upload icon
anatomy.description: An upload-to-tray icon in the drop zone hinting at the upload action.

anatomy.name: Placeholder
anatomy.description: Hint text shown when no files are selected.

anatomy.name: File name display
anatomy.description: Shows the name(s) of selected files.

anatomy.name: Clear button
anatomy.description: A close button that removes selected files and returns focus to the file-selection trigger.

anatomy.name: Spinner
anatomy.description: Loading indicator that appears during async upload actions.

anatomy.name: Status message
anatomy.description: Validation feedback showing error, warning, or success with a message.

components.name: FormLayout
components.description: A layout container that arranges form fields with consistent spacing and direction. FormLayout handles where fields go, not state or submission. Wrap it in a native <form> for that; <form> has no Astryx replacement, so it stays a plain element. Supports vertical (default), horizontal, and horizontal-labels directions, and can be nested to mix them.

props.name: direction
props.description: Controls field arrangement. Vertical stacks top-to-bottom, horizontal uses one fractional grid track per field in logical inline order, and horizontal-labels uses CSS Grid with labels beside inputs on the inline-start side (collapsing to vertical when the viewport is <=480px).

props.name: defaultOptionality
props.description: The state the form treats as its default, so only the exception shows an optional/required indicator. With "optional", only fields marked isRequired show an indicator; with "required", only fields marked isOptional do. A field that restates the default shows nothing. Under "required" the unmarked fields also expose aria-required so screen readers match the visual default; aria-required only, never the native required attribute. CheckboxInput, Switch and CheckboxList are the exception: an unchecked box, an off switch or an empty group is an answer, so they take no required state from the default. A CheckboxInput or Switch is required only through its own isRequired. Leave unset for today's per-field behavior.

props.name: defaultEntryErrorBehavior
props.description: When DateInput, DateTimeInput, TimeInput, and NumberInput fields in the layout show their own entry errors: a date, time, or number the field rejects. It sets when the error shows, not when validation runs, so it is not React Aria's validationBehavior (native versus ARIA validation), and it never changes a caller status. 'complete' shows each error at the field's own moment. 'blur-or-enter' holds the message, aria-invalid, the invalid styling, the announcement, and the onEntryErrorChange report until Enter or blur; an edit that makes the entry valid or empty still clears the error at once. NumberInput shows its errors only at Enter or blur under both values. A field's own entryErrorBehavior wins. A nested FormLayout replaces the default for its fields, and unset there means 'complete'. Content in a layer, such as a Dialog opened from the form, starts without it. Leave unset for 'complete'.

props.name: children
props.description: Form fields to arrange. Accepts Astryx inputs (TextInput, Selector, etc.) and Field-wrapped custom controls.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

bestPractices.text: Stack fields vertically for most forms. It's the easiest to scan top to bottom.
Nest a horizontal FormLayout inside a vertical one when fields naturally pair up, like First Name + Last Name or City + State + ZIP.
Use horizontal-labels for settings pages where labels sit beside their inputs.
Use FormLayout for form state or submission. It's just layout. Wrap it in a native <form> for that.
Put unrelated fields side by side in a horizontal layout. Save it for fields that belong together.
Nest horizontal-labels inside another FormLayout. It uses CSS Grid and needs to be the outermost container.

anatomy.name: Layout container
anatomy.description: Owns field arrangement, spacing, direction, and form-level optionality.

anatomy.name: Form title
anatomy.description: Heading that describes the purpose of the form.

anatomy.name: Fields
anatomy.description: Input components with labels for collecting user data.

anatomy.name: Footer
anatomy.description: Contains confirmation buttons such as Submit or Cancel.

components.name: Grid
components.description: A CSS grid layout container for arranging children in rows and columns. Use Grid for card galleries, dashboards, and any multi-column layout. For columns that reflow on small screens, use `columns={{minWidth, max}}`; a numeric `columns` is exactly N columns at every width and never reflows.

props.name: columns
props.description: Column configuration. A number creates exactly N `1fr` tracks at every width and never reflows (e.g. `columns={3}`); a child's minimum content may widen its track. For columns that reflow on small screens, use `{minWidth, max}`. Use an object for responsive columns: `minWidth` sets the minimum column width in px, `repeat` controls track behavior (`"fill"` preserves empty tracks for consistent widths, `"fit"` collapses empty tracks so items stretch; defaults to `"fill"`), and `max` caps the maximum number of columns.

props.name: width
props.description: Container width. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is.

props.name: height
props.description: Container height. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is.

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: Maximum container width. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is.

props.name: minHeight
props.description: Minimum container height. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is.

props.name: gap
props.description: Spacing between all items.

props.name: rowGap
props.description: Row spacing; overrides `gap` for the row axis.

props.name: columnGap
props.description: Column spacing; overrides `gap` for the column axis.

props.name: rowHeight
props.description: Height of each implicit row track in pixels. Pair with `GridSpan rows={N}` for masonry-style layouts.

props.name: align
props.description: Vertical alignment of items (`align-items`). Unset leaves the browser default, `normal`, which stretches items that have no natural size or aspect ratio.

props.name: justify
props.description: Horizontal alignment of items (`justify-items`). Unset leaves the browser default, `normal`, which stretches items that have no natural size or aspect ratio.

props.name: children
props.description: Grid content.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

bestPractices.text: Default to responsive columns for anything that must survive a phone: `columns={{minWidth: 240, max: 4}}` renders at most 4 columns, each at least 240px, and drops to one full-width column when narrow.
Use `columns={4}` for a row that must work on small screens; a number never reflows and renders four narrow tracks on a phone. Reserve numbers for rows that must stay fixed, such as a 7-day week.
Pair `minWidth` with `max` to cap the count on wide screens. In a container narrower than `minWidth`, one column shrinks to the container width, with or without `max`.

`{minWidth}` alone keeps each column at its track width, and a grid with fewer items than tracks keeps the empty tracks: two items in an 880px grid with `minWidth: 280` leave an empty third column. To let the items grow to fill the row, use `repeat: 'fit'`, or set `max` to no more than the item count.
Use `repeat: 'fill'` (the default) for consistent item widths. Use `'fit'` when items should stretch to fill leftover space.
Write manual CSS grid; Grid handles spacing and responsive behavior for you.
Use `HStack` with wrapping for grids; use Grid instead.
Track templates use CSS-variable indirection (not raw inline styles), so `xstyle` overrides of `gridTemplateColumns` (including inside `@media` queries) take effect.

anatomy.name: Grid container
anatomy.description: Two-dimensional layout container that arranges caller-supplied items in rows and columns.

anatomy.name: Spanning item
anatomy.description: Optional GridSpan wrapper that changes one item's column or row participation.

components.name: GridSpan
components.description: Grid item that spans multiple columns or rows.

props.name: columns
props.description: Columns to span; use `'full'` to span all explicit columns.

props.name: rows
props.description: Rows to span.

props.name: children
props.description: Content.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles applied to the span wrapper. Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name applied to the span wrapper.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles applied to the span wrapper. When `columns` or `rows` is set, its `grid-column` or `grid-row` replaces the same property in `style`.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the span wrapper.

components.name: Heading
components.description: Semantic heading component that renders h1-h6 elements with themed styling, themed sizing via type scale tokens, and line-clamp truncation.

props.name: level
props.description: Heading level. Determines the semantic HTML element (h1-h6) and the visual styling from the theme (unless `type` is set). Pass it on every heading: without a level from 1 to 6, the heading renders as `h2` and warns in development.

props.name: type
props.description: Display type variant. Overrides the visual styling from `level` with display-scale sizing (larger, lighter weight, tighter line-height). Themes may add custom visual types. The `level` still determines the HTML element for accessibility. Use for hero banners, marketing headlines, and data callouts.

props.name: weight
props.description: Explicit font-weight override. Wins over the selected visual type or heading-level default.

props.name: children
props.description: Heading content.

props.name: accessibilityLevel
props.description: Accessibility level override. When set and different from `level`, applies `aria-level` so the document outline differs from the visual style.

props.name: color
props.description: Text color. Themes may add custom colors.

props.name: display
props.description: Display type. Silently overridden to 'block' when maxLines > 0 or hasCapsize is true.

props.name: maxLines
props.description: Maximum lines before truncation. 0 means no truncation. When set, shows a tooltip on hover if content is truncated.

props.name: hasTruncateTooltip
props.description: Controls tooltip behavior for truncated text. true shows the tooltip at the default position, false disables it, or a placement string ('above' | 'below' | 'start' | 'end') sets a specific position.

props.name: wordBreak
props.description: Word break behavior when truncating. Defaults to 'break-all' for single-line truncation, 'break-word' otherwise. Without truncation, a token longer than its line (a URL, an ID) wraps (`overflow-wrap: break-word`), so in ordinary flow text does not make the page scroll sideways. Inside a flex row, give the flex child `min-width: 0` so it can shrink. A container you style with `overflow-wrap: anywhere` does not reach this text; Astryx's own containers pass their wrap through.

props.name: textWrap
props.description: Text wrapping behavior.

props.name: justify
props.description: Text alignment (justification). Uses logical values (start/end) for i18n/RTL compatibility.

props.name: hasCapsize
props.description: Enable optical alignment using text-box-trim. Forces block display.

props.name: hasStrikethrough
props.description: Apply strikethrough text decoration.

props.name: id
props.description: HTML id attribute.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles applied to the heading element. Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name applied to the heading element.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles applied to the heading element. When `maxLines` is above 1, its line clamp replaces any `WebkitLineClamp` in `style`.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the heading element.

components.name: HoverCard
components.description: HoverCard shows additional information when the user hovers or focuses a trigger element. Use it for profile cards, link summaries, or inline definitions where the user needs more context without navigating away.

bestPractices.text: Keep content supplementary; hover cards should enhance understanding without blocking the primary workflow.
Provide a dashed underline on text triggers so users know the element is hoverable.
Use the hook API (useHoverCard) when you need more control over timing or placement.
Leave touchTrigger on auto so a tap opens the card on triggers that do nothing else, and stays out of the way on triggers that perform an action.
Place critical actions or required information inside a hover card; users may miss content that only appears on hover.
Use a hover card when a simple Tooltip or Popover would suffice.
Use a HoverCard for content the user must interact with; it disappears when the cursor leaves.

Put the trigger inside SVG <foreignObject>. In Chromium it cannot be a CSS anchor, so the card opens at the viewport corner. Render the trigger in an HTML layer positioned over the SVG node instead, and keep the SVG for shapes, edges and labels.

Prefer placing HoverCard in a block context rather than directly in a

, heading, or link. Those placements are supported when necessary through a corrective portal, but the DOM and tab order may differ.

anatomy.name: Trigger
anatomy.description: The element that opens the hover card on hover or focus: a button, link, or inline text.

anatomy.name: Card
anatomy.description: The floating overlay with the preview content, anchored to the trigger.

anatomy.name: Body
anatomy.description: The main content area: profile info, link summary, or any rich content.

anatomy.name: Actions
anatomy.description: Optional buttons inside the card for follow-up actions like Follow or Message.

components.name: Icon
components.description: Icons are small visual symbols that represent actions, objects, or concepts. They improve scannability and reinforce meaning alongside text. Supports both direct SVG components and built-in meanings that adapt to the active theme.

props.name: icon
props.description: Built-in meaning, or any SVG component from your icon library (`icon={TrashIcon}`). Built-in meanings: close, chevronDown, chevronLeft, chevronRight, chevronsLeft, chevronsRight, check, success, error, warning, info, calendar, clock, externalLink, menu, moreHorizontal, search, upload, arrowUp, arrowDown, arrowsUpDown, funnel, eyeSlash, viewColumns, copy, checkDouble, wrench, stop, microphone. A namespaced key such as `richtext:bold` names a glyph that one component or library registers, and a theme can replace it by key; a namespaced key that nothing registers renders nothing. For any icon not in this list, pass an SVG component directly (e.g. import from lucide-react or @heroicons/react). Note: this prop is called `icon`, not `name`; a call with only `name` renders that glyph and warns in development.

props.name: color
props.description: Color variant mapped to Astryx icon color tokens. Semantic values (primary through warning) follow the role, and inherit uses the surrounding text color. On the web, Icon also accepts the palette values blue, red, green, gray, cyan, teal, yellow, orange, pink, and purple, which pick a non-semantic hue.

props.name: size
props.description: Icon size. xsm, sm, md, and lg are 12, 16, 20, and 24px at a 16px root and scale with the root font size; a theme sets a size's glyph dimension with width and height, in px or rem, on components.icon['size:sm'] (and the other sizes). An explicit value wins. When omitted, Icon uses the nearest default supplied by an owning Astryx component for its icon slot, then falls back to md when no contextual default exists.

props.name: variant
props.description: Requests the active theme's alternate artwork for a built-in meaning, such as 'filled'. Names come from IconVariantMap, which an application augments from @astryxdesign/core/Icon; Astryx defines none. The theme's icon entry receives the variant only when the active theme lists it in iconVariants (and, for an entry the theme inherited, the theme that defined the entry lists it too); otherwise it draws its normal artwork. Ignored by an icon component passed directly. Selects artwork only: it is not written to the DOM and has no theming selector.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for a MEANINGFUL, standalone icon (a status glyph or icon-only indicator with no adjacent text). Setting it exposes the icon to screen readers as role="img" with this text as the accessible name (aria-label) and removes the default aria-hidden. Omit it (default) for decorative icons and the icon stays hidden from assistive tech (aria-hidden="true"). This is the accessible-name / alt-text prop for icons: one prop instead of manually setting aria-label + role + aria-hidden. An empty string is treated as decorative. Do not set it when an interactive parent (Button, IconButton, link) already names the control.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for customization (color, size, opacity). Folded into the icon's own stylex.props() call so it composes with the base color/size styles. Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name added to the rendered glyph, beside the astryx-icon target class.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles merged onto the rendered glyph after Icon's own size and color styles.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the rendered SVG element, for an icon component and for a built-in meaning or namespaced key. For a name, it is the <svg> inside the wrapper, or null when the resolved glyph has no <svg>.

bestPractices.text: Use built-in meanings when available; they adapt to theme changes automatically.

Override icons through the theme, not globally: defineTheme({icons: {close: <XMarkIcon />}}) scopes the swap to the active <Theme>, and extends shallow-merges it into derived themes. registerIcons() mutates a process-wide registry and warns in dev, so keep it for app bootstrap rather than making it a library's theming seam.

To match artwork to the rendered size, make a theme or registered icon entry a pure, synchronous function of {size, variant}: defineTheme({icons: {info: ({size}) => <InfoIcon weight={size === 'sm' ? 'bold' : 'regular'} />}}). Icon passes the size it renders at; getIcon(), useIcon(), getIconRegistry() and theme.icons read the function at size md. A function that returns null draws nothing instead of falling back to the default icon. Do not use hooks, measure the DOM, or read browser or mutable state inside it.
Pair icons with text labels for accessibility; icon-only elements need an accessible label.
For a meaningful standalone icon (no adjacent text), give it an accessible name via the `label` prop: it sets role="img" + aria-label and unhides the icon.
Use color tokens for icon colors, not hardcoded hex values.
Be mindful of context; decorative icons in compact components can distract rather than help.
Use icons as the sole means of conveying meaning; always provide a text alternative.
Resize icons with arbitrary pixel values; use the provided size props.
Mix icon styles (e.g. outline and filled) within the same context.
Render raw SVG elements; always wrap in Icon for consistent sizing and color.
Pass a `name` prop; Icon uses `icon` (not `name`) to specify which icon to render.

anatomy.name: Glyph
anatomy.description: Visual symbol rendered for the selected icon.

components.name: IconButton
components.description: A button that shows only an icon with no visible text. Use IconButton in toolbars, table rows, and compact UI where space is tight and the icon is universally understood.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label. Used as aria-label (not rendered as visible text).

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon element rendered inside the button: `<Icon icon="close" />` for a built-in meaning, or `<Icon icon={TrashIcon} />` for any SVG component from your icon library. An Astryx Icon with no explicit size defaults to sm for sm/md buttons and md for lg buttons.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual style variant.

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant.

props.name: elevation
props.description: Resting shadow depth. The most common FAB shape is an icon-only button, so raise it with `low`/`med`/`high` for a floating action button. `none` is the default flat button.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Shows a loading spinner and blocks re-activation while staying focusable (aria-busy + aria-disabled, not native disabled).

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the button. Uses aria-disabled instead of native disabled so the button stays focusable.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Tooltip text shown on hover and keyboard focus. It also describes the button, unless it repeats the button's accessible name.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Standard click handler.

props.name: clickAction
props.description: Async click handler with automatic loading state.

props.name: isInterruptible
props.description: Keep the button clickable while a clickAction is pending: the spinner and aria-busy still show, but the button is not disabled and the action is not deduped, so a re-click lands and interrupts the in-flight action with a fresh one. Use it for interruptible actions, not fire-once actions (submit, save, pay).

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the button. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is. Without it the button keeps its icon-only aspect, square by default; with it the button takes that width.

props.name: type
props.description: HTML button type attribute.

props.name: name
props.description: HTML name attribute for form submission.

props.name: value
props.description: HTML value attribute for form submission.

props.name: form
props.description: Associates the button with a form element by ID.

props.name: href
props.description: When provided, renders the button as a link element (<a> or custom link component). A disabled IconButton still renders a <button>.

props.name: as
props.description: Custom link component to use when href is provided (e.g. Next.js Link).

props.name: target
props.description: HTML target attribute when rendered as a link (e.g. "_blank").

props.name: rel
props.description: HTML rel attribute when rendered as a link (e.g. "noopener noreferrer").

bestPractices.text: Make the aria-label specific: a trash icon labeled "Delete conversation" is clearer than just "Delete" for screen readers.
Add a tooltip: even a gear icon can mean Settings, Preferences, or Configure.
Use ghost in toolbars and dense areas to reduce visual clutter.
Use IconButton if the action isn't obvious from the icon alone; use Button with text.
Skip the tooltip; label only reaches screen readers, sighted users need the hover hint.

accessibility.name: Essential icon or spinner arc
accessibility.description: IconButton has no visible label. Its icon must have at least 3:1 contrast with the button background in Rest, Hover, and Pointer down. The moving spinner arc must also meet 3:1 while loading.

accessibility.name: Visible control boundary
accessibility.description: The button edge needs 3:1 contrast only when users need it to see the control.

accessibility.name: Keyboard focus indicator
accessibility.description: The focus outline must have at least 3:1 contrast with the area around the button. Check the red outline on destructive buttons too.

accessibility.name: Disabled appearance
accessibility.description: Disabled controls do not need to meet these contrast ratios.

components.name: Indicator
components.description: Indicators are the componentized selection visuals shared by CheckboxInput, RadioList, and menu selection rows. They are decorative: the owning component keeps the input, role, accessible name, focus, and keyboard behavior, while the indicator turns state into a picture. That split is what makes them themeable: restyle one through its class targets, or replace the component outright.

bestPractices.text: Reach for the canonical `components['checkbox-indicator']` override first. Replacing the component is the heavier path, for when the shape itself is wrong.

Match the shipped replacement-content branch with `isRenderable(children)`, not `children != null` or `children ?? mark`. The helper is deliberately shallow: it excludes nullish values, booleans, and the empty string, while React elements and containers take the replacement path even when their descendants render nothing. The owning control passes `children={isBusy && <Spinner/>}`, so a nullish check deletes the state mark whenever that value is `false` (#4893).
A replacement must set aria-hidden. The owning control provides the role and accessible name; a visible indicator would be announced twice.
Use theme tokens for every color, radius, and border width in a replacement. Run `astryx docs tokens` for the set.

Render a single root ELEMENT, and let it keep the border-radius you want the focus ring to follow. A control whose real input is visually hidden cannot show focus on that input, so the owner paints the standard ring onto the indicator element itself at focus time (useIndicatorFocusRing), and `outline` then picks up that element's radius. A replacement needs no cooperation and can forget nothing: the ring is never missing (WCAG 2.4.7), it is only the wrong shape if the root has no radius of its own. Do not draw a focus ring yourself; the owner already did.
Thread hover or pressed state in as props. Interaction state reaches an indicator through the owner's CSS ancestor marker, so hovering the row tints the control with no props involved.

Assume you are only mounted when selected. The host renders its indicator unconditionally and passes `state`, in every state; that is what lets a replacement draw where the default draws nothing (a radio's empty circle on an unchosen row). Drawing nothing in a state is a decision the indicator makes, not one the host makes for it.

anatomy.name: Chrome (checkbox, radio)
anatomy.description: The persistent box or circle rendered by CheckboxIndicator and RadioIndicator in every state. CheckIndicator is the state mark itself and intentionally owns no chrome.

anatomy.name: State mark
anatomy.description: The checkmark, indeterminate bar, or radio dot shown inside the chrome for the current state.

components.name: InfoTip
components.description: An info icon that reveals help: a small "i" button. Hover and keyboard focus preview the help, and a click, tap, Enter, or Space pins it open until Escape, a second press, a press outside, or focus leaving. Use it next to labels, values, and metrics for permission notes, metric definitions, and field help. Its value over hand-composing Icon inside Tooltip is the pre-wired accessible trigger: a real button with an aria-label, Tab-reachable, tooltip on hover AND focus AND tap, and Escape dismissal. It follows the toggletip pattern: the button reports `aria-expanded="true"` while the help is pinned, and a screen reader hears the help once when it pins. Host `data-*` attributes reach the button; its name and disclosure attributes stay component-owned.

props.name: content
props.description: Content to display in the tooltip. Typically short, non-interactive text. Mirrors Tooltip's content prop.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the trigger button. Defaults to the translated "More information".

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the info icon (12px, 16px, 20px, 24px). Maps 1:1 to Icon sizes.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

bestPractices.text: Keep tooltip content concise, plain, and non-interactive; use Popover or HoverCard for links and buttons.
Override label when "More information" is too generic, e.g. "About this metric".

Rely on InfoTip rather than a hand-rolled info button on touch: it pins its help on a press, so a tap, a click, Enter, or Space pins the tooltip even though the trigger is a button, and a tap outside dismisses it.
Hand-compose Icon inside Tooltip for info affordances; the bare Icon is aria-hidden and unfocusable, so keyboard and screen-reader users never see it.
Use InfoTip for essential information users must see to complete a task; put that text inline instead.

anatomy.name: Trigger button
anatomy.description: Small round native button, named by `label`, that previews and pins the help.

anatomy.name: Info icon
anatomy.description: The `info` icon at `size`; a theme may replace it.

anatomy.name: Help surface
anatomy.description: Tooltip surface that shows `content` while the help is shown.

components.name: InputGroup
components.description: InputGroup connects an input with prefix/suffix addons in a single visual unit. Use it for URL fields, currency inputs, search fields with action buttons, or any input that needs contextual decorations.

props.name: children
props.description: InputGroupText, Button addons, and compatible input children: TextInput, NumberInput, TimeInput, DateInput, Typeahead, Tokenizer, Selector, or MultiSelector.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the group.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hide the label.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text between label and input group.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disable the entire group.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Show the "Optional" indicator after the label.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Mark the field as required.

props.name: size
props.description: Default size for inputs in the group.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status. Its message shows below the group. The group border does not change; a theme can style the row from `data-status`.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text at the end of the label.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector.

bestPractices.text: Use text addons to show units, prefixes, or suffixes that clarify the input format (e.g., "$", "kg", "https://").
Use InputGroupText for static prefixes/suffixes like "$", "kg", or "https://".
Use Button for an action attached to the input; InputGroup connects its corners automatically.
Use InputGroup with compatible single-line inputs: TextInput, NumberInput, TimeInput, DateInput, Typeahead, Tokenizer, Selector, and MultiSelector.
Keep each inner input's label specific; grouped inputs automatically combine the group label with their own label and inherit the group description/status context.
Keep multi-value controls (Tokenizer, MultiSelector) short inside a group — the group is a fixed-height single-line surface, so cap or summarize selections instead of letting them fill the row.
Don't put multiple text inputs in one group; use separate fields instead.
Don't use InputGroup for unrelated inputs; it's for a single input with decorations.
Don't use InputGroup with TextArea, Slider, Switch, CheckboxInput, or RadioList.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Text above the group.

anatomy.name: Prefix addon
anatomy.description: Content before the input (text, icon, or button).

anatomy.name: Input
anatomy.description: The main input element (TextInput, NumberInput, TimeInput, DateInput, Typeahead, Tokenizer, Selector, or MultiSelector).

anatomy.name: Suffix addon
anatomy.description: Content after the input (text, icon, or button).

anatomy.name: Status message
anatomy.description: An error, warning, or success message below the group.

components.name: InputGroupText
components.description: Use InputGroupText inside InputGroup for a short fixed prefix or suffix, such as a currency symbol, a protocol, or a unit, or for a decorative icon. It is plain text, not a control, and it is not part of the input's accessible name.

props.name: children
props.description: Text or icon content.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name(s).

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the text cell element.

bestPractices.text: Keep the text short, such as $, https://, or kg. It stays on one line and does not shrink.

Plain text keeps its character order under right-to-left, so https:// and .com read as written. When rich content mixes directions, mark the direction on your own content, for example with `dir` or `<bdi>`.
Put what a screen reader user needs in the input's own label, such as "Amount in USD" beside a $ prefix. The addon is read as plain text in reading order.
Put buttons, links, or other controls inside InputGroupText. Use a Button addon for an action.
Use InputGroupText outside InputGroup. Its borders and corners join an InputGroup row.

anatomy.name: Text cell
anatomy.description: A non-interactive cell that holds text or an icon and joins the borders of its neighbours in the row.

components.name: InternationalizationProvider
components.description: Wraps your app to set the active locale and (optionally) merge additional translation catalogs + per-locale overrides. Astryx components inside the subtree resolve their strings against this context. If no provider is present, components fall back to the shipped English defaults.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP 47 language tag for the active locale (e.g. "en", "pt", "pt-BR", "zh-Hans"). Regional tags fall back to their base language, then to the shipped "en" catalog.

props.name: messages
props.description: Optional map of BCP 47 tag to a rich or generated runtime catalog. Import compact shipped catalogs from `@astryxdesign/core/locales/*.generated.js`; the shipped "en" catalog is always available and does not need to be listed here.

props.name: overrides
props.description: Sparse per-locale key overrides applied on top of shipped defaults. Overrides are locale-keyed so a runtime locale swap picks up the correct set.

props.name: dir
props.description: Explicit text-direction override for the context. When omitted, direction is derived from `locale` via `Intl.Locale.getTextInfo()`. This sets the direction Astryx reads, but it does NOT set the DOM `dir` attribute; you must set `dir` on `<html>` (or a wrapping element) yourself, since Astryx components mirror layout and directional icons from the DOM `dir`, not from this prop. Set both to the same value and keep them in sync.

props.name: calendar
props.description: Calendar system of the subtree, such as 'persian', 'hebrew', or 'buddhist'. `Calendar`, `DateInput`, `DateRangeInput`, and `DateTimeInput` show it, and Timestamp, PowerSearch, and Lab's Schedule write their dates in it. When omitted, the calendar is Gregorian: a locale never selects it, neither by its default calendar nor by a `-u-ca-` keyword. A component's own `calendar` prop takes precedence. Values stay Gregorian ISO dates. Calendars other than gregory, iso8601, buddhist, roc, and japanese need `Temporal`; the context keeps the requested calendar, and where the runtime lacks `Temporal`, these components show Gregorian dates and warn in development. Load a polyfill such as `temporal-polyfill/full/global` on the server and in the browser.

props.name: children
props.description: Content to render with the internationalization provider.

bestPractices.text: Use shipped Astryx locale catalogs from `@astryxdesign/core/locales/*` when one exists for your target locale.
Use a same-shape local catalog only when Astryx has not shipped that locale yet or you are testing in-progress translations.
Use real BCP 47 tags such as `fr-FR`, `pt-BR`, or `ar-SA`; regional locales fall back to their base language before English.

Set the `dir` attribute on `<html>` (or a wrapping element) yourself; the provider does not set it. Astryx components mirror layout and directional icons from the DOM `dir`, so an RTL locale won't visually mirror without it. Use `getLocaleDirection(locale)` to derive the value for both the provider and the DOM.

Set `calendar` to show `Calendar`, `DateInput`, `DateRangeInput`, and `DateTimeInput` in another calendar system and write Timestamp, PowerSearch, and Schedule dates in it. A locale never selects the calendar: `fa-IR` shows Gregorian dates until you set `calendar="persian"`, and a `-u-ca-` keyword in `locale`, as in `th-TH-u-ca-buddhist`, keeps Gregorian dates too. Date values stay Gregorian ISO strings.
Cast custom catalog maps to `any`; the i18n package exports `ProviderMessagesByLocale`, `MessagesByLocale`, `Catalog`, and `RuntimeCatalog` for local catalog typing.

anatomy.name: Provider boundary
anatomy.description: A nonvisual context boundary that supplies locale, message catalogs, overrides, and direction to descendant Astryx components, and a calendar system to `Calendar`. It renders no DOM element.

components.name: Item
components.description: A single, flexible item primitive that unifies the "start content + label + description + end content" pattern across Astryx. Use it wherever you need a structured row: dropdown menus, selectors, contact lists, notifications, file browsers, and activity feeds.

bestPractices.text: Use named slots (startContent, label, description, endContent) for the common layout. These cover the 80% case.
