anatomy.description: Arbitrary React content supplied directly as the trigger icon override.

anatomy.name: Menu surface
anatomy.description: DropdownMenu panel that also carries MoreMenu’s current public target.

anatomy.name: Pointer action row
anatomy.description: Action or nested-action trigger row rendered by DropdownMenu in the anchored presentation.

anatomy.name: Touch action row
anatomy.description: ListItem button rendered by DropdownMenu in the BottomSheet presentation.

components.name: MultiSelector
components.description: A checkbox dropdown for selecting multiple values from a list. Selected items can display as a count, labels, or badges. Use it for filtering or when presenting a finite set of options where multiple choices are needed.

bestPractices.text: Use for a moderate, finite set of options where multiple choices are needed.
Enable search filtering when the list exceeds ~15 options.
Use renderOption for custom option rows; the checkbox affordance remains owned by MultiSelector.
Enable select-all when most users will want all or nearly all options selected.
Use inside InputGroup only when the control needs a short prefix or suffix addon as part of one decorated input surface; prefer count or labels trigger display so the group stays single-line.

Use variant="secondary" when a multi-selector sits beside secondary buttons or segmented controls, and variant="ghost" when it sits beside ghost buttons. If validation status is needed there, prefer statusVariant="tooltip" so the toolbar height stays compact.
Use presentation="adaptive" when the multi-selector should become a bottom sheet on compact touch screens.
Use for single-value selection; use Selector instead.
Show more than ~20 options without enabling search.
Wrap a disabled MultiSelector in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop, which attaches the reason to the trigger itself.

anatomy.name: Field
anatomy.description: Standalone Field shell that provides the label and optional supporting content; omitted inside InputGroup.

anatomy.name: Trigger
anatomy.description: Painted control that displays the current selection or placeholder and opens the selection surface when editable.

anatomy.name: Icon-rendered start icon
anatomy.description: Optional leading icon, by built-in meaning or icon component, rendered through Icon.

anatomy.name: Caller-rendered start content
anatomy.description: Optional arbitrary React content rendered directly at the start of the trigger.

anatomy.name: Trigger clear button
anatomy.description: Shared clear action that removes every selected value when hasClear is enabled.

anatomy.name: Status icon
anatomy.description: Status glyph shown in place of the disclosure indicator for attached or tooltip status.

anatomy.name: Indicator icon
anatomy.description: Trailing chevron shown when status presentation does not replace it; reflects collapsed or expanded state.

anatomy.name: Search row
anatomy.description: Panel header with a borderless search input and optional clear action.

anatomy.name: Search icon
anatomy.description: Leading magnifier rendered through Icon inside the search row.

anatomy.name: Search clear button
anatomy.description: Shared clear action shown in the search row while a query is present.

components.name: NavHeadingMenu
components.description: Accessible menu container and items for nav heading popovers. NavHeadingMenu provides role="menu" with keyboard navigation; NavHeadingMenuItem renders individual selectable items. Pass as the menu prop of SideNavHeading or TopNavHeading.

props.name: children
props.description: Menu items.

props.name: size
props.description: Controls min-width and item padding.

props.name: minWidth
props.description: Minimum width override. Takes precedence over the size-based minimum width.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the menu element.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

bestPractices.text: Pass NavHeadingMenu as the menu prop of SideNavHeading or TopNavHeading. Where the heading closes on a choice, choosing an enabled item runs its onClick or link and closes the menu.

NavHeadingMenu follows the keyboard model of the WAI-ARIA APG Menu pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/): a menu of menuitem rows. ArrowDown and ArrowUp move one row and wrap, Home and End go to the first and last row, typing a character moves to the matching row, Enter or Space activates the row, and Escape closes the heading menu where the heading supplies a close action.
Give a NavHeadingMenu used on its own an aria-label. The menu has no accessible name unless you pass one.

Remove a destination the user cannot use right now when knowing it exists helps them. Set isDisabled instead: the row stays reachable by the arrow keys and typeahead, is announced as disabled, and does nothing when chosen.
Put other interactive controls in the menu. The arrow keys move only between NavHeadingMenuItem rows, so another control is skipped.

anatomy.name: Menu
anatomy.description: Menu container for nav-heading actions, with menu semantics and keyboard navigation.

anatomy.name: Item
anatomy.description: Selectable action or navigation link inside the Menu.

anatomy.name: Icon
anatomy.description: Optional Icon-rendered artwork shown before an Item label.

anatomy.name: Text-rendered item label
anatomy.description: String Item label rendered through Text.

anatomy.name: Caller-rendered item label
anatomy.description: Non-string Item label content rendered directly by the caller.

anatomy.name: Item description
anatomy.description: Optional supporting description rendered through Text.

components.name: NavIcon
components.description: NavIcon is a circular icon container with an accent-colored background. Use it in navigation headers such as TopNavHeading and SideNavHeading to visually identify a section or application.

props.name: icon
props.description: The icon element to render inside the circular background. Should be an Icon or similar icon component.

bestPractices.text: Use in navigation headers to provide a recognizable visual anchor for the section.
Pass an Icon or similarly sized icon component to ensure proper proportions.
NavIcon adds no role or name of its own, so the icon you pass decides what assistive technology announces. An Icon is hidden from screen readers unless you give it a label.
Use NavIcon for interactive purposes; it is a display-only container, not a button.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: Circular painted container for the supplied icon.

anatomy.name: Icon
anatomy.description: Caller-supplied visual content rendered inside the container.

components.name: NumberInput
components.description: A form input for numeric values with built-in validation, min/max constraints, and step controls. Use NumberInput for quantities, measurements, percentages, and similar inputs.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the input (always rendered for accessibility).

props.name: value
props.description: Current value of the input.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when a valid text edit commits on blur or Enter, or when a step or clear control changes the value.

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hide the label (still accessible to screen readers).

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed between the label and input.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Whether the field is optional (mutually exclusive with isRequired).

props.name: onKeyDown
props.description: Callback fired on keydown events on the input.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Whether the field is required (mutually exclusive with isOptional).

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the input is disabled.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: Makes the input read-only: the value is shown at full opacity and still submits with the form, but cannot be edited. Unlike isDisabled, a read-only input is not dimmed and keeps its form value. Stepping is off in every form while read-only: arrow keys, the wheel, and the number steppers. isDisabled takes precedence when both are set.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the input is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the input focusable via aria-disabled (the field becomes read-only). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled NumberInput in Tooltip.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text to display in an info icon at the end of the label.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon to display at the start of the input; pass a built-in meaning such as 'search' (see `astryx docs icons`), an icon component, or an icon element.

props.name: labelIcon
props.description: Icon to display before the label text; pass a built-in meaning such as 'search' (see `astryx docs icons`), an icon component, or an icon element.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status with optional message. Typing never shows a rejection: a typed number is complete only at commit. When Enter or blur meets text that is not a number, a fraction in an integer-only field, or any number while min is above max, the text stays in the field and the field shows its own error message in place of status. An error status with a message shows instead of that message, and the rejection is still announced and marks the field invalid. A warning or success status, or an error status without a message, never replaces it. A number outside an ordinary range clamps instead.

props.name: onEntryErrorChange
props.type: (error: {kind: 'unreadable' | 'fractional' | 'outOfRange', text: string, value?: number} | null) => void
props.description: Called each time the field's rejection of typed text changes, and with null when the rejection ends. A rejection starts only at Enter or blur. kind is 'unreadable' (text that is not a number), 'fractional' (a fraction when isIntegerOnly), or 'outOfRange' (any number while min is above max); text is the typed text; value is the number it names, for 'fractional' and 'outOfRange'. It also runs when an edit makes the text valid or empty, when a new value, min, max, or isIntegerOnly changes or ends the rejection, and when disabling the field drops the text, and never twice for the same rejection; it reports null when the field unmounts while a rejection stands. Pass an error status with a message to word the rejection yourself.

props.name: entryErrorBehavior
props.description: When the field shows its own entry error: typed text it rejects, as onEntryErrorChange reports it. It sets when the error shows, not when validation runs, so it is not React Aria's validationBehavior (native versus ARIA validation), and it never changes a caller status. A typed number is complete only at Enter or blur, so 'complete' and 'blur-or-enter' behave the same: the message, aria-invalid, the invalid styling, the announcement, and the onEntryErrorChange report appear together at Enter or blur, never while a person types, and an edit that makes the text valid or empty clears the error at once. Set it to match the other fields of a form; the field's own value wins over the nearest FormLayout's defaultEntryErrorBehavior.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip hides the message box and surfaces it in a tooltip on the status icon.

props.name: min
props.description: Minimum value allowed. A smaller entry commits at this value on blur or Enter.

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum value allowed. A larger entry commits at this value on blur or Enter.

props.name: step
props.description: Step increment for the input.

props.name: formatValue
props.description: Formats the committed value while the input is not focused. The plain number, with the locale's decimal separator, is shown on focus for editing and the formatted value is exposed through aria-valuetext.

props.name: isWheelEnabled
props.description: Whether scrolling the wheel over the focused input steps the value. Disable this when page scrolling should always take priority.

props.name: hasNumberSteppers
props.description: Shows increment and decrement buttons at the end of the input on fine pointers. Hidden on coarse pointers (such as touch screens); text entry and keyboard stepping remain available. Holding a button with a mouse or a pen repeats the step and commits once, when the hold ends.

props.name: units
props.description: Units text to display at the end of the input (e.g., "%" or "GB").

props.name: isIntegerOnly
props.description: Only allow integer values (no floating point).

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Shows a clear (×) button while the input has a value and is editable (not disabled or read-only). When true, the onChange callback also accepts null to signal the user cleared the input.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: HTML name attribute for form submissions. While blur keeps rejected text, the form posts the committed number, until the person edits the text or a new value replaces it.

props.name: autoComplete
props.description: HTML autocomplete attribute.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Whether to focus the input on mount.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Callback fired when the input receives focus.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Callback fired when the input loses focus.

props.name: onEnter
props.description: Callback fired when the user presses the Enter key.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the element that paints the border and background and holds icons and end controls. Never the native input.

bestPractices.text: Let people paste formatted numbers: a pasted 1,234,234,234 is read under the field's locale and commits as 1234234234 on blur. Typing is never intercepted.
Set min, max, and step to guide users toward valid values.
Show units (e.g. "%" or "GB") so users know what the number represents.
Set isWheelEnabled={false} when the input appears in a scrolling surface where wheel gestures should always scroll the page.
Use NumberInput for free-form text that happens to contain numbers; use TextInput instead.
Set both isOptional and isRequired on the same field.
Wrap a disabled NumberInput in Tooltip to explain why it's disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop, which attaches the reason to the field itself.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: The label for the number input.

anatomy.name: Description
anatomy.description: Additional description text below the label.

anatomy.name: Icon
anatomy.description: An optional icon within the input.

anatomy.name: Placeholder
anatomy.description: Placeholder text shown when the input is empty.

anatomy.name: Number steppers
anatomy.description: Optional buttons that increment or decrement by the configured step.

components.name: Outline
components.description: A table-of-contents sidebar for documentation pages, help centers, wikis, and long settings pages. Use it for navigation within a single page, not for app routes. Features a sliding indicator track that animates to the active heading. Each link is in the normal Tab order, and Enter/Space activate.

bestPractices.text: Pass a flat ordered list of headings and let level control indentation.
Use activeId when custom scroll logic owns the active section.
Use density="compact" in dense sidebars where vertical space is tight.

Use useOutlineFromMarkdown or useOutlineFromDOM when headings are generated from content. For linkable Markdown headings, pass the same createMarkdownHeadingLinks() entry to Markdown and Outline; configure headingIdPrefix on that plugin for multiple roots.
Pass scrollContainerRef when the content scrolls in a split pane, modal, or panel instead of the viewport.
Set offset to the height of a fixed header that overlays the content, so headings land below it instead of underneath it.
Give each Outline a distinct label when a page has more than one navigation landmark, so screen reader users can tell them apart.
Use Outline for application navigation - use SideNav or TopNav for routes.
Use Outline for expandable hierarchy - use TreeList when nodes need expand and collapse.
Rely on onNavigateEnd to mean "arrived" - it also fires when the user interrupts the scroll.

anatomy.name: Outline
anatomy.description: Navigation container for the same-page heading links and indicator.

anatomy.name: Heading link
anatomy.description: Anchor for one heading, indented by level and marked when active.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Heading text displayed inside its heading link.

anatomy.name: Indicator track
anatomy.description: Painted vertical rule behind the active indicator.

anatomy.name: Active indicator
anatomy.description: Sliding bar positioned beside the currently active heading link.

components.name: OverflowList
components.description: A horizontal list that automatically hides items when they exceed the available width. Use OverflowList for breadcrumbs, toolbars, tag lists, or any row that needs to collapse gracefully at smaller sizes.

props.name: children
props.description: Items to render. Each child should be a single element.

props.name: overflowRenderer
props.description: Render function for the overflow indicator. Receives the list of hidden items (each with child and index). Only called when items are overflowing.

props.name: onOverflowChange
props.description: Called whenever the collapsed set changes: with the collapsed items once something collapses, and with an empty array once the row widens back out. Membership and order changes report even when the count stays the same; unrelated re-renders and callback identity changes do not. Silent while nothing overflows, including on mount. Use stable React keys for dynamic items.

props.name: gap
props.description: Gap between items as a spacing token step (0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10).

props.name: minVisibleItems
props.description: Minimum number of items to always show, even when overflowing.

props.name: maxVisibleItems
props.description: Maximum number of items to ever show, even when they all fit. The ceiling partner to minVisibleItems; extra items collapse into the overflow indicator. If less than minVisibleItems, the floor wins.

props.name: maxRows
props.description: Wrap items across up to this many rows before collapsing the rest into the overflow indicator. A number, not a boolean. Leave undefined (or set 1) for single-line behavior. Assumes uniform row height.

props.name: collapseFrom
props.description: Which end to collapse items from when overflow occurs.

props.name: behavior
props.description: Controls which element is measured for available width. 'observeSelf' uses the container's own width. 'observeParent' observes the parent element, useful when the list should stay content-sized while still detecting available space.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object.

bestPractices.text: Provide a meaningful overflowRenderer: a "+N more" badge, a dropdown, or a count indicator.
When the row already has its own menu, use onOverflowChange to feed the collapsed items into it instead of adding a second anchor with overflowRenderer.
Set minVisibleItems to keep key items visible, and maxVisibleItems to cap the row at a fixed count regardless of available width.
Use maxRows to let items wrap onto a bounded number of rows (e.g. a two-row tag cloud) before collapsing the rest into the indicator.
Use OverflowList for a vertical stack; horizontal multi-row wrap is supported via maxRows, but items still flow left-to-right, not top-to-bottom.
Render a count-only indicator when people need the collapsed items: make the indicator a control, such as a dropdown menu, so keyboard and screen reader users can reach them.

anatomy.name: List
anatomy.description: Visible horizontal list container for the currently shown content.

anatomy.name: Items
anatomy.description: Caller-supplied items selected for visible display by the current width and count limits.

anatomy.name: Overflow indicator
anatomy.description: Optional caller-rendered indicator for items collapsed by width or count limits.

components.name: Overlay
components.description: Overlay layers action or supporting content over media, cards, video, or other bounded surfaces with an optional scrim and reveal behavior. Host attributes and DOM handlers (id, data-*, aria-*) reach the root element.

props.name: content
props.description: Content rendered inside the overlay scrim.

props.name: children
props.description: Base content such as an image, video, card, or media surface that the overlay sits on top of.

props.name: showOn
props.description: Visibility trigger. Hover mode also reveals on focus for keyboard accessibility; hover-or-focus is an alias for hover.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Controlled visibility override. When set, this takes precedence over showOn and touch toggle behavior.

props.name: scrim
props.description: Scrim background mode. Set to false to render overlay content without a scrim background.

props.name: position
props.description: Where the scrim appears within the base surface.

props.name: align
props.description: Alignment of the overlay content within the scrim.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name(s) appended to the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling when possible.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles applied to the root element. Prefer xstyle for design-system styling.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the overlay root element.

bestPractices.text: Use overlays for short, contextual actions or labels that belong directly to the underlying media or surface.
Keep overlay content compact so it remains legible over the scrim and does not obscure important visual information.

Give an overlay action a label that names what it does, such as "Quick view". With showOn hover or focus on a device with a mouse or trackpad, Tab reaches the action while the overlay is hidden, and focus reveals the overlay.
Do not use Overlay for floating content anchored outside the surface. Use Popover, Tooltip, or Dialog for those patterns.

Do not put information people need to choose the item, such as its title or price, only in a hover or focus overlay. On a touch device a hover overlay shows only after a tap, and a focus overlay does not show.

anatomy.name: Base content
anatomy.description: The media, card, or bounded surface that the overlay sits on top of.

anatomy.name: Scrim
anatomy.description: Optional dark or light overlay background that improves content contrast.

anatomy.name: Overlay content
anatomy.description: Actions, labels, or supporting content rendered above the base surface.

components.name: Pagination
components.description: Pagination lets users step through pages of content. Place it below a table, list, or card grid so users can move forward and backward through results. Pick a variant to match the context: numbered pages for data tables, a count for large lists, compact for tight spaces, or dots for carousels.

props.name: page
props.description: Current page number (1-based). Page 1 is the first page.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when the page changes. With getPageHref it also runs when a page link is activated: use it there for state or analytics, and do not navigate in it, because the link navigates.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action on page change. Fires after onChange and uses React transitions for built-in loading state.

props.name: getPageHref
props.description: Returns the URL of a page. When set, the page number, previous, next, first and last controls render as links to it, so a page opens in a new tab, its address can be copied, and it works before scripts load. onChange still runs when a link is activated. pageSize is the current page size when pageSize or pageSizeOptions is set. The dots, the page box and the page-size selector are not links. For a page-size choice, navigate in onPageSizeChange to the URL of page 1 with the new size, not in the onChange(1) that follows. When onChange navigates for the dots or the page box, leave getPageHref unset in the dots and input variants, or their arrow links navigate twice. In cursor pagination, map the page before or after the current one to the cursor's URL. The destination follows the shared navigation rule described on the Link `href` prop.

props.name: as
props.description: Custom link component for the links getPageHref makes (e.g. Next.js Link). Overrides the LinkProvider default.

props.name: totalItems
props.description: Total number of items. Used to calculate the page count when totalPages is not given.

props.name: totalPages
props.description: Total number of pages. Use when you know page count but not item count. Takes precedence over totalItems if both are given.

props.name: hasMore
props.description: Whether more pages exist after the current one. Use for cursor-based pagination where total is unknown.

props.name: pageSize
props.description: Number of items per page. Coerced to a positive integer; non-finite values fall back to the default.

props.name: pageSizeOptions
props.description: Available page size options. Shows a page size selector dropdown when provided.

props.name: onPageSizeChange
props.description: Called when the page size changes. Automatically resets to page 1.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual variant controlling what appears between prev/next buttons. 'pages' shows page number buttons with ellipsis, 'count' shows 'X-Y of Z' text, 'compact' shows 'Page X of Y' (add first/last buttons with hasFirstLast), 'dots' shows dot indicators, 'input' shows an editable page-number box with a leading label ('Page [ n ] / N') flanked by first/last buttons by default (the box needs a known total to clamp against, so it is disabled in cursor/hasMore mode), 'none' shows just prev/next buttons.

props.name: pageLabel
props.description: The noun rendered before the editable box in the 'input' variant, e.g. 'Page' or 'Row'. Navigation is always page-based (via onChange); this only relabels the box. Defaults to the localized 'Page'.

props.name: hasFirstLast
props.description: Whether to show first/last («/») double-chevron buttons flanking prev/next. Applies to the 'input' variant (shown unless false) and the 'compact' variant (shown only when true); other variants ignore it. Omitted when the page count is unknown (cursor/hasMore pagination).

props.name: step
props.description: Number of pages the previous/next buttons advance per click. Clamped to the valid page range, so a step that would overshoot lands on the first/last page. When greater than 1, the buttons' accessible names reflect the stride. Non-integer or values < 1 fall back to 1.

props.name: siblingCount
props.description: Number of page buttons to show on each side of the current page. Only applies when variant='pages'.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the pagination controls.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the component is disabled.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the navigation landmark.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

bestPractices.text: Place pagination below the content it controls so users see results before navigating.
Use the pages variant for data tables where users need to jump to a specific page.
Use the count variant with a page size selector when users need to control how many items they see at once.
Use the dots variant for carousels and walkthroughs where the total is small and position matters more than a number.
Pass totalItems when the total is known so users can see how much content remains.
Pass getPageHref when each page has its own URL, so a page opens in a new tab and its address can be copied.
Give each Pagination a distinct label when a page has more than one, so screen-reader users can tell the navigation landmarks apart.
Show pagination when all items fit on a single page; there is nothing to paginate.
Use the dots variant for more than about 10 pages; the dots become too small to be useful.
Place pagination above the content; users expect it at the bottom.
Navigate in onChange when getPageHref is set; the link navigates, so keep onChange for state or analytics.

anatomy.name: Pagination
anatomy.description: Navigation landmark containing the current paging controls and optional page-size selector.

anatomy.name: Control row
anatomy.description: The row that holds the previous/next, first/last and page-number buttons and the readout between them.

anatomy.name: Page-size selector
anatomy.description: Optional Selector for choosing how many items appear per page.

anatomy.name: First/last buttons
anatomy.description: Optional Button controls that jump to the first or last known page.

anatomy.name: Previous/next buttons
anatomy.description: Button controls that move backward or forward through the pages.

anatomy.name: Page number button
anatomy.description: Button for one directly selectable page in the numbered presentation.

anatomy.name: Ellipsis
anatomy.description: Visual omission marker between non-adjacent page-number buttons.

anatomy.name: Count readout
anatomy.description: Text showing the current item range and total item count.

anatomy.name: Compact readout
anatomy.description: Text showing the current page and total page count.

anatomy.name: Dot
anatomy.description: Page indicator control that reflects and changes the active page.

components.name: Popover
components.description: A click-triggered overlay anchored to a button or trigger element. Use it for secondary actions, inline confirmations, or supplementary information that does not warrant a full dialog. For hover previews use HoverCard, for brief helper text use Tooltip. Under a finger (a coarse primary pointer), it is presented like a native popover: it grows out of its trigger and shrinks back into it on the theme’s motion tokens; with reduced motion it cross-fades, opacity only, in 200 ms or less.

bestPractices.text: Don't add your own focus return or try to turn it off. When the anchored popover closes with focus inside it, focus goes back to the opener, or to the nearest control that stands in for it, never to the page; as a BottomSheet it uses the sheet's own return. To send focus somewhere specific, focus that element in onOpenChange.
Keep popover content focused on a single task or piece of information.
Provide a clear way to close: either by clicking outside or with an explicit close button.
Theme the painted surface through the canonical popover target.
Nest popovers inside other popovers; it creates confusing focus and navigation.
Assume input complexity alone determines the presentation; evaluate the task's focus, space, and interaction requirements.
Assume scrolling alone means Popover is the wrong component; a bounded Popover may scroll while a focused anchored interaction remains appropriate.

anatomy.name: Trigger element
anatomy.description: Caller-supplied or externally referenced control that anchors and toggles the popover.

anatomy.name: Popover surface
anatomy.description: Painted surface owned and themed by Popover through the canonical popover target.

anatomy.name: Touch sheet
anatomy.description: BottomSheet surface that holds the same content in place of the popover surface for presentation="bottom-sheet", or "adaptive" on a compact touch screen; themed through the bottom-sheet target.

anatomy.name: Popover content
anatomy.description: Caller-supplied content rendered inside the surface.

anatomy.name: Fallback close control
anatomy.description: Keyboard-reachable close affordance appended by usePopover when enabled.

components.name: PowerSearch
components.description: PowerSearch is a structured filter bar where each token represents a field, operator, and value. Use it for complex multi-dimensional filtering when users need to combine multiple search criteria. For simple single-field search, use a text input instead. Host `data-*` attributes, `data-testid` included, reach the primary control: the combobox input in the popover presentation and the trigger button in the sheet presentation. The `components.Token` and `components.Editor` defaults, `PowerSearchToken` and `PowerSearchFilterEditor`, pass them to the token and the editor root.

props.name: config
props.description: Configuration defining available fields, operators, and their value types.

props.name: filters
props.description: Currently active filters.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when filters change. changeType is 'add', 'edit', or 'remove'. index is the affected filter's position.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the search input.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when no filters are selected.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Auto-focus the input on mount.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Show a clear-all button that removes every editable filter. Read-only filters stay.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: Prevent adding, editing, or removing filters.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the entire component.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the search is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the input focusable via aria-disabled (input stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled PowerSearch in Tooltip. Disabled controls swallow the hover events an external Tooltip needs.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status object with type and optional message.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon to display at the start of the input, before any filter tokens; pass a built-in meaning such as 'search' (see `astryx docs icons`), an icon component, or an icon element. Forwarded to the internal Tokenizer.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip reveals the message in an info-tip button.

props.name: maxTokenLength
props.description: Max character length for filter value display in tokens.

props.name: maxOperatorMenuItems
props.description: Maximum suggestions shown in string and entity value typeaheads. Does not affect the main field search menu or enum value menus.

props.name: maxSearchResults
props.description: Max ranked results for a non-empty query. Does not affect a field value editor. Browsing with an empty query shows up to 1,000 fields.

props.name: menuWidth
props.description: Width in pixels for the main field/search menu; it never shrinks below the input width. Does not affect field value editors.

props.name: popoverSaveButtonLabel
props.description: Label for the save button in the edit popover.

props.name: timezoneID
props.description: IANA zone a date-only date_absolute value, and each absolute part of a date_range, is read and written in: the day shows, edits and stores (as that midnight) in it; unset, a day is its UTC day. A date_absolute with isDateOnly: false shows and edits its date and time in it; unset, in the viewer's zone. E.g. "America/New_York". Date values are written in the InternationalizationProvider calendar, such as calendar="persian"; filter values stay Unix seconds.

props.name: handleRef
props.description: Imperative handle with focusTypeahead() and blurTypeahead() methods.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content to display at the end of the input row. Useful for action buttons or other controls.

props.name: resultCount
props.description: Number of results matching the current filters. When a number, formatted as "N results". When a string, displayed as-is. Changes are announced to screen readers via a polite live region.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the search input and tokens.

props.name: components
props.description: Per-type overrides for the filter token and the filter editor. Keys are operator value types, such as 'string', 'enum' or 'date_absolute'. An entry's Token replaces the token for filters of that type, and its Editor replaces the editor content. PowerSearchToken and PowerSearchFilterEditor are the defaults.

props.name: tokenOverflowBehavior
props.description: Controls how tokens overflow when the container is too narrow. Forwarded to Tokenizer.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Fires when focus enters the search input.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Fires when focus leaves the search input.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

props.name: presentation
props.description: How the field presents filter editing. adaptive (the default) uses the bottom sheet on compact touch screens and the popover otherwise, resolved the same way Selector resolves it; the server render and the hydrating render are the popover. popover is the tokenizer field with its typeahead and the editor popover on every device. bottom-sheet makes the whole field, on every device, one trigger showing display-only filter tokens: it opens a Filters sheet listing the filters as rows that edit or remove a filter, with Add filter, Done, and Clear all (which asks first and keeps read-only filters); an Add filter sheet with the fields (or the content search with inline suggestions) opens above it, and a value step that stages operator → value and confirms from its footer opens above that. Dismissing a step reveals the one beneath. The flow edits a draft: adding, editing and removing filters and Clear all change the draft, and onChange is called when Done applies it, once per edit in order; dismissing the flow with a changed draft asks before discarding it. List values edit through the Tokenizer's own sheet. In the sheet presentation menuWidth and tokenOverflowBehavior have no surface to act on and warn in development. Pass presentation="popover" to keep the tokenizer field and the editor popover on every device.

bestPractices.text: Define clear, descriptive field names and aliases so users can quickly find the filter they need.
Provide a result count to give users feedback on how their filters affect the data set.
Use PowerSearch for simple keyword searches; a standard text input is more appropriate for single-field lookups.
Wrap a disabled PowerSearch in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Names the search field for assistive technology. Defaults to the localized 'Search' and is visually hidden unless isLabelHidden is false.

anatomy.name: Filter tokens
anatomy.description: One token per filter, reading field, operator and value. Activating a token opens its editor, except for an operator that takes no value. A remove button follows it unless the field is read-only or disabled, or the filter is read-only.

anatomy.name: Search input
anatomy.description: The combobox after the tokens. Typing lists fields, field-and-operator pairs and value matches. Choosing a field opens the editor; a value match or an operator that takes no value adds the filter at once.

anatomy.name: Filter editor
anatomy.description: A popover that picks the operator and the value and applies them. For a built-in token it opens as a dialog named by the token text.

anatomy.name: Clear all
anatomy.description: Removes every editable filter and keeps read-only ones. Shows while hasClear is set, the field is neither read-only nor disabled, and an editable filter exists.

anatomy.name: End content
anatomy.description: The result count, endContent and the status icon, at the end of the field.

anatomy.name: Sheet trigger and sheets
anatomy.description: In the bottom-sheet presentation the field is one button with display-only tokens. It opens the Filters sheet when a filter exists or the field is read-only, otherwise the Add filter sheet; a value step opens above them.

components.name: ProgressBar
components.description: A horizontal bar showing the completion progress of a task. Use it for operations where the duration is known, or as an animated indicator when progress can't be calculated. Supports semantic color variants, value labels, and custom formatting. Under a finger a new value animates as on iOS: linearly, in proportion to how far it moves (a full track takes one second at the theme's default tempo), and the fill keeps a minimum visible length above zero.

props.name: label
props.description: accessible label

props.name: value
props.description: Current value (ignored when indeterminate).

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum value.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hide the label (remains accessible).

props.name: hasValueLabel
props.description: Show formatted value text (ignored when indeterminate).

props.name: formatValueLabel
props.description: Custom value label formatter; defaults to a percentage string.

props.name: variant
props.description: Semantic color variant. A variant a theme adds paints the accent fill until the theme styles it.

props.name: isIndeterminate
props.description: Animated loading indicator for unknown progress. Under reduced motion it pulses in place instead of sliding.

props.name: marks
props.description: Fixed target marks drawn on the track at values in the same 0..max scale as value (e.g. a goal line). They stay visible whether progress is below or past them, and take their color from what they sit on: a mark inside the filled area uses the color that reads on the fill (on-accent on an accent fill, the surface color on the others), a mark still out on the bare track uses the primary text color (the secondary one on a disabled bar, whose track and fill dim). Each mark requires a label: it is the mark's accessible name and the text revealed via a tooltip on hover/focus. Ignored when indeterminate.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Visually disabled state: grays out the fill and text. Use for canceled or inactive operations.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

bestPractices.text: Use a determinate bar when the total amount of work is known, and indeterminate when it's not.
Choose a color variant that matches the context: accent for general progress, success for completion, warning or error for alerts.
Always provide a label, even if hidden; screen readers need it to announce what's loading.
Screen readers announce the track as a progressbar: the label is its name and the value text is what they read. Pass formatValueLabel when a percentage would mislead, such as "3 of 5 files".
Place icons or labels inside the bar; compose them alongside it using layout components.
Use a progress bar for instant actions; it's meant for operations that take noticeable time.
Use multiple progress bars stacked together for the same operation; use one bar with a value label instead.

anatomy.name: Progress bar
anatomy.description: Container arranging the label row and progress track.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Text naming the operation, optionally hidden visually while remaining accessible.

anatomy.name: Value text
anatomy.description: Formatted determinate value shown beside the label when requested.

anatomy.name: Track
anatomy.description: Remaining-progress rail that carries the progressbar semantics.

anatomy.name: Fill
anatomy.description: Painted segment showing completed progress or indeterminate movement.

anatomy.name: Mark
anatomy.description: Labeled target tick positioned on a determinate track.

components.name: RadioList
components.description: A group of options where only one can be selected at a time. All options are visible at once, making it easy to compare choices. Use it when users need to pick one option from a small set.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the radio group (always rendered for accessibility).

props.name: value
props.description: The currently selected value.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the selected value changes.

props.name: children
props.description: RadioListItem elements.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Whether to visually hide the label.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed below the label.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Layout direction of the radio items.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether all radio items are disabled.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: The HTML name attribute shared by the radio inputs, useful for form submissions. When omitted, a unique internal name still groups the radios.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the group is disabled. Applies to the whole-group disabled state (isDisabled), not per item. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the radios focusable via aria-disabled (selection stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled RadioList in Tooltip. Disabled controls swallow the hover events an external Tooltip needs.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Whether the radio group is required.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Whether the field is optional (mutually exclusive with isRequired).

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator ({ type, message }).

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the radio controls.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text for an info icon next to the label.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the role="radiogroup" element that lays out the options. Never a native radio.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Class name for the role="radiogroup" element.

props.name: controlStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the role="radiogroup" element.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the role="radiogroup" element.

bestPractices.text: Keep the number of options small: typically 2 to 7 choices.
Use clear, concise labels that differentiate each option at a glance.
Pre-select a default option when there's a sensible default; don't leave the group empty unless the choice is optional.
Use when multiple selections are needed; use CheckboxList instead.
Use for long lists; use Selector for better discoverability.
Use horizontal layout with more than 4 options; it wraps awkwardly.
Wrap a disabled RadioList in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

accessibility.name: Radio circle
accessibility.description: The circle edge (unselected) and fill (selected) must have at least 3:1 contrast with the surface behind them. For Hover and Pointer down, measure the final colors after the tint and the pressed overlay are applied.

anatomy.name: Group label
anatomy.description: Names the radio group. Screen readers still read it when isLabelHidden hides it.

anatomy.name: Description
anatomy.description: Optional text below the group label.

anatomy.name: Options
anatomy.description: The RadioListItem rows, one radio each, in a column or a row.

anatomy.name: Status message
anatomy.description: Optional message below the options for an error, warning, or success status.

components.name: RadioListItem
components.description: Individual radio item with label, description, and content slots. Under a coarse pointer an enabled option’s target grows toward 44 px through an invisible hit area. It never shrinks below the row and stops at half the gap to a closer neighbour; the row keeps its size. That hit area is the row’s `::after`, so decorate a row with a child.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary label for the radio item. Rich labels may contain links or buttons, which keep their own behavior without selecting the item. The label text names the radio; use aria-label only when that text is absent, or retain every visible label word in the override.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Plain-text accessible name for the radio, applied to the control rather than the row. It overrides the name derived from the label. Use it when a rich label has no visible text; otherwise retain every visible label word.

props.name: value
props.description: Value of this radio item.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary content displayed below the label. Links and buttons keep their own click behaviour — the row only delegates clicks from its non-interactive surface to the radio.

props.name: align
props.description: Vertical alignment of the start and end content against the label, passed through to Item unchanged. `first-line` keeps a small mark (a radio) level with the first line of a wrapped label. See Item.align.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether this individual radio item is disabled.

props.name: startContent
props.description: Content to render before the radio circle.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content to render after the label.

components.name: Resizable
components.description: Hook-based resizable panel system. useResizable() manages size state and ResizeHandle provides the interactive pill-grip separator. Pass the hook's output to existing layout components via their resizable prop.

bestPractices.text: Use percent(value, {min: pixel(value)}) or percent(value, {max: pixel(value)}) when a percentage needs exactly one pixel floor or ceiling. Reuse Table’s pixel() helper; numbers, exact Npx, and pixel(value) remain pixels. State, persistence, callbacks, paint, and ARIA remain resolved pixels.
Use useResizable() with existing Astryx layout components. Pass its output to the resizable prop on LayoutPanel, ResizeHandle or SideNav; any other element can use its size.
Provide an accessible label on each ResizeHandle when multiple handles exist (e.g. "Resize sidebar", "Resize terminal").
Wrap panels in extra container components for resize. The hook-first architecture avoids extra DOM; use it directly on existing components.

anatomy.name: Handle
anatomy.description: Focusable separator that owns pointer and keyboard resize interaction.

anatomy.name: Grip pill
anatomy.description: Default visible grip indicator; dragging it resizes, wherever it sits. Custom handle content can replace it.

anatomy.name: Grab zone
anatomy.description: Invisible enlarged pointer region centred on the divider. An inline zone takes at most half of a pane shorter than it; an overlay handle takes at most half of its pane.

components.name: ScrollableArea
components.description: Provides a native scroll viewport and a real observed content box. The viewport enters the tab order only while a requested logical axis is effectively scrollable, and containment applies only to effective axes.

props.name: axis
props.description: Logical axis or axes where native scrolling is allowed.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the viewport when it becomes keyboard scrollable.

props.name: role
props.description: Semantics for the named viewport; use `region` only for areas that belong in landmark navigation.

props.name: overscroll
props.description: Whether effective axes continue scrolling an ancestor at their edge.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the viewport; a number is interpreted as pixels, a string is used as-is.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the viewport; a number is interpreted as pixels, a string is used as-is.

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: Maximum width of the viewport.

props.name: minHeight
props.description: Minimum height of the viewport.

props.name: stickyContainment
props.description: Whether fitting content passes Sticky ownership to an outer container or deliberately keeps this viewport as the CSS Sticky boundary.

props.name: padding
props.description: Content padding on every logical edge; publishes matching inset geometry.

props.name: paddingInline
props.description: Logical inline-axis content padding; overrides `padding` on that axis.

props.name: paddingInlineStart
props.description: Logical inline-start content padding; overrides broader padding values.

props.name: paddingInlineEnd
props.description: Logical inline-end content padding; overrides broader padding values.

props.name: paddingBlock
props.description: Logical block-axis content padding; overrides `padding` on that axis.

props.name: paddingBlockStart
props.description: Logical block-start content padding; overrides broader padding values.

props.name: paddingBlockEnd
props.description: Logical block-end content padding; overrides broader padding values.

props.name: isFullBleed
props.description: Lets the viewport escape inherited container padding without changing content padding.

props.name: children
props.description: Content rendered inside the observed content box.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX sizing and native scrollbar presentation overrides for the viewport. Must be a `stylex.create()` value, not an inline style object.

bestPractices.text: Give every area a concise label that identifies the content keyboard users will scroll.

Leave `role` unset (it renders `group`) for ordinary scroll containers. Choose `role="region"` only when the area is significant enough to appear in screen-reader landmark navigation; every `region` adds an entry to that list.
Choose `inline`, `block`, or `both` from content intent; the component maps the logical axes through writing mode and direction.
Keep the default `overscroll="allow"` for nested areas unless the interaction deliberately needs containment.

Use `useScrollableArea` instead when a component already owns both a viewport and a suitable content box, or when children must remain direct flex/grid items or retain a definite percentage block-size basis.

ScrollableArea owns one normal block content box with a 100% minimum size. Inline and both-axis modes use max-content inline sizing, so intrinsic inline layout is intentionally wider than the viewport.
Use logical padding props on the content box so nested full-bleed components receive the same inset geometry.
Set `isFullBleed` only when the viewport itself should reach an ancestor container edge; it is off by default.
Set `stickyContainment="always"` only when a fitting viewport should intentionally remain a Sticky boundary.
Hide the native scrollbar without another visible and operable overflow affordance.
Add another overflow wrapper around ScrollableArea; one native viewport should own scrolling.

anatomy.name: Viewport
anatomy.description: The root native scroll container, accessible name owner, focus target while effective, and `astryx-scrollable-area` theme target.

anatomy.name: Content box
anatomy.description: A real inner layout box observed together with the viewport. For inline scrolling it uses max-content inline sizing with a 100% minimum.

components.name: Section
components.description: Section is the correct way to create page regions and group related content on a page. Use it for settings groups, form sections, sidebar areas, or any time you need visual separation between parts of a page. If you are tempted to use a Card for a page section, use Section instead.

props.name: variant
props.description: Background variant applied to the section container.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the section; a number is interpreted as pixels, a string is used as-is.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the section; a number is interpreted as pixels, a string is used as-is.

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: Maximum width of the section.

props.name: minHeight
props.description: Minimum height of the section.

props.name: children
props.description: Content rendered inside the section.

props.name: dividers
props.description: Which sides of the section have divider borders.

props.name: padding
props.description: Internal padding using the spacing scale (0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10). Use padding={0} for edge-to-edge content.

props.name: paddingInline
props.description: Inline (horizontal) padding override. Overrides only the inline-axis padding while preserving block padding from `padding` or the container theme default. Accepts the spacing scale (0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10).

props.name: paddingInlineStart
props.description: Inline-start padding override (left in LTR, right in RTL). Overrides paddingInline and padding on that edge only.

props.name: paddingInlineEnd
props.description: Inline-end padding override (right in LTR, left in RTL). Overrides paddingInline and padding on that edge only.

props.name: paddingBlock
props.description: Block (vertical) padding override. Overrides only the block-axis padding while preserving inline padding from `padding` or the container theme default. Accepts the spacing scale (0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10).

props.name: paddingBlockStart
props.description: Block-start (top) padding, using the spacing scale. Overrides paddingBlock and padding on that edge only.

props.name: paddingBlockEnd
props.description: Block-end (bottom) padding, using the spacing scale. Overrides paddingBlock and padding on that edge only.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object.

bestPractices.text: Use Section for page-level grouping: settings panels, form groups, sidebar regions. These are sections of a page, not discrete items.
Start with the default variant. Use muted only to call attention to a specific region.
Add dividers between same-background sections that need separation.
Combine with a heading + Stack for a typical page section pattern.
Use Card when you mean Section. Cards are for discrete items (one notification, one profile). Sections are for page regions.

To center a Section, set marginInlineStart and marginInlineEnd to 'auto' in xstyle. If Astryx source is compiled in your app's own StyleX pass, the marginInline shorthand loses to Section's own inline margins.

anatomy.name: Section container
anatomy.description: Painted container that groups a page region.

anatomy.name: Consumer content
anatomy.description: Caller-provided content rendered inside the section container.

components.name: SegmentedControl
components.description: A segmented button group that allows users to make a single selection from a small set of mutually exclusive options. Use SegmentedControl when all options should be visible at once and the selection controls a value or mode, not page navigation. Under a finger, on a touch device (a coarse primary pointer), the selection slides to the new segment, whether a tap, an arrow key or a new value moved it; with Reduce Motion nothing travels: the old selection fades out as the new one fades in. There, pressing the selected segment lifts it, and dragging it carries the selection along with the selected label’s colour following it, and the segment under the finger is chosen when it lets go; a tap selects through the browser’s click; a pressed unselected segment shows the shared pressed overlay, and nothing dims. A drag that drifts off the control still chooses by its position along it. Going back to the selected segment, or Escape, changes nothing. With a mouse or a pen every change, a click included, slides on the theme’s duration and easing, and dragging the selected segment carries it as a finger does.

props.name: value
props.description: The currently selected value (controlled).

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when a segment is selected.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the radio group (used as aria-label, never rendered visually).

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant for the control.

props.name: layout
props.description: Layout mode. hug (default) sizes segments to content, capped at the container width (segment labels truncate when it is too narrow); fill stretches them equally to fill the container.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the entire control is disabled. The selected segment keeps the Tab stop, announced as disabled (aria-disabled), and nothing can be selected.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the control is disabled. Applies to the whole-group disabled state (isDisabled), not per segment. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus, and the reason describes each segment (selection stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled SegmentedControl in Tooltip, so the reason is attached to the control itself.

props.name: children
props.description: SegmentedControlItem children.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

bestPractices.text: Use for switching between 2–5 mutually exclusive views or modes where all options should be visible.
Provide a descriptive label for the control to ensure the group is accessible to screen readers.
Use for page-level navigation; use TabList instead. TabList is a navigation component, while SegmentedControl is an input that always has exactly one selected option.
Use for simple on/off states; use ToggleButton instead. ToggleButton can be toggled on or off independently, while SegmentedControl enforces a single selection from a group.
Wrap a disabled SegmentedControl in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; the reason is then not attached to the control or its segments. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

accessibility.name: Text label
accessibility.description: Each label must have at least 4.5:1 contrast with its segment background. Check unselected, Hover, Pointer down, and selected colors as they appear on screen. For Hover and Pointer down, measure the final background after the overlay is applied. The track is translucent, so label contrast depends on the background behind the control. Check the labels on every background the control sits on, including a custom page color.

accessibility.name: Essential icon
accessibility.description: When a segment has no visible label, its icon must have at least 3:1 contrast with the segment background. An icon beside a visible label does not need its own check.

accessibility.name: Selected state indicator
accessibility.description: The selected background must reach 3:1 only when users need it to tell selected from unselected. Label color and weight also show selection.

accessibility.name: Visible control boundary
accessibility.description: The control edge or segment borders need at least 3:1 contrast when users need them to see the choices.

accessibility.name: Keyboard focus indicator
accessibility.description: The focus outline must have at least 3:1 contrast with the area around the segment. Check it on the track and selected background.

accessibility.name: Disabled appearance
accessibility.description: Disabled controls do not need to meet these contrast ratios.

anatomy.name: Control
anatomy.description: Container for the mutually exclusive segment choices.

anatomy.name: Segment
anatomy.description: Individual choice within the control.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Visible text identifying a segment when its label is not hidden.

anatomy.name: Icon
anatomy.description: Optional caller-supplied icon shown inside a segment.

components.name: SegmentedControlItem
components.description: Individual segment item rendering as a radio button within the segmented control.

props.name: value
props.description: Unique value for this segment, matched against the parent value.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for this segment. Rendered as visible text unless isLabelHidden is true.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Whether the label is visually hidden. When true, only the icon is displayed and label is used as aria-label.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon element displayed before the label.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether this individual item is disabled. A disabled selected item keeps the control's Tab stop.

components.name: SelectableCard
components.description: A card that toggles between selected and unselected states with an accent border. For navigation use ClickableCard.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessibility label.

props.name: isSelected
props.description: Controlled selection state.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when toggled.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the card.

props.name: children
props.description: Card content.

props.name: padding
props.description: Inner padding.

props.name: variant
props.description: Background color variant.

props.name: elevation
props.description: Resting shadow depth. The selection ring composes on top, so a selected card keeps its shadow.

props.name: width
props.description: Card width.

props.name: height
props.description: Card height.

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: Maximum card width.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

bestPractices.text: Use for multi-select choices: filter chips, feature add-ons, or option grids where several can be on.
Use for multi-select groups; track the selected IDs in a Set.
When focused, toggle selection with Space or Enter.
Use for navigation; use ClickableCard for that.
Use for a single-select group: each card is a checkbox, so assistive technology announces a multi-select group with one tab stop per card.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: Interactive div with accent border on selection.

anatomy.name: Content
anatomy.description: Children rendered inside the card.

components.name: Selector
components.description: A dropdown selector for choosing a single value from a list of options. Supports labels, validation, descriptions, and required/optional states. Use it in forms and settings when presenting a moderate number of options. Keyboard typeahead matches a native select: typing on the focused closed trigger selects the matching option directly, repeated presses cycle through options sharing a first letter, and spaces count as match characters ("new y" reaches "New York"). With the menu open, typing moves the highlight and Enter commits. With hasSearch, typing on the closed trigger opens the popup and seeds the search input.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for accessibility.

props.name: options
props.description: Array of items: strings, objects with value/label/description/icon/disabled, dividers ({type: "divider"}), or sections ({type: "section", title, options}).

props.name: value
props.description: Currently selected value: a string, or undefined to show the placeholder; with hasClear, value is required and null means no selection. Without hasClear the type is string; with hasClear it is string | null.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the selected option value; it receives null only when hasClear is set and the user clears the selection. Without hasClear the type is (value: string) => void; with hasClear it is (value: string | null) => void, so a useState<string | null> setter fits.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action on change. Fires after onChange; the selector shows the new value and a busy state while it runs. Receives null on clear only with hasClear.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Shows a clear (×) button when a value is selected; with it, value becomes required and accepts null, and onChange receives null when the user clears the selection.

props.name: hasSearch
props.description: Whether to show a search input for filtering options. As the user types, the match count (or "No results found") is announced to screen readers via a polite live region. The search field has built-in affordances: a leading magnifier icon and, once a query is typed, a trailing clear (✕) button that resets the query and returns focus to the input.

props.name: searchPlaceholder
props.description: Placeholder text for the search input.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Content shown in the dropdown panel when there are no options to show, and announced in a polite live region when the panel opens. The announcement is the text this content renders, read from the DOM, so an element is announced as written and aria-hidden parts are left out of both. Not shown while isLoading.

props.name: emptySearchText
props.description: Content shown in the dropdown panel when a search query matches no options, and announced in a polite live region at the same time. The announcement is the text this content renders, read from the DOM, so an element is announced as written and aria-hidden parts are left out of both.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when no value is selected.

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant for the selector.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual trigger style. input is the bordered input treatment for forms; secondary matches the secondary buttons of the active theme (borderless and neutral-filled by default) for navs and toolbars; ghost is borderless and transparent, matching ghost buttons for toolbar usage.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the selector.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: Makes the selector read-only: the selected value stays visible, focusable, and included in form submission, and retains its combobox identity with aria-readonly. The selection surface, clear action, and disclosure indicator are removed. Unlike isDisabled, the control is not dimmed. isDisabled takes precedence when both are set.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: The HTML name attribute for form submissions. Renders a hidden input carrying the selected value, like a native select.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the selector is disabled. With isDisabled, shows the reason as a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus of the trigger, which stays focusable (aria-disabled) like every disabled selector; activation stays blocked. Use this instead of wrapping a disabled Selector in Tooltip.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text displayed below the label.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text displayed in an info icon at the end of the label.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Marks the field as optional.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Marks the field as required.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status with an optional message.

props.name: statusVariant
props.defaultValue: 'attached' for input selectors; 'detached' for secondary and ghost selectors
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the bordered input and is only valid for the input variant; secondary and ghost selectors detach attached status messages by default. Use tooltip for compact toolbar controls.

props.name: renderOption
props.description: Custom render function for each selectable option in the dropdown. Use this instead of JSX children; dividers and sections are rendered by the selector.

props.name: renderValue
props.description: Custom render function for the selected option inside the closed trigger. A one-line value follows the active size token, including compact or wide spacing scales with icons or a clear control. Padding accommodates the trigger line box, and each extra line grows the control by one line (28/32/36 for one line and 48/52/56 for two with the default tokens). Content inherits the trigger line height; content that sets a larger font should set its own line height so the trigger grows to fit it. Inside an InputGroup the group owns the row height: a SelectorOption folds onto one line and ellipsizes, and any taller node is cut off at the row.

props.name: indicatorPosition
props.description: Which logical edge of the option row carries a rendered selection mark. An empty mark consumes no space, so selected and unselected labels may shift or have different available width. end is the house convention shared with Typeahead and CommandPalette.

props.name: presentation
props.description: How the option list is presented. adaptive uses a bottom sheet on compact touch screens and an anchored popover otherwise.

props.name: placement
props.description: Position of the popup relative to the trigger. Omit it to place the selected option over the trigger, kept inside the viewport; with hasSearch, the popup then opens below the trigger. Set it for explicit layer positioning, such as placement="above" for a toolbar fixed to the bottom.

props.name: isDefaultOpen
props.description: Whether the dropdown starts open on mount. Useful for showcases and previews.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned. Without a width the field follows its displayed value and can shrink with its row (the value truncates) instead of overflowing it; use `<HStack wrap="wrap">` for filter bars so selectors move to a second line on phones.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon displayed at the start of the selector trigger; pass a built-in meaning such as 'search' (see `astryx docs icons`), an icon component, or an icon element.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Shows a loading spinner in the trigger.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler on the trigger button. Runs before the selector toggles its surface; preventDefault() does not keep it closed.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Focus handler on the trigger button. Runs before the selector's own focus handling.

props.name: onKeyDown
props.description: Key handler on the trigger button. Runs after the built-in keyboard model and is skipped for keys it handles and cancels.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the element that paints the border and background and holds the value, icons, and end controls. Never the trigger button itself.

bestPractices.text: Provide a visible label so users understand what they are selecting.
Use sections and dividers to organize options when the list exceeds ~8 items.
Use renderOption for custom option rows. Do not pass SelectorOption directly as JSX children.
Set a meaningful placeholder that hints at the expected selection (e.g. "Choose a country" not "Select...").
Use inside InputGroup only when the selector needs a short prefix or suffix addon as part of one decorated input surface.

Use variant="secondary" when a selector sits in a nav or toolbar beside secondary buttons or a segmented control, so it shares their treatment instead of reading as a form field. Use variant="ghost" when a selector sits in a toolbar with ghost buttons. If validation status is needed there, prefer statusVariant="tooltip" so the toolbar height stays compact.
Use presentation="adaptive" when the selector should become a bottom sheet on compact touch screens.
Use for action menus; use Dropdown Menu for triggering commands or navigation.
Use when there are only two options; use a SegmentedControl or radio buttons instead.
Use Selector for navigation; links should be links, not dropdown options.
Use for yes/no or on/off choices; use Switch or CheckboxInput instead.
Put more than ~20 options without sections; consider Typeahead for large lists.

anatomy.name: Trigger clear button
anatomy.description: Shared clear action that removes the selected value when hasClear is enabled.

anatomy.name: Status icon

anatomy.name: Indicator icon
anatomy.description: Trailing chevron shown when status presentation does not replace it; reflects collapsed or expanded state.

anatomy.description: Panel header with a borderless search input and optional clear action.
