anatomy.name: Search clear button
anatomy.description: Shared clear action shown in the search row while a query is present.

components.name: SelectorOption
components.description: Helper component for custom item rendering inside an Selector renderOption prop.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary label text for the item.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon displayed before the label; pass a built-in meaning such as 'search' (see `astryx docs icons`), an icon component, or an icon element.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary description text displayed below the label.

props.name: layout
props.description: How the label and description sit together. 'stacked' puts the description on its own line; 'inline' keeps both on one line so the row fits a fixed-height host. Inside a Selector trigger the trigger's padding sizes itself to whichever layout you pick, so both land on the 4px rhythm; an InputGroup pins the row height and forces 'inline'.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Additional content rendered after the label and description.

components.name: SideNav
components.description: A sidebar navigation component for organizing application pages with sections, nested items, and icons. Use SideNav as the primary navigation when an app has 5 or more destinations or requires hierarchical grouping.

props.name: header
props.description: Header area (typically SideNavHeading). Sticky.

props.name: topContent
props.description: Content below the header, e.g., a create button.

props.name: children
props.description: Navigation sections and items. Scrollable.

props.name: footer
props.description: Footer area above the icon bar.

props.name: footerIcons
props.description: Footer icon bar. The row cascades a 'sm' size to the interactive children it contains, so its icons and the built-in collapse button come out one height; pass an explicit size on a child to opt out.

props.name: collapsible
props.type: boolean | { defaultIsCollapsed?: boolean; isCollapsed?: boolean; onCollapsedChange?: (isCollapsed: boolean) => void; hasButton?: boolean; buttonLabel?: string }
props.description: Enables collapse behavior. true for uncontrolled with default toggle button, or an object for controlled mode and advanced config (defaultIsCollapsed, isCollapsed + onCollapsedChange, hasButton, buttonLabel). A controlled config can also be passed to a SideNavCollapseButton rendered outside this SideNav, so both share one state.

props.name: resizable
props.type: boolean | { defaultWidth?: number; minWidth?: number; maxWidth?: number; autoSaveId?: string; onWidthChange?: (width: number) => void; defaultIsCollapsed?: boolean; isCollapsed?: boolean; onCollapseChange?: (isCollapsed: boolean) => void } | ResizableRegion
props.description: Enables a resize handle at the inline-end edge. true for defaults (260px initial, 180-480px range), or a ResizableConfig object (defaultWidth, minWidth, maxWidth, autoSaveId for localStorage persistence of width and collapse state, onWidthChange). It can also own collapse state (defaultIsCollapsed, isCollapsed + onCollapseChange); when both props carry collapse state, resizable wins and a dev warning names the conflicting keys. It also takes the output of useResizable(), whose axis ('horizontal' | 'vertical') must be 'horizontal': that region then owns the width and the collapse state, so the rail follows its isCollapsed, the toggle calls its collapse and expand, and its autoSaveId saves the width. With the hook's output, the region's own collapsible option also decides whether the rail collapses; a collapsible prop that disagrees, or the collapse state it sets, is ignored, with a dev warning. The handle is hidden while collapsed.

props.name: handleRef
props.description: Deprecated. Imperative collapse handle for SideNavCollapseButton instances rendered outside this SideNav; hand both the same controlled collapsible config instead. Separate from `ref`, which continues to expose the root HTMLElement.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

bestPractices.text: Use sections to group related navigation items and help users scan for their destination.
Pair outline and filled icon variants so the selected state is visually distinct.
Mark the current page with isSelected: it sets aria-current="page", so the current destination is announced rather than carried by color alone.

SideNav renders a navigation landmark, and a collapsible item follows the WAI-ARIA APG Disclosure pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/): the toggle carries aria-expanded and aria-controls, and the group it owns is inert while collapsed. Keep item labels short; they name icon-only items unless a meaningful aria-label supplies more context.

While the nav is collapsed, an item with children shows them in a submenu flyout. On a device that can hover, pointing at the item opens it after a short delay and moving away closes it; a flyout opened by clicking stays open until it is dismissed. On touch, it opens on tap. Do not put an action in there that has no other route to it.
Include a SideNavHeading when a TopNav is already providing app identity; this duplicates branding.
Use for filtering content; use tabs or filter buttons instead.

props.name: collapsible

props.name: handleRef

bestPractices.text: Match the size and shape of the content being loaded to create a realistic placeholder.
Stagger multiple skeletons with the `index` prop for a natural wave animation.
Use when the content dimensions are unknown; use Spinner instead.
Combine with a Spinner on the same content area; pick one loading pattern.
Show skeletons indefinitely; if loading takes too long, show an error or empty state instead.

anatomy.name: Placeholder
anatomy.description: Painted shape that stands in for content while it loads.

components.name: Slider
components.description: A draggable control for selecting a numeric value or range within defined bounds. Supports single value and range selection, tick marks, custom value formatting, and vertical orientation. Use it when users need to explore a continuous range, such as volume, price, or percentage. Under a finger, on any touch device, it tracks as UISlider does: only the thumb takes a drag, through a target larger than it, the value follows the finger’s travel rather than jumping to it, a release coasts on before `onChangeEnd`, a swipe from the track scrolls the page, and a tap on the track or a mark sets the value when the finger lifts (the thumb springs there). A mouse drag on a thumb tracks the same way, past the same 10 px in any direction, with no lift or coast; a mouse press on the track moves the thumb there, and only a primary click presses. A pen drags as a finger does, claiming only along the track, and its drag ends at the release with no coast. A wheel or a trackpad scroll over the slider goes to whatever scrolls under it.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text (always rendered for accessibility).

props.name: value
props.description: Current value: a `number` for single thumb mode or `[number, number]` for range mode.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired on value change during drag.

props.name: onChangeEnd
props.description: Callback fired when drag ends.

props.name: min
props.description: Minimum value.

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum value.

props.name: step
props.description: Step increment.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Orientation of the slider.

props.name: formatValue
props.description: Custom value formatting function used for display and `aria-valuetext`.

props.name: valueDisplay
props.description: How the current value is displayed.

props.name: marks
props.description: Tick marks at specified positions with optional labels. Unfilled marks use the track color; marks inside the filled region (at or behind the thumb, or between the thumbs in range mode) use the fill color.

props.name: minStepsBetweenThumbs
props.description: Minimum number of steps between thumbs in range mode; prevents thumbs from overlapping.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the slider is disabled.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: The HTML name attribute for form submissions. Renders hidden inputs carrying the current value (two entries in range mode).

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the slider is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the thumb focusable via aria-disabled (value changes stay blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled Slider in Tooltip. Disabled controls swallow the hover events an external Tooltip needs.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Whether the field is optional.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Whether the field is required.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Whether to visually hide the label.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text rendered below the label.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator object (`{ type, message }`) for validation feedback.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text for an info icon displayed next to the label.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the element that paints the border and background and holds icons and end controls. Never the native input.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Class name for the visual control box.

props.name: controlStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the visual control box.

bestPractices.text: Always provide a label, even if visually hidden, so the slider is accessible to screen readers.
Format values with meaningful units like "$50" or "75%" instead of raw numbers.
Use for precise numeric entry; pair with a text input or use NumberInput instead.
Set a step size so large that only a few positions are possible; use SegmentedControl or radio buttons instead.
Wrap a disabled slider in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

accessibility.name: Thumb
accessibility.description: The thumb must have at least 3:1 contrast with the track and the surface behind it. Pointer down is the whole drag: measure the thumb with the pressed overlay applied.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Text identifying the numeric setting controlled by the slider.

anatomy.name: Description
anatomy.description: Helper text between the label and the slider control.

anatomy.name: Slider
anatomy.description: Control row containing the track, thumb or thumbs, and optional text value.

anatomy.name: Interactive control
anatomy.description: Pointer and keyboard interaction surface containing the rail, fill, marks, and thumbs.

anatomy.name: Track
anatomy.description: Background rail representing the available numeric range.

anatomy.name: Filled range
anatomy.description: Accent segment from the minimum to a single value, or between two range values.

anatomy.name: Tick mark
anatomy.description: Position marker supplied through the marks collection.

anatomy.name: Mark label
anatomy.description: Optional text displayed beside a tick mark.

anatomy.name: Thumb
anatomy.description: Draggable value indicator; range mode renders a minimum and maximum thumb.

anatomy.name: Value display
anatomy.description: Formatted current value shown beside the slider when valueDisplay is text.

components.name: Spinner
components.description: An animated loading indicator for processes with unknown duration, such as data fetching or form submission. Supports visible labels, multiple sizes, and a dark background variant. For content with known dimensions, use Skeleton instead.

props.name: size
props.description: Spinner size: ring diameter (10px, 14px, 18px, 28px).

props.name: shade
props.description: Color shade for light or dark backgrounds.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible content below the spinner. A string label names the indicator through aria-labelledby.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name for screen readers. Defaults to label (if string) or a translated "Loading" from the i18n catalog.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

bestPractices.text: Provide a meaningful label to describe what is loading for screen reader users.
Use the "onMedia" shade when placed on dark or accent-colored backgrounds.
Use for content areas with known dimensions; use Skeleton to preserve layout instead.
Stack multiple spinners in the same view; use one to represent the overall loading state.

components.name: Stack
components.description: Stack arranges items in a row or column with consistent spacing. Use the gap prop to control the space between items.

bestPractices.text: Use the gap prop for spacing between items; don't add margins manually.
Use StackItem with size="fill" to make one item stretch and fill the leftover space.
Nest stacks inside stacks; try wrap="wrap" first to let items flow to the next line.

anatomy.name: Stack container
anatomy.description: Layout container that arranges content along one flex axis.

anatomy.name: Item
anatomy.description: Optional StackItem wrapper that controls one item in the stack.

anatomy.name: Content
anatomy.description: Caller-supplied content rendered by a Stack or StackItem.

components.name: StatusDot
components.description: A small colored dot that communicates status like online/offline presence or severity levels. Supports five semantic variants and an optional pulse animation. Always pair with a visible text label, as color alone should not carry meaning.

props.name: variant
props.description: Semantic color variant.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label surfaced via aria-label.

props.name: isPulsing
props.description: Enables a pulse animation; respects prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Tooltip text shown on hover to explain the status meaning.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon rendered centered inside the dot, painted in currentColor (the variant's ink). Gives the status a non-color mark, so use a different icon per status. Booleans and empty strings are ignored, so `cond && <Icon />` is safe. Same contract as AvatarStatusDot.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

bestPractices.text: Use StatusDot as a binary present/absent signal; avoid encoding many distinct states in a single dot, since color and size alone cannot reliably distinguish them.
Always pair with a visible text label so status is not conveyed by color alone.
Provide a descriptive `label` prop for screen reader accessibility.
Pair the dot with an icon that carries the status as a distinct shape when it must stand on its own without adjacent text, so meaning survives without color.
If you can't add a label or an icon, make sure the status is conveyed elsewhere accessibly (e.g. adjacent text, a table column, or a live region).

Rely on color alone to communicate status; StatusDot is not fully accessible in isolation, so the builder must make the status distinguishable in context via a label, an icon, or an accessible alternative.
Use the pulse animation for purely decorative purposes; reserve it for states that require immediate attention.

anatomy.name: Dot
anatomy.description: Painted status dot that carries the selected semantic variant.

anatomy.name: Status icon
anatomy.description: Optional caller-supplied icon rendered inside the dot.

components.name: Step
components.description: Individual step within a Stepper. Renders a progress-bar segment, an indicator, and a label with optional description. Progress (completed/active/not-started) is derived from the parent Stepper's activeStep and this step's step index.

props.name: step
props.description: Zero-based index of this step. Used to derive progress (completed/active/not-started) relative to the parent activeStep.

props.name: label
props.description: Step label text. Kept to a single line and ellipsized when the step is narrower than the label, so a row of horizontal steps stays the same height and the track under them stays straight. The full string is still read out as part of the step, so a truncated label costs nothing in the accessible name — but short labels survive narrow layouts better.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional description shown below the label for additional context.

props.name: children
props.description: Content rendered below the label and description. Useful in vertical steppers for form fields or detailed step content. In a compact horizontal Stepper, the content remains mounted to preserve local state while it is hidden with the expanded step details.

props.name: status
props.description: Semantic color for the step. Controls color only and maps to the global Astryx semantic tokens. Leave unset for the progress-derived default coloring.

props.name: indicator
props.description: What to show as the step indicator. 'auto' shows a number until completed then a check, 'number' always shows a numbered badge, 'none' hides it, or pass any ReactNode (e.g. an Icon) for a fully custom indicator.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables interaction and dims the step indicator and label.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Marks the step as optional, appending an "Optional" affordance after the label.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Trailing content rendered at the end of the label row.

props.name: density
props.description: Controls vertical padding of the step. Falls back to the stepper-level density when unset.

components.name: Stepper
components.description: Steppers display progress through a sequence of logical and numbered steps. Use them for multi-step workflows like forms, onboarding flows, or checkout processes where users need to see their position and the steps ahead. Rendered as an ordered list (not a navigation landmark).

bestPractices.text: Keep step labels short and descriptive: "Payment" not "Enter your payment information".

Use the vertical orientation when steps carry longer descriptions. A horizontal stepper handles narrow containers itself: once the frame gives each step less than horizontalOptions.minimumStepWidth (112px by default) it drops the labels for a segmented track and uses the configured collapsedVariant beneath it.

Set horizontalOptions.collapsedVariant to 'withLabel' when the page already supplies Back/Continue, or to 'hiddenLabel' when surrounding UI owns both the current-step heading and navigation and only a bare progress track is needed.
Provide onStepClick for non-linear workflows where users may need to revisit earlier steps.
Use status only to apply a semantic color (accent/success/warning/error); pass a custom icon for richer indicators.
Use a stepper for fewer than 3 steps; a simple heading or progress bar works better.
Use more than 7 steps; consider grouping related steps or using a different pattern.

anatomy.name: Stepper
anatomy.description: The ordered list holding the steps. Owns the orientation and the indicator placement the whole flow is laid out on.

anatomy.name: Frame
anatomy.description: The layout frame that groups the ordered steps with the optional compact summary shown at narrow widths.

anatomy.name: Compact summary
anatomy.description: The optional row a horizontal Stepper adds directly beneath the track once it is too narrow to label every step. horizontalOptions.collapsedVariant chooses a label with Previous/Next controls, the label alone, or no row for a bare progress track. The on-track layout keeps its indicators on the rail instead of repeating the active indicator beside the label. Every step keeps its name in the accessible sequence at any width.

anatomy.name: Step
anatomy.description: One step in the flow, and the element carrying its status. Wraps the indicator, label, description, and the track segments belonging to it.

anatomy.name: Progress bar
anatomy.description: A 4px segmented bar per step. Filled for completed and active steps. Advancing one step grows the fill along the track it just covered, so the movement reads as progress rather than a bar changing color. Every other change applies at once: going back, jumping forward by more than one step, mounting mid-flow, and any change at all under prefers-reduced-motion. Where a span is drawn by more than one segment (the on-track layouts split it between two steps, three when a content slot sits between them), the segments run in track order at one constant speed, so the fill reads as a single line growing rather than pieces lighting in turn.

anatomy.name: Connector
anatomy.description: The track drawn between indicators in the on-track layouts. Each connector paints an unfilled line and, over it, the accent fill covering the progress made. How many pieces a connector is drawn from is an implementation detail of the layout, not a themeable part; use --step-connector-gap to hold the track off the indicator.

anatomy.name: Indicator
anatomy.description: A numbered badge, a check, or any custom icon. Controlled via the indicator prop.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Text identifying the step.

anatomy.name: Description
anatomy.description: Supporting text below the label with additional context.

components.name: Switch
components.description: A toggle control for on/off states that take effect immediately. Supports labels, descriptions, loading states, and validation. Use it for settings or preferences that apply instantly. For changes requiring a form submission, use a checkbox instead. Under a finger it moves like the iOS switch on every touch screen: a press lifts the thumb, a drag across flips it, lifting the finger commits, and a tap toggles through the browser’s click. The thumb keeps its circle and size on every device, and under a coarse pointer the invisible hit area grows toward 44 × 44 px, stopping halfway to any neighbouring control so a tap goes to the nearer one. With reduced motion on, a change cross-fades on a touch screen and is immediate with a mouse.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the underlying <input> element.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the switch (always rendered for accessibility).

props.name: value
props.description: Whether the switch is on or off.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the switch state changes.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action fired after onChange. Triggers optimistic UI and shows a loading spinner until the promise resolves.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Whether the switch is in a loading state, showing a spinner inside the thumb.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible to screen readers.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed below the label.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the switch is disabled.

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant controlling track and thumb dimensions. sm (32x20px) matches sm checkbox/radio vertical rhythm; md (40x24px, default) matches md checkbox/radio vertical rhythm.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: The HTML name attribute for the underlying checkbox input, useful for form submissions (submits "on" when the switch is on).

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the switch is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the switch focusable via aria-disabled (toggling stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled Switch in Tooltip. Disabled controls swallow the hover events an external Tooltip needs.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Whether the field is optional. Mutually exclusive with isRequired.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Whether the switch is required. Mutually exclusive with isOptional.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator with type and message. Displays a colored message box below the switch and sets aria-invalid when type is "error".

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Callback fired when the switch receives focus.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Callback fired when the switch loses focus.

props.name: labelIcon
props.description: Icon displayed before the label text; pass a built-in meaning such as 'search' (see `astryx docs icons`), an icon component, or an icon element.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text shown in an info icon at the end of the label.

props.name: labelPosition
props.description: Which side of the switch the label appears on. "start" places the label before the switch.

props.name: labelSpacing
props.description: Spacing behavior between label and switch. "hug" places them next to each other; "spread" pushes them to opposite ends of the container (full width).

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

bestPractices.text: Use for settings that apply immediately; the toggle should take effect without a separate save action.
Pair with a clear, concise label that describes the setting being controlled.
Use for options that require a form submission to take effect; use a checkbox instead.
Use a switch for multi-state values; it's strictly on/off.
Wrap a disabled switch in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

accessibility.name: Track and thumb
accessibility.description: The on and off tracks must each have at least 3:1 contrast with the surface behind them, and the thumb with its track. For Hover and Pointer down, measure the final colors after the tint and the pressed overlay are applied.

anatomy.name: Field
anatomy.description: Container arranging the switch, label, and feedback.

anatomy.name: Track
anatomy.description: Pill-shaped surface that shows the off or on state.

anatomy.name: Thumb
anatomy.description: Indicator that moves across the track when state changes.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Text identifying the setting controlled by the switch.

anatomy.name: Description
anatomy.description: Helper text below the label.

anatomy.name: Spinner
anatomy.description: Loading indicator shown inside the thumb while busy.

anatomy.name: Status message
anatomy.description: Error, warning, or success message below the switch.

components.name: SyntaxTheme
components.description: Applies syntax highlighting colors to CodeBlock and any code component in the subtree. By default, code components use the theme-level syntax colors (set via defineTheme({ syntax: ... })), which derive from the palette (--color-text-accent for keywords, --color-text-green for strings, etc.). SyntaxTheme lets you override those per-region. The system uses 14 semantic tokens (keyword, string, comment, number, function, type, variable, operator, constant, tag, attribute, property, punctuation, background) validated against 11 community themes. Custom themes are created with defineSyntaxTheme() and can use [light, dark] tuples for automatic color-scheme adaptation. Built-in presets: oneDarkPro, dracula, monokai, nord, tokyoNight, catppuccinMocha, githubLight, githubDark, solarizedLight, oneLight (import from @astryxdesign/core/theme/syntax).

props.name: theme
props.description: Syntax highlighting theme: a preset from @astryxdesign/core/theme/syntax or a custom theme created with defineSyntaxTheme().

props.name: children
props.description: Content subtree. All CodeBlock components within will use this syntax theme.

bestPractices.text: Use the syntax field in defineTheme() for app-wide code styling. Use SyntaxTheme only when a specific section needs a different look.
Pick from built-in presets or create a custom theme with defineSyntaxTheme() for brand-specific colors.
Syntax themes support light-dark() tuples: each token can have different values for light and dark mode, resolved automatically by the color scheme.
For a single CodeBlock, pass the syntaxTheme prop directly: it is shorthand for wrapping that block in SyntaxTheme. Use the SyntaxTheme wrapper when theming a whole region of code components.

components.name: Tab
components.description: Individual tab item that renders as a button or an anchor link, with selected-state styling and optional icons.

props.name: value
props.description: Unique value for this tab, matched against TabListContext.value.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for this tab. Used as visible text by default, or as aria-label when isLabelHidden is true.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Whether the label is visually hidden. When true, only the icon and endContent are displayed, and label is used as aria-label for accessibility.

props.name: href
props.description: URL to navigate to; when provided, the tab renders as an anchor element. Ignored in a TabList given an explicit role="tablist".

props.name: panelId
props.description: Id of the panel this tab controls, wired up as aria-controls where the TabList speaks the tabs pattern. Put the same id on the panel element. No effect under the navigation pattern, and a development warning says so.

props.name: as
props.description: Custom component to render instead of <a> for link tabs. Overrides the LinkProvider default. Only applies when href is provided.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon element shown when the tab is not selected.

props.name: selectedIcon
props.description: Icon element shown when the tab is selected; falls back to icon if not provided.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content rendered after the label, such as a badge count or status dot. The tab is one button, so endContent holds only non-interactive content: no button, link, InfoTip, or other focusable control. To explain a tab, anchor a Tooltip on the Tab through its ref, render it after the TabList, and put a decorative info Icon here.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

components.name: Table
components.description: Table displays structured data in rows and columns with consistent dimensionality. It supports rich cell content, sorting, selection, pagination, and column management through a composable plugin system. Use Table for data sets with uniform structure; for simpler or inconsistent data, consider a list or card layout instead.

props.name: data
props.description: Array of data items to render as rows. T must extend Record<string, unknown> (use `interface MyRow extends Record<string, unknown>` for custom types).

props.name: columns
props.description: Column definitions: each column has {key, header, width?, align?, renderCell?}, and Table has no onRowClick prop; the supported way to open a dialog, side panel or detail page from a row is a Link or Button in the row's main cell (renderCell) that opens it, and to show a row's details inline on a click anywhere on it, use useTableRowExpansion with hasRowClickExpansion; on a phone, column floors wider than the screen scroll sideways, so for a phone-first page also render one List with `hasDividers` (not a Card per item) and switch with a StyleX `display` rule under `@media` (Best practices). The `header` field sets the column heading text. If omitted, columns are auto-generated from data object keys. The `width` field is typed as `ColumnWidth` (not a number); use `proportional(n)` or `pixel(n)` helpers imported from `@astryxdesign/core/Table`. Omitting `width` keeps an equal flexible share with a compact 60px readability floor. To give one column a different floor, set `width: proportional(1, {minWidth: 80})`; its `minWidth` replaces the 60px floor for that column. Example: `width: pixel(120)` for 120px fixed, `width: proportional(1)` for a flexible column with a 120px default minimum.

props.name: idKey
props.description: Canonical row identity: a property name projects valid strings and finite numbers to strings; a function retains string/number type. Optional legacy tables fall back to index. Virtualization requires explicit unique valid keys.

props.name: density
props.description: Row density controlling cell padding and font size.

props.name: dividers
props.description: Divider style rendered between cells.

props.name: isStriped
props.description: Stripes alternate rows (every other row, zebra striping): a background wash on the even-numbered body and footer rows. A theme restyles either stripe of a data-driven table through the `table-row` target's `parity` (odd or even); every row a striped table may stripe (body and footer rows, not the header row) carries the `striped` state. A pinned column (`useTableStickyColumns`) follows the row's stripe.

props.name: hasHover
props.description: Applies a hover highlight background to rows on pointer devices.

props.name: verticalAlign
props.description: Vertical alignment for body row cells. Controls `vertical-align` on the `<td>` elements.

props.name: textOverflow
props.description: How cell text behaves when it exceeds the column width. 'wrap' lets text wrap and the row grow taller; 'truncate' clips with an ellipsis (default-rendered cells show a tooltip on hover when truncated). Header cells follow the same mode: under 'wrap' a long heading wraps in a data-driven table, and in children mode its column grows to keep it on one line. When you pass `columns`, a data-driven table sizes them from their definitions, not their content, so under 'wrap' a token longer than its column, such as a code identifier or a URL, breaks inside the token where the line ends. To keep such tokens whole, give that column a floor that fits them, or compose the table in children mode, whose columns follow their content.

props.name: virtualization
props.description: Geometry-only capability from useTableRowsVirtualization or useTableColumnsVirtualization, or a list with at most one of each; any other list renders without windowing. useTableColumnsVirtualization({initialViewportWidth}) mounts only the unpinned columns near the viewport. useTableRowsVirtualization({rowHeight, initialViewportHeight}) takes sizes that are both positive finite CSS pixels; the Table scrolls inside the height its parent gives it, and initialViewportHeight only sizes the first window. Give the Table's parent a height, fixed or relative, or a flex child, so windowing can bound the rows; with no height every row renders. Pass complete flat data and an explicit idKey. Default text truncates; custom renderers, wrapping, structural plugins, incompatible offsets, invalid identity or unrepresentable geometry use full rendering. Logical row positions include the header.

props.name: plugins
props.description: Named plugins: the objects that the useTable* hooks return, or your own TablePlugin<T> (import the type from @astryxdesign/core/Table), an object of optional transform functions. When the table renders, Table calls transformColumns, transformTable, transformHeaderCell for each header cell, transformHeaderRow, transformScrollWrapper, and then transformTableContext in reverse plugin order, so the first plugin wraps outermost. With column virtualization, transformHeaderCell and transformHeaderRow run after transformScrollWrapper and transformTableContext, because the header renders inside the column window. Then, as each body row renders, Table calls transformBodyRow for that row and then transformBodyCell for each of its cells. Their arguments and results: transformColumns(columns) adds, removes, or reorders columns; transformTable(props) changes the <table> props; transformHeaderCell(props, column, columnIndex, columns) changes a <th>, with slots before, content, after, overlay, and below; transformHeaderRow(props) changes the header <tr>; transformBodyCell(props, column, item, columnIndex, columns, context) changes a <td>; transformBodyRow(props, item, index, context) changes a body <tr>, and can add afterRow content below the row; transformScrollWrapper(props, context) changes the scroll region and can add beforeTable or afterTable content; transformTableContext(children) wraps the table in providers. The element transforms (table, header row, header cell, body row, body cell, scroll wrapper) receive {htmlProps, xstyle, ...} and must return the same shape, with the earlier values kept. Header and body cell transforms can also append contextMenuActions for a right-click menu. A plugin that has transformBodyRow or transformBodyCell and keeps one row per data item must set rowModel: 'flat'; without it, row virtualization uses full rendering and Table ignores plugin loading state (renderState). Keep each plugin object stable (create it in useMemo): a new object on each render renders all rows again. Plugins with the first-party names columnSettings, sort, tree, selection, and pagination run in that order; other names run after them, in record order.

props.name: rowIndexStart
props.description: ARIA row index (1-based) for the first rendered body row. The row ordinal is an accessibility concern independent of any visible index column, so setting this (or rowCount) makes the table emit aria-rowindex on body rows and aria-rowcount on the table. For a paginated/windowed view, pass the offset of the first visible row (e.g. (page - 1) * pageSize + 1) so aria-rowindex reflects position in the full dataset. Data-driven mode only.

props.name: rowCount
props.description: Total number of body rows across all pages/windows, used for aria-rowcount so assistive tech can announce "row X of Y" against the full dataset. When omitted but rowIndexStart is set (windowed view with an unknown total), aria-rowcount is set to -1 per the ARIA unknown-count convention. Data-driven mode only.

props.name: emptyState
props.description: Content that shows when data is an empty array, for example an EmptyState that says no rows match the filters. It renders in one row across all columns. Omit it for a compact "No data" EmptyState. Pass false for an empty body. Table does not know why data is empty: choose the content from your own state, for example "No results" when filters are active and "No users yet" when they are not.

props.name: children
props.description: Children mode: compose the table yourself from TableHeader / TableBody / TableFooter, each holding TableRow and TableCell, instead of using data-driven rendering. The children are passed straight to the <table>, so the section is yours to supply. A TableRow placed directly in Table emits <table><tr>, which is invalid HTML and mismatches on hydration (the parser inserts an implied <tbody> for server-rendered markup; React does not on the client). Data-driven mode renders the sections for you.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

bestPractices.text: Use density and divider variants to match the information density and scanning needs of your data.
Compose rich cell content with Astryx components like Text, StatusDot, and Avatar via renderCell. Pair a StatusDot with Text, and keep a solid Badge for the rare cell that needs attention.

Do not put a control (a button, link, or input) in the header of a sortable column. The Sort control wraps the whole header, so the control nests inside it and assistive technology cannot operate it. Keep header controls on columns that are not sortable.

In children mode, put every row inside TableHeader, TableBody, or TableFooter. <table> cannot contain a <tr> directly: the HTML parser inserts an implied <tbody> for server-rendered markup and React does not on the client, so unwrapped rows mismatch on hydration.

Omit width for equal flexible columns with a compact 60px readability floor. Give one column its own floor with proportional(1, {minWidth}), weight columns with proportional(n), and fix widths with pixel(); the Table scroll region activates when the combined floors no longer fit.

Use the data-driven API from React Server Components: proportional(), pixel(), and column definitions without function props are server-safe. Columns using renderCell (or any function prop) need the table wrapped in a "use client" component, since functions cannot cross the server-client boundary.

To open a row (go to a detail page, open a side panel), put a Link or a Button in the row's main cell with renderCell. Table has no row-click prop. A click handler on the <tr> cannot be reached with the keyboard or a screen reader, so do not use it as the only way to open a row. A renderCell column makes a windowed Table (virtualization) render every row.
When filters or a search can leave no rows, set emptyState to say so and offer a way out, for example an EmptyState with a "Clear filters" Button.

Keep long tokens such as code identifiers whole. When you pass `columns`, a data-driven table sizes them from their definitions, not their content, so a token that does not fit its column breaks inside the token. Give that column proportional(1, {minWidth}) or pixel() wide enough for the token, or compose the table in children mode, whose columns follow their content.

When you pass `columns`, floors set with `minWidth` or `pixel()` are minimums and cell content never widens a column, except that a windowed table’s numbering column fits its largest number (only children mode sizes columns to content). When the floors add up to more than the screen, the table scrolls sideways on a phone: the columns past the edge stay out of sight until the reader swipes.

For a page read mostly on phones, show the data as a List below a breakpoint instead of a wide table. Render both the List and the Table, and switch them with a StyleX `display` rule, for example `display: {default: 'none', '@media (not (min-width: 768px))': 'block'}` on the List’s wrapper and the reverse on the Table’s, below the theme’s `md` breakpoint (768px by default, or your theme’s own `md`). CSS picks the layout in the first paint and without script; `useMediaQuery` picks it only after the page’s script runs.
Use a table for data without consistent columns. Use a list or card layout for heterogeneous content.

anatomy.name: Table
anatomy.description: Semantic table element that groups the table sections, rows, and cells.

anatomy.name: Scroll region
anatomy.description: Outer region that scrolls horizontally when columns overflow. Fixed-height virtualization also enables block scrolling; the region enters keyboard order while either applicable axis overflows.

anatomy.name: Header section
anatomy.description: Column-heading section generated when data-driven columns are present or supplied with TableHeader in children mode.

anatomy.name: Column header cell
anatomy.description: Cell that identifies one column and may contain sorting or bulk-selection controls.

anatomy.name: Sort control
anatomy.description: Button that wraps a sortable column label and changes that column's sort direction.

anatomy.name: Sort indicator glyph
anatomy.description: Directional symbol rendered by Icon inside a Sort control.

anatomy.name: Sort priority
anatomy.description: Number shown for a sorted column when multi-column sorting is active.

anatomy.name: Selection control
anatomy.description: CheckboxInput rendered in the header and selectable body rows by the selection plugin.

anatomy.name: Body section
anatomy.description: Section containing data rows or the current empty state; data-driven mode renders it automatically.

anatomy.name: Row
anatomy.description: Repeated TableRow that groups cells in a standard header, body, or footer row.

components.name: TableBody
components.description: <tbody> wrapper for children mode. Holds the data rows. A row must sit inside a section: <table> cannot contain a <tr> directly, because the HTML parser inserts an implied <tbody> when it parses server-rendered markup and React does not when it renders on the client, so rows written straight into Table mismatch on hydration. The data-driven data={...} mode renders this element itself; in children mode it is yours to supply.

props.name: children
props.description: The <tbody> rows.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

components.name: TableCell
components.description: <td> wrapper that reads TableContext to apply density padding, font size, and divider borders when used inside Table.

props.name: children
props.description: Cell content.

components.name: TableFooter
components.description: <tfoot> wrapper for children mode. Holds summary or total rows beneath the body. A row must sit inside a section: <table> cannot contain a <tr> directly, because the HTML parser inserts an implied <tbody> when it parses server-rendered markup and React does not when it renders on the client, so the two trees mismatch on hydration. Children mode only: the data-driven data={...} path renders a header and a body, never a footer.

props.name: children
props.description: The <tfoot> rows.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

components.name: TableHeader
components.description: <thead> wrapper for children mode. Holds the header row, whose cells are TableHeaderCell. A row must sit inside a section: <table> cannot contain a <tr> directly, because the HTML parser inserts an implied <tbody> when it parses server-rendered markup and React does not when it renders on the client, so the two trees mismatch on hydration. The data-driven data={...} mode renders this element itself whenever columns are supplied; in children mode it is yours to supply.

props.name: children
props.description: The <thead> rows.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

components.name: TableHeaderCell
components.description: <th> wrapper that reads TableContext to apply density padding, semibold weight, secondary text color, and divider borders when used inside Table.

props.name: children
props.description: Header cell content.

components.name: TableRow
components.description: <tr> wrapper that reads TableContext to apply striped, hover, and divider styles when used inside Table.

props.name: children
props.description: Row cell elements.

components.name: TableSelectionToolbar
components.description: Pass both outputs of useTableSelectionState to their matching consumers: selectionConfig to useTableSelection and selectionState to TableSelectionToolbar. An app that keeps its own selection, such as every row matching a query across server pages, passes its own config and state instead. Render product actions through startContent. Keep fixed or floating placement in the surrounding layout.

props.name: selection
props.description: Shared selection state: selectedKeys, selectedCount, hasSelection, and clearSelection. Usually useTableSelectionState returns it; an app that keeps its own selection builds it.

props.name: startContent
props.description: Product-owned action controls aligned to the logical start. Child controls inherit the toolbar size.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the action surface.

props.name: renderSelectionLabel
props.description: Overrides the visible count text for localisation or domain-specific copy.

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: Visible label for the command that clears the complete controlled selection.

props.name: size
props.description: Toolbar size. Cascades to product action controls and the clear action.

props.name: variant
props.description: Toolbar surface variant.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: Caller-owned layout styles, including sticky positioning for floating compositions.

bestPractices.text: Pass selectionState directly from useTableSelectionState so the count and clear action stay synchronized with row selection, unless the app keeps its own selection across server pages.
Provide product actions as startContent instead of encoding them as configuration objects.
Inject the toolbar through the Table plugin or its horizontal scroll wrapper.

components.name: TabList
components.description: TabList provides tab-style navigation for organizing content into categorized sections. Use it to let users switch between related views without leaving the page. A strip narrower than its tabs scrolls horizontally and keeps the selected tab in view.

props.name: value
props.description: The currently selected tab value.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when a tab is selected.

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant applied to all child tabs.

props.name: layout
props.description: Layout mode for tab sizing. 'hug': each tab hugs its content width. 'fill': tabs stretch equally to fill the container width.

props.name: hasDivider
props.description: Whether to show a bottom border divider under the tab list.

props.name: isFullBleed
props.description: Makes the tab strip escape its parent's container padding, extending to the container's content edges (cancels the nearest padded Layout container's --container-padding-* custom properties with negative margins). The inner strip pads back by the portion of the container inset that is not already supplied by the first or last tab stop, keeping edge labels aligned while a hasDivider underline spans the full content width. Matches Divider's isFullBleed: inline (start/end) edges only; block-edge docking stays with the surrounding layout.

props.name: role
props.description: ARIA role for the strip. 'tablist' asks for the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern: role="tablist" / role="tab" and aria-selected, with each tab pointing at the panel it controls via its panelId; only tabs may live in a tablist strip, and an href on a tab is ignored there. Left unset, the strip is a nav landmark marking the current tab with aria-current. Any other value is passed through to the element unchanged.

props.name: overflow
props.description: What happens when the tabs are wider than the strip. 'auto' lets the component choose, which today always scrolls. 'scroll' scrolls the tabs horizontally, with edge fades and arrow affordances for pointers that can hover. 'visible' turns overflow handling off and lets the tabs spill out of the strip. The selected tab is always scrolled back into view.

props.name: children
props.description: Tab and TabMenu items to render inside the strip.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

bestPractices.text: Keep tab labels short and descriptive so users can quickly scan available sections.
Leave overflow handling on: a strip narrower than its tabs scrolls, and the selected tab is kept in view. Use TabMenu when you want a curated group of extra options rather than a scrolling strip.

When using hasDivider with action buttons alongside tabs, match the Button size to the TabList size (both md, both sm); the divided tab strip reserves space so tabs and same-size buttons align to a shared baseline above the rail.

Reach for role="tablist" when the strip switches panels in place, and give each tab a panelId pointing at the panel it opens: that link is how a screen reader gets from a tab to its content. Leave it off for navigation between views.
Set isFullBleed to stretch a tab bar inside a padded LayoutHeader, Card, or Section to the container's inline content edges, instead of reaching for negative-margin CSS.
Use tabs for sequential steps or workflows; use a stepper or wizard pattern instead.
Place more than 6–8 visible tabs before the overflow menu; prioritize the most important categories.

Confuse TabList with SegmentedControl or ToggleButton. TabList is for navigation between views. SegmentedControl and ToggleButton are input controls: SegmentedControl always has exactly one selected option, while ToggleButton can be toggled on or off.

accessibility.name: Tab label
accessibility.description: Each label must have at least 4.5:1 contrast with the tab surface behind it. For Hover and Pointer down, measure the final background after the overlay layer is applied.

anatomy.name: Left Content
anatomy.description: Most important area; hugs content width.

anatomy.name: Center-Fill Content
anatomy.description: Stretches to fill available space.

anatomy.name: Right Content
anatomy.description: Hugs content width.

components.name: TabMenu
components.description: Overflow menu trigger that opens a dropdown of additional tab options, showing the selected option's label as the trigger text. Host attributes and DOM event handlers (id, aria-*, data-*, drag and drop) reach the trigger button, not the popup or its options. The button keeps its role, tab stop, and menu disclosure attributes.

props.name: label
props.description: Label for the trigger button (shown when no option is selected) and the dropdown heading divider.

props.name: options
props.description: Array of menu options rendered in the dropdown.

components.name: Text
components.description: Text renders styled body text and headings from the theme. Use Text with a semantic type for body copy, labels, and captions, and Heading for section titles that output the correct h1–h6 element.

props.name: type
props.description: Semantic text type. Determines size, weight, and line-height from the theme. 'inherit' takes all three from the surrounding text instead. Themes may add custom types. Note: this prop is called `type`, not `variant`.

props.name: children
props.description: Text content.

props.name: size
props.description: Explicit font size override. Overrides the size from `type` but preserves other type properties. Prefer using `type` alone.

props.name: color
props.description: Text color. Defaults to 'secondary' for the 'supporting' type, 'primary' for all others. Themes may add custom colors.

props.name: weight
props.description: Font weight override.

props.name: display
props.description: Display type. Silently overridden to 'block' when maxLines > 0 or hasCapsize is true.

props.name: as
props.description: HTML element to render.

props.name: maxLines
props.description: Maximum lines before truncation. 0 means no truncation. When set, shows a tooltip on hover if content is truncated.

props.name: hasTruncateTooltip
props.description: Controls tooltip behavior for truncated text. true shows the tooltip at the default position, false disables it, or a placement string ('above' | 'below' | 'start' | 'end') sets a specific position.

props.name: wordBreak
props.description: Word break behavior when truncating. Defaults to 'break-all' for single-line truncation, 'break-word' otherwise. Without truncation, a token longer than its line (a URL, an ID) wraps (`overflow-wrap: break-word`), so in ordinary flow text does not make the page scroll sideways. Inside a flex row, give the flex child `min-width: 0` so it can shrink. A container you style with `overflow-wrap: anywhere` does not reach this text; Astryx's own containers pass their wrap through.

props.name: textWrap
props.description: Text wrapping behavior.

props.name: justify
props.description: Text alignment (justification). Uses logical values (start/end) for i18n/RTL compatibility.

props.name: hasCapsize
props.description: Enable optical alignment using text-box-trim. Forces block display.

props.name: hasStrikethrough
props.description: Apply strikethrough text decoration.

props.name: hasTabularNumbers
props.description: Use tabular (monospace) numbers for aligned numeric data.

props.name: id
props.description: HTML id attribute.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

bestPractices.text: Pick a semantic type (body, label, supporting, large, code) instead of manually setting size and weight; the theme handles the details.
Set accessibilityLevel on Heading when the visual level differs from the document outline so screen readers announce the correct hierarchy.
Use maxLines with a number to truncate long content; a tooltip appears automatically on hover so no text is lost.
Enable hasTabularNumbers for columns of numeric data so digits align vertically across rows.
Override size and weight when a semantic type already matches; extra overrides fight the theme and break when themes change.
Skip heading levels in the document outline; go h1 then h2 then h3, never h1 then h3.

Use raw HTML tags like

,

–

, or for text; Text and Heading apply the correct theme tokens automatically.
Pass a `variant` prop; Text does not have a `variant` prop. Use `type` for semantic styling (body, label, large, supporting, code) or use Heading for headings.
Use Text for headings; use Heading with a `level` prop (1–6) for section titles and headings.

anatomy.name: Text
anatomy.description: Polymorphic text element that renders the supplied content with themed typography.

anatomy.name: Heading
anatomy.description: Referenced Heading member that renders the supplied content as a semantic h1–h6 element.

anatomy.name: Truncation tooltip
anatomy.description: Tooltip-owned surface available only when Text or Heading is measured as truncated and truncation tooltips are enabled.

components.name: TextArea
components.description: TextArea is a multi-line text input for collecting longer-form content like comments, descriptions, or messages. Use it when the expected input spans multiple lines. For shorter, single-line values, use TextInput.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the underlying <textarea> element.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the textarea. Always rendered for accessibility.

props.name: value
props.description: Current value of the textarea.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the textarea value changes.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action fired after onChange inside a React transition. Enables optimistic updates via useOptimistic.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible to screen readers.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text displayed between the label and textarea.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Displays an "Optional" indicator next to the label. Mutually exclusive with isRequired.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Displays a "Required" indicator next to the label and sets aria-required. Mutually exclusive with isOptional.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the textarea, preventing interaction.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: Makes the textarea read-only: the value is shown at full opacity and still submits with the form, but cannot be edited. Unlike isDisabled, a read-only textarea is not dimmed and keeps its form value. isDisabled takes precedence when both are set.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the textarea is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the textarea focusable via aria-disabled (the field becomes read-only). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled TextArea in Tooltip, so the reason is attached to the field itself.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Puts the textarea in a loading state, showing a spinner inside the input.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when the textarea is empty.

props.name: rows
props.description: Number of visible text rows.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Maximum number of characters allowed, counted as user-perceived characters: an emoji or flag sequence counts as one. When set, a character counter (current/max) is displayed inside the input container, anchored to the bottom-right beneath the text. Does not enforce the limit natively; when exceeded the counter turns red and shows a warning icon (a non-color cue), and screen-reader users hear the remaining/over-limit count announced. Consumers validating the limit should count with characterCount (exported from the package) so enforcement matches the displayed count.

props.name: htmlMaxLength
props.description: The native `maxlength` attribute: the browser stops typing past this many UTF-16 code units (an emoji can take two or more). It is separate from `maxLength`, the soft counter of user-perceived characters: it works without the counter, and it neither shows nor changes the counter. It can stop typing before the counter reaches its limit. TextArea adds no truncation or validation of its own, so a longer controlled value stays as set. The attribute is in the server-rendered HTML, so it applies before hydration. Validate on the server too: the browser limit does not bind requests that skip the UI.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator that applies a colored border and icon. An optional message is displayed in a floating box below the textarea.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip hides the message box and surfaces it in a tooltip on the status icon.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text displayed in an info icon at the end of the label.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon rendered inside the leading edge of the textarea wrapper; pass a built-in meaning such as 'search' (see `astryx docs icons`), an icon component, or an icon element.

props.name: hasSpellCheck
props.description: Enables or disables browser spell checking.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Automatically focuses the textarea on mount.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the textarea, affecting internal padding. Height is controlled by rows, not size.

props.name: onPaste
props.description: Callback fired when content is pasted into the textarea.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: HTML name attribute for the textarea element, useful for form submissions.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Callback fired when the textarea receives focus.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Callback fired when the textarea loses focus.

props.name: autoComplete
props.description: The native autocomplete attribute, forwarded to the textarea unchanged. Does not affect the controlled value.

props.name: enterKeyHint
props.description: What the Return key of a touch keyboard says (the native `enterkeyhint`). iOS gives `done`, `go`, `next`, `search` and `send` their own key (a glyph on iOS 26: a checkmark, an arrow, a chevron, a magnifier, an up arrow); `enter` and `previous` keep the plain Return key. Chrome on Android (Gboard) gives every value its own key; with no hint a TextArea keeps Return. It only labels the key: what Enter does stays with your handlers.

props.name: inputMode
props.description: Which touch keyboard the field asks for (the native `inputmode`) without changing what it accepts: `numeric` brings up the number pad, `decimal` the decimal pad, `tel` the phone pad, `search` the web-search keyboard (whose Return key reads Go on iOS even with `enterKeyHint="search"`).

props.name: autoCapitalize
props.description: When a touch keyboard capitalizes as you type (the native `autocapitalize`). Unset, iOS capitalizes sentences. `off` and `none` never capitalize; `on` and `sentences` capitalize each sentence.

props.name: hasAutoCorrect
props.description: Whether a touch keyboard corrects words as you type (the native `autocorrect`). Unset, the browser decides; turn it off for usernames, codes and other values that are not words.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the element that paints the border and background and holds icons and end controls. Never the native input.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Class name for the visual control box.

props.name: controlStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the visual control box.

bestPractices.text: Provide a visible label so users know what to enter. If the label must be hidden, set isLabelHidden with a descriptive label for screen readers.
Set maxLength with a character counter when there is a defined limit; it helps users stay within bounds before they submit.
Keep Return a line break in a multi-line field. Relabel it with enterKeyHint (send, done) only when your own Enter handling does what the label says.
Use the status prop to surface validation feedback inline: show success when input is valid, warning for soft limits, and error for hard failures.
Add a description or placeholder to clarify expected content, like "Describe the issue in detail," but never rely on placeholder alone as the only label.
Avoid using TextArea for short, single-line values like names or emails; use TextInput instead.
Don't rely solely on placeholder text to communicate the purpose of the field; placeholders disappear on focus and are not accessible labels.
Don't show a status message without also setting the status type; the colored border and icon are what draw the user's attention to the message.
Don't wrap a disabled TextArea in Tooltip to explain why it's disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop, which attaches the reason to the field itself.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Text identifying the multi-line field.

anatomy.name: Description
anatomy.description: Helper text between the label and the input.

anatomy.name: Input container
anatomy.description: Painted boundary containing the text area and its overlays.

anatomy.name: Text area
anatomy.description: Multi-line control that displays and edits the value.

anatomy.name: Placeholder
anatomy.description: Hint text shown inside the empty text area.

anatomy.name: Start icon
anatomy.description: Astryx Icon rendered at the start when startIcon is a built-in meaning or icon component.

anatomy.name: Custom start content
anatomy.description: Caller-provided ReactNode rendered at the start instead of an Astryx Icon.

anatomy.name: Spinner
anatomy.description: Loading indicator shown at the end of the input container.

anatomy.name: Status icon
anatomy.description: Error, warning, or success icon shown inside the input.

anatomy.name: Character counter
anatomy.description: Current and maximum character counts shown inside the input container.

components.name: TextInput
components.description: TextInput collects short-form text like names, emails, or search queries. Use it for single-line values where the expected input is brief. Pair it with validation status to guide users through required or formatted fields.

props.name: type
props.description: The HTML input type. `email`, `tel` and `url` also bring up the matching touch keyboard (email, phone pad, URL); `search` makes the field a search box (pair it with `enterKeyHint="search"` for a Search key on iOS; Chrome on Android shows one for `type="search"` alone).

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the input: always rendered for accessibility.

props.name: value
props.description: Current value of the input.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the input value changes.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action fired after onChange (if not prevented). Triggers optimistic update and shows a loading spinner while pending.

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant of the input.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible to screen readers.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed between the label and input.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Displays an "Optional" indicator next to the label. Mutually exclusive with isRequired.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Displays a "Required" indicator next to the label and sets aria-required. Mutually exclusive with isOptional.

props.name: onEnter
props.description: Callback fired when the user presses the Enter key. IME-safe: Enter used to commit a Japanese/Chinese/Korean conversion does not fire it.

props.name: onKeyDown
props.description: Callback fired on keydown events on the input.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the input, preventing interaction and dimming the element.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: Makes the input read-only: the value is shown at full opacity and still submits with the form, but cannot be edited. Unlike isDisabled, a read-only input is not dimmed and keeps its form value. isDisabled takes precedence when both are set.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the input is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the input focusable via aria-disabled (the field becomes read-only). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled TextInput in Tooltip, so the reason is attached to the field itself.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Puts the input in a loading state, showing a spinner and setting aria-busy.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when the input is empty.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text displayed in an info icon at the end of the label.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon displayed at the start of the input; pass a built-in meaning such as 'search' (see `astryx docs icons`), an icon component, or an icon element.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status: applies a colored border and status icon. If message is provided, displays a floating message below the input. Error type also sets aria-invalid.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip hides the message box and surfaces it in a tooltip on the status icon.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Shows a clear (×) button when the input has a value. Clicking it clears the value and returns focus to the input.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Automatically focuses the input on mount.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: The HTML name attribute for the input, useful for form submissions.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned. Without a width the field can shrink with its row, so a filter bar never overflows; use `<HStack wrap="wrap">` when the controls should move to a second line instead.

props.name: autoComplete
props.description: The native autocomplete attribute, forwarded to the input unchanged. Does not affect the controlled value. It is also how AutoFill knows what a field holds: tag sign-in, address and payment fields (`username`, `new-password`, `one-time-code`, `email`, `tel`, `street-address`, …).

props.name: enterKeyHint
props.description: What the Return key of a touch keyboard says (the native `enterkeyhint`). iOS gives `done`, `go`, `next`, `search` and `send` their own key (a glyph on iOS 26: a checkmark, an arrow, a chevron, a magnifier, an up arrow); `enter` and `previous` keep the plain Return key. Chrome on Android (Gboard) gives every value its own key, `enter` and `previous` included; with no hint the key reads Next while another field follows, and a `type="url"` field shows Next instead of `go` while another field follows. It only labels the key: what Enter does stays with your handlers.

props.name: inputMode
props.description: Which touch keyboard the field asks for (the native `inputmode`) without changing what it accepts: `numeric` brings up the number pad, `decimal` the decimal pad, `tel` the phone pad, `search` the web-search keyboard (whose Return key reads Go on iOS even with `enterKeyHint="search"`; Chrome on Android shows the Enter key for `inputMode="search"` alone).

props.name: autoCapitalize
props.description: When a touch keyboard capitalizes as you type (the native `autocapitalize`). Unset, iOS capitalizes sentences, except in a URL field. `off` and `none` never capitalize; `on` and `sentences` capitalize each sentence.

props.name: hasAutoCorrect
props.description: Whether a touch keyboard corrects words as you type (the native `autocorrect`). Unset, the browser decides; turn it off for usernames, codes and other values that are not words.

props.name: hasSpellCheck
props.description: Whether misspelled words are underlined (the native `spellcheck`). Unset, the browser decides.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the element that paints the border and background and holds icons and end controls. Never the native input.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Class name for the visual control box.

props.name: controlStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the visual control box.

bestPractices.text: Always provide a visible label so users know what the field is for. Only hide the label when surrounding context makes it obvious, like a search bar with a magnifying-glass icon.
Use validation status with a message to explain what went wrong: "Email must include @" is better than just turning the border red.
Size the input to match the expected content length so users can gauge how much to type: small for zip codes, medium for names, large for URLs.
Add a clear button for search and filter inputs so users can quickly reset without selecting all text.

Tell a touch keyboard what the field holds: `type="email"`, `"tel"` or `"url"` for those values, `inputMode="numeric"` for digits that are not a number (a one-time code), `enterKeyHint` for what Return does (Search, Send, Next), and `autoComplete` so AutoFill can fill it.
Don't use placeholder text as a replacement for a label; placeholders disappear on focus and are not reliably read by screen readers.
Don't use TextInput for multi-line content like comments or descriptions; use TextArea instead.
Don't mark every field as required; only flag mandatory fields so users are not overwhelmed by validation errors.
Don't wrap a disabled TextInput in Tooltip to explain why it's disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop, which attaches the reason to the field itself.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Text that identifies the field. Always rendered for accessibility even when visually hidden.

anatomy.name: Description
anatomy.description: Helper text between the label and the input that provides additional context or formatting hints.

anatomy.name: Start icon
anatomy.description: A leading icon inside the input that hints at the expected content, like a magnifying glass for search.

anatomy.name: Placeholder
anatomy.description: Hint text shown when the input is empty. Disappears on focus.

anatomy.name: Clear button
anatomy.description: A trailing × button that resets the value and returns focus to the input.

anatomy.name: Spinner
anatomy.description: Loading indicator that appears during async actions like server-side validation.

anatomy.name: Status icon
anatomy.description: A trailing icon (error, warning, or success) that communicates validation state.

components.name: Theme
components.description: Wraps a subtree with a specific Astryx theme. For static production themes, use `astryx theme build` and import the generated CSS plus built theme object for first-paint and SSR performance. Use runtime `defineTheme()` when themes are dynamic or for prototyping. `defineTheme` accepts a `tokens` object whose keys are CSS custom property names (always prefixed with `--`). Common token names include `--color-accent`, `--color-background-surface`, `--color-background-body`, `--color-text-primary`, `--color-text-secondary`, `--radius-container`, `--spacing-1` through `--spacing-6`. Values can be a string (same for light/dark) or a `[light, dark]` tuple. Example: ```ts import {defineTheme} from '@astryxdesign/core/theme'; const myTheme = defineTheme({ name: 'ocean', tokens: { '--color-accent': ['#0077B6', '#48CAE4'], '--color-background-surface': ['#F0F8FF', '#0A1628'], '--color-text-primary': ['#0A1317', '#FFFFFF'], '--radius-container': '16px', }, }); ```

props.name: theme
props.description: Theme object to apply. Prefer built theme objects for static production themes; use runtime `defineTheme()` for dynamic themes. Its `motion` can set `tempo` (0.75–1.5) and `character` (`'crisp' | 'standard' | 'expressive'`). A color mode goes in `mode`: `theme="light"` applies no theme.

props.name: mode
props.description: Color mode. System takes the page’s light or dark scheme: reset.css makes it the reader’s preference, and the page or its host can set the root’s scheme itself.

props.name: children
props.description: Content to render with the theme.
