bestPractices.text: Build app themes that are known ahead of time with `astryx theme build`, then import the generated CSS and built theme object.
Use runtime themes when the theme is created or edited in the browser, such as theme editors, user branding, or prototypes.
Token names always start with `--` (e.g. `--color-accent`, `--color-background-surface`). Do not omit the prefix.
Default to runtime themes in SSR production apps. Component overrides inject after hydration instead of shipping as static CSS.

components.name: Thumbnail
components.description: Thumbnail displays a compact, square preview of an image attachment. It shows a shimmer effect while uploading, the image on success, and a placeholder icon when no source is set. Use it in chat composers, file upload lists, or anywhere you need a small image preview with optional remove and click actions.

props.name: src
props.description: Image source URL.

props.name: alt
props.description: Alt text for the image. When omitted, the image is explicitly decorative (alt="", role="presentation", aria-hidden) and hidden from screen readers; a dev warning fires if neither alt nor label is set.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label (e.g. file name). Shown as tooltip on hover.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: Callback for the overlaid remove button.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler. Adds button semantics and a hover overlay.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Shows skeleton (no src) or upload overlay (with src).

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the thumbnail is disabled.

props.name: showRemoveOn
props.description: When the remove button is visible. `hover` (the default) reveals it on hover and on keyboard focus, and keeps it visible under a coarse primary pointer (a phone or tablet); `always` shows it at rest. Only applies when `onRemove` is set.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling; className is provided for integration with non-StyleX systems.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling; inline styles bypass StyleX optimization.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

bestPractices.text: Always provide a label prop with the file name so the thumbnail and its remove button are accessible to screen readers and show a tooltip on hover.
Use isLoading without a src to show a skeleton during initial upload, and isLoading with a src to show a spinner overlay once a preview URL is available.
Pair onClick with a lightbox or detail view so users can inspect the full image; the thumbnail adds button semantics and a hover overlay automatically.
Don't use Thumbnail for non-image file types like PDFs or spreadsheets; use a file attachment component with an appropriate icon instead.
Don't omit alt text when a src is provided; screen readers need a description of the image content, not just the file name from label.

anatomy.name: Image
anatomy.description: The preview image, displayed as a square with cover fit.

anatomy.name: Placeholder
anatomy.description: An image silhouette icon shown when no src is provided.

anatomy.name: Remove button
anatomy.description: An overlaid close button in the top-right corner. Appears when onRemove is set. Sits on a fixed --color-overlay scrim with an --color-on-dark icon to stay visible on any image.

anatomy.name: Upload overlay
anatomy.description: A semi-transparent overlay with a spinner, shown when isLoading is true and a src preview is available.

anatomy.name: Skeleton
anatomy.description: A shimmer animation shown when isLoading is true and no src is set.

components.name: TimeInput
components.description: TimeInput uses a browser/OS time picker on coarse pointers by default and Astryx's typed field on fine pointers. It converts values to a standard format and supports arrow-key adjustment on the typed surface. Use it in forms, scheduling flows, or any interface where users need to select a specific time.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the input (required for accessibility).

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible to screen readers.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed between the label and input.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Shows an "(optional)" indicator next to the label. Mutually exclusive with isRequired.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Marks the field as required and sets aria-required. Mutually exclusive with isOptional.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the input and suppresses interactions. The input stays focusable and exposes `aria-disabled`.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the input is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and describes the input (activation stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled TimeInput in Tooltip.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled time value in ISO format (HH:MM or HH:MM:SS).

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the time changes. Receives undefined when the input is cleared.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action fired after onChange. Wrapped in a React transition to provide optimistic UI; triggers the loading spinner while pending.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Puts the input into a loading state, displaying a spinner.

props.name: min
props.description: Minimum selectable time in ISO format. Values outside the range are rejected.

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum selectable time in ISO format. Values outside the range are rejected.

props.name: hasSeconds
props.description: Includes seconds in the time display and parsing.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Shows a clear button when a value is set and the input is not disabled.

props.name: hourFormat
props.description: Controls the display format. '12h' shows the locale's day period (e.g. '2:30 PM', '오후 2:30'); '24h' uses 24-hour notation (e.g. '14:30'). When unset, follows the InternationalizationProvider locale's hour cycle: en-US reads 12-hour, en-GB and de-DE read 24-hour. To honor a person's own preference, pass it on the locale tag (e.g. 'en-US-u-hc-h23') rather than per field.

props.name: increment
props.description: Number of minutes to add or subtract when the user presses the up or down arrow key. Steps are whole minutes; a fractional value leaves the time unchanged.

props.name: presentation
props.description: Which surface selects the time. 'adaptive-native' (the default) uses Astryx's typed field on a fine pointer and the browser/OS input type=time on a coarse pointer — except hasSeconds or increment other than 1, which retain the typed field because iOS has no seconds wheel and treats step as validation rather than picker cadence; 'native' always uses the browser/OS control with no Astryx fallback; 'adaptive-bottom-sheet' uses the typed field on a fine pointer and Astryx's bottom-sheet time wheels on a coarse pointer; 'bottom-sheet' forces the wheels on every pointer; 'text-input' (like 'popover', which has no distinct TimeInput surface) keeps only the typed field. Native mode forwards min/max and enforces them on commit. hourFormat formats the closed value; the open OS picker follows the device locale.

props.name: nativePicker
props.description: Deprecated: use presentation ('touch' = 'adaptive-native', 'always' = 'native', 'never' = 'text-input'). Still works exactly as released; presentation wins when both are set.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when no time is selected. When the input is focused and empty, a format hint overrides this text.

props.name: size
props.description: Controls the height of the input element.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator that colors the border and displays an icon. When a message is provided it is rendered below the input. A typed time the field rejects, and a native edit outside min or max, show the field's own error message instead; an error status with a message shows in its place, and the rejection is still announced. A warning or success never replaces a rejection.

props.name: onEntryErrorChange
props.type: (error: {kind: 'unreadable' | 'outOfRange', text: string, value?: ISOTimeString} | null) => void
props.description: Called each time the field's rejection of typed text changes, and with null when the rejection ends. kind is 'unreadable' (text that is not a time) or 'outOfRange' (a time before min or after max); text is the typed text; value is the ISO time the text names, for 'outOfRange'. Under entryErrorBehavior 'complete', a rejection shows once the typed time is complete (in 12-hour text, with its day period unless the hour reads 0 or 13–23), or at Enter or blur; under 'blur-or-enter', only at Enter or blur. Rejected text stays in the field. It also runs when a new min, max, or value, or disabling the field, changes the rejection, never twice for the same rejection, and with null when the field unmounts while a rejection stands. The native and bottom-sheet surfaces take no typed text, so they never report.

props.name: entryErrorBehavior
props.description: When the field shows its own entry error: a typed time it rejects, as onEntryErrorChange reports it, or a native edit outside min or max. It sets when the error shows, not when validation runs, so it is not React Aria's validationBehavior (native versus ARIA validation), and it never changes a caller status. 'complete' shows a complete typed time outside min or max, and a native edit outside them, at once, and other rejected text at Enter or blur. 'blur-or-enter' holds every rejection until Enter or blur: the message, aria-invalid, the invalid styling, the announcement, and the onEntryErrorChange report then appear together. Under both values, an edit the field accepts or empties clears the error at once; under 'blur-or-enter', an edit that leaves the entry wrong keeps the shown error until the next Enter or blur. The field's own value wins over the nearest FormLayout's defaultEntryErrorBehavior.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip hides the message box and surfaces it in a tooltip on the status icon.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text rendered as an info icon at the end of the label row.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the Field box around the label, control, and status. containerClassName and containerStyle take a class name and inline styles for the same box. No effect (development warning) where no Field box renders: inside InputGroup (style the group) and in a horizontal-labels FormLayout.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the bordered element that holds the text, icons, and end controls, never the native input. controlClassName and controlStyle take a class name and inline styles for the same box. Replaces root xstyle, className, and style, which this component does not accept.

bestPractices.text: Base props such as ref, id, data-*, aria-*, and DOM event handlers go to the time input, the element that is focused and announced. A DOM handler runs after TimeInput's own handler for the same event and still receives events it handled (including ones it called preventDefault on), so it cannot cancel built-in behavior.

Leave hourFormat unset so the field follows the InternationalizationProvider locale's hour cycle (12-hour in en-US, 24-hour in en-GB or de-DE). Set it only when the field itself needs a fixed format, and carry a person's own 12/24-hour preference on the provider locale (e.g. 'en-US-u-hc-h23') rather than on each field.
Set min and max constraints when the context has a valid range, like business hours or event windows, so users cannot submit an out-of-bounds time.
Provide a description or placeholder that hints at the expected format or purpose, like "Business hours: 9 AM – 5 PM".
Use the status prop to surface validation errors inline: show a message like "Time must be during business hours" so users know exactly what to fix.
Enable hasClear when the field is optional, so users can remove a previously selected time.
Place TimeInput inside InputGroup when the time needs a single-line prefix or suffix addon, like a start/end label or timezone marker.
Don't use TimeInput for combined date-and-time selection; pair it with a separate DateInput instead.
Don't hide the label; even when space is tight, keep the label visible or provide a description so the purpose is clear.
Wrap a disabled TimeInput in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop instead, which ties the reason to the field.

anatomy.name: Clock icon
anatomy.description: A leading clock icon that identifies the field and opens the browser/OS picker in native mode.

anatomy.name: Time control
anatomy.description: A real input type=time in native modes, or Astryx's editable text field for fine pointers, presentation="text-input", seconds, and custom increments.

anatomy.name: Clear button
anatomy.description: A trailing button to reset the value, shown when hasClear is true and a value is set.

anatomy.name: Status icon
anatomy.description: A trailing icon indicating error, warning, or success state.

anatomy.name: Spinner
anatomy.description: Replaces trailing content during loading to show an async action is in progress.

components.name: Timer
components.description: Displays a standardized elapsed duration for active work without scheduling a React render on every tick. Elapsed format updates by second below one hour and by minute after one hour; clock format remains second-precise.

props.name: startTime
props.description: Unix time in milliseconds when the measured operation began. Omit it to start from this Timer's mount.

props.name: format
props.description: Standard duration representation. Elapsed uses compact units and drops seconds after one hour; clock uses m:ss or h:mm:ss.

props.name: type
props.description: Semantic text type. Uses the same typography behavior as Timestamp.

props.name: size
props.description: Explicit font size override. Overrides the size from type.

props.name: color
props.description: Text color.

props.name: weight
props.description: Font weight override.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the Text wrapper. Must be a stylex.create() value.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name for the Text wrapper. Prefer xstyle for styling.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the Text wrapper. Prefer xstyle for styling.

bestPractices.text: Use elapsed for compact duration text that may span seconds, minutes, or hours.
Use clock for stopwatch-like surfaces where seconds remain meaningful after an hour.
Pass startTime when the operation began before Timer mounted so the display reflects the complete wait.
Do not use Timer for dates, time zones, or relative calendar language; use Timestamp instead.
Do not add aria-live unless hearing an announcement every tick is appropriate for the specific task.

anatomy.name: Elapsed time
anatomy.description: Semantic time element containing a standardized elapsed duration.

components.name: Timestamp
components.description: Timestamp formats a date or time value into human-readable text. Use it to show when something was created, updated, or is scheduled; picking relative for recency, absolute for precision, or auto to let the component decide.

props.name: value
props.description: The date/time to display. Accepts Unix timestamps (seconds) or ISO 8601 strings.

props.name: format
props.description: Display format. 'relative' uses the locale's native long relative-time wording ('2 hours ago' in English), 'relative_short' uses its narrow pattern ('2h ago' in English) for compact surfaces, 'date' shows 'Mar 21, 2025', 'date_long' shows 'March 21, 2025', 'date_weekday' shows 'Wed, Mar 21, 2025', 'date_time' shows 'Mar 21, 2025, 2:51 PM', 'time' shows '2:51 PM', 'system_*' variants use ISO-style formatting, 'unix_seconds' shows the Unix time in whole seconds since the epoch (an absolute, zone-independent value), 'auto' switches from relative to date_time based on recency. Absolute formats never read the current time. 'relative', 'relative_short' and 'auto' read it on the client only: a server render or static prerender shows the full date and time in UTC, labelled, and the client switches to the format's normal output after hydration. Date-bearing formats ('date', 'date_long', 'date_weekday', 'date_time', and the full date in the hover card and the accessible name) use the InternationalizationProvider calendar, such as calendar="persian"; 'time', the relative formats, 'system_*', and 'unix_seconds' do not change.

props.name: timezoneID
props.description: IANA time zone the absolute formats render in, such as 'UTC' or 'America/Los_Angeles'. Omit (or pass 'local') for the viewer's own zone. An explicit zone renders identically on the server and the client, so it is the way to show an absolute time without a hydration mismatch; relative formats' visible text ignores it, while configured tooltipEntries rows still follow it. An unknown identifier warns once in development and falls back to the viewer's zone.

props.name: autoThreshold
props.description: Threshold in seconds for 'auto' format to switch from relative to date_time.

props.name: hasTooltip
props.description: Whether to show a copyable hover card with the full date/time on hover or keyboard focus. Applies to relative timestamps and to any format once tooltipEntries is configured.

props.name: tooltipEntries
props.type: ReadonlyArray<{timezoneID?: string; format?: TimestampTooltipFormat; label?: string; isCopyable?: boolean}>
props.description: Lines to show on hover, so one instant can be read (and optionally copied) in several time zones and/or formats at once. Each entry is one line, in the order given. An entry without timezoneID follows the Timestamp timezoneID when set, else the viewer's zone; 'local' always means the viewer's zone; format defaults to the full absolute style and also accepts 'full' alongside every non-relative TimestampFormat. Rows are read-only unless they set isCopyable (default false); copyable rows show a copy button in a dedicated trailing action column so buttons align, and the column is only present when some row is copyable. With no entries the card shows a single default row with the full absolute time, which is copyable. Configuring entries also attaches the surface to absolute formats, which otherwise have none.

props.name: isTimezoneShown
props.description: Whether to append the timezone abbreviation to the visible text. Applies to the date_time and time formats; system_* formats stay machine-readable and never carry one. Use tooltipEntries to control the tooltip's time zones.

props.name: isLive
props.description: Whether the relative time should update live (e.g. "2 min ago" → "3 min ago").

props.name: type
props.description: Semantic text type from Text. Determines size, weight, and line-height.

props.name: size
props.description: Explicit font size override. Overrides the size from type.

props.name: color
props.description: Text color.

props.name: weight
props.description: Font weight override.

bestPractices.text: Use the auto format in feeds and lists so recent items show "2 hours ago" and older items show the full date automatically.
Keep formatting consistent within the same list or table; mixing relative and absolute timestamps in the same column confuses scanning.
Enable isTimezoneShown when the audience spans multiple time zones, like a global team calendar or audit log.
Use tooltipEntries when readers must compare zones, such as an incident log where the reader's time and the event's origin zone both matter.

Pass timezoneID when an absolute time must read the same for every viewer and on the server, like an incident log timestamp or anything server-rendered; without it the server markup depends on the server zone.
Label every entry once a tooltip shows more than one zone; a bare abbreviation is not always recognizable (Tokyo renders as "GMT+9", not "JST").
Use isLive for active dashboards or real-time feeds so the relative time stays accurate without a page refresh.

Reach for tooltipEntries when readers need to grab an exact value: an incident log or deploy record where someone pastes the UTC time or Unix seconds elsewhere; configuring entries turns the hover into copy-to-clipboard rows.
Don't display raw Unix timestamps or ISO strings to users; always pass them through Timestamp to get a human-readable format.
Avoid system_date or system_time formats in user-facing UI; they are meant for developer tools, logs, and machine-readable contexts.
Don't disable the hover card on relative timestamps; users expect to hover for the full date when they see "3 hours ago".
Don't stack many zones into one card; it is capped at 300px wide and long labelled lines wrap. Two or three entries read well.

anatomy.name: Formatted text
anatomy.description: The rendered date, time, or relative label like "2 hours ago" or "Mar 21, 2025".

anatomy.name: Hover card
anatomy.description: A copyable hover card showing the full absolute date and time when the display is relative, or the rows configured via tooltipEntries. Its default single row carries the full absolute time.

anatomy.name: Hover card row
anatomy.description: One row of the card: an optional label beside the instant rendered in one time zone and format. Rows opt into a copy button via isCopyable.

anatomy.name: Copy button
anatomy.description: Per-row copy-to-clipboard button in the hover card; copies that row's formatted value.

components.name: Toast
components.description: Toast shows a brief, non-blocking notification to confirm an action or present temporary information; show one with `const showToast = useToast()`, which needs no provider or mounted ToastViewport: inside LayerProvider (or a ToastViewport) it uses that viewport, and otherwise the first toast mounts a fallback viewport on document.body with a development warning. Use it for scenarios where the user needs feedback but not a decision, such as saving, deleting, or changing a status. For production use, prefer the `useToast()` hook; it handles positioning, stacking, auto-dismiss, and deduplication via `ToastViewport`. Only the viewport announces a toast: a `Toast` rendered on its own, as in a preview, is not a live region and announces nothing. Toasts stay within viewport and safe-area gutters, wrap long message content, and enter, exit, or swipe-dismiss toward their configured top or bottom edge. The vertical swipe uses the same spatial model as placement motion: top Toasts leave upward and bottom Toasts leave downward. Swipe waits for dominant edge-directed intent before cancelling native touch movement and reports the existing manual dismissal reason. Pen is supported as direct-contact input; mouse drag is excluded to avoid conflicting with desktop text selection, where the visible close control remains available. Set `isAutoHide: false` explicitly when an action or message must remain available. The `Toast` component renders the visual toast element inline and is useful for previews, documentation, and static showcases where the viewport lifecycle is not needed. Host `data-*` attributes on `Toast` reach the toast element; its role, live-region attributes, and theme attributes stay component-owned.

props.name: body
props.description: Primary message content.

props.name: type
props.description: Toast type controlling background color. useToast()'s show function sets it when it is not given.

props.name: isAutoHide
props.description: Whether the toast auto-dismisses. useToast()'s show function sets it by type when it is not given.

props.name: autoHideDuration
props.description: Duration in ms before auto-dismiss. Timed content must satisfy WCAG 2.2.1. useToast()'s show function sets it when it is not given.

props.name: isExiting
props.description: Whether the toast is leaving: it plays its exit motion and stops responding to swipes. The toast viewport sets it while a toast leaves; set it only when you render Toast yourself.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content rendered at the trailing end (e.g. Undo button, link). Keep action labels short.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Callback fired when the toast is dismissed.

props.name: renderContent
props.description: Replaces the content of this toast's card with your own layout. Astryx keeps the card, its astryx-toast theme target and auto-hide behavior (inside a ToastViewport the viewport announces the toast, over a modal too, and the card itself is not a live region), then hands the renderer the message, endContent, resolved toast settings and a dismiss callback. The custom renderer owns every control in its layout: compose the control you want and call dismiss from it. Astryx does not inject a fallback close into custom content. Per-toast: an app shares one layout by wrapping useToast and passing it on every call, while a toast raised by library code that never passes it renders as an ordinary Astryx toast. The argument is {body, endContent, type, isAutoHide, autoHideDuration, dismiss}, where type is 'info' | 'error'.

bestPractices.text: Keep messages short: only a few words that tell the user what happened, like "Changes saved" or "Message sent".
Add a short undo action in the endContent slot for reversible operations. Set isAutoHide to false when the action must remain available.
Pass useToast()'s uniqueID option to deduplicate toasts that fire from repeated actions, like clicking a save button multiple times.
Use error type for failures that need attention but not immediate action; it persists until dismissed so the user won't miss it.
Don't use a toast for critical errors that block the user. Use Banner for persistent, in-context messaging that requires acknowledgment.
Don't put long or multi-line content in a toast; it disappears after 5 seconds and the user may not finish reading.
Don't show form validation errors as toasts. Use inline field validation so the user can see exactly which field needs fixing.

anatomy.name: Body
anatomy.description: The primary message text describing what happened or what the user should know.

anatomy.name: End content
anatomy.description: A trailing action like an Undo button or a link, placed after the body text.

anatomy.name: Dismiss button
anatomy.description: A close button that lets the user manually dismiss the toast before auto-hide.

components.name: ToggleButton
components.description: ToggleButton switches between selected and unselected states to represent a persistent on/off choice. Use it standalone for binary actions like bold, mute, or favorite, or inside a ToggleButtonGroup for single-select or multi-select toolbar controls.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the button. Used as visible text, or as aria-label for icon-only buttons.

props.name: isPressed
props.description: Whether the button is currently pressed. Ignored for a ToggleButtonGroup member with a value.

props.name: onPressedChange
props.description: Called synchronously when pressed state should change. Receives the next state and the click event; call event.preventDefault() to skip pressedChangeAction. Without an Action, the callback produces no Action-pending feedback. Ignored for a ToggleButtonGroup member with a value.

props.name: pressedChangeAction
props.description: Action handler for API- or navigation-backed toggles, run in a transition after the synchronous onPressedChange callback unless that callback calls event.preventDefault(). Works without onPressedChange. Shows an optimistic pressed state and a spinner while pending, and remains interruptible by re-clicks. Omit it for callback-only toggles with no Action-pending feedback. Ignored for a ToggleButtonGroup member with a value.

props.name: size
props.description: Button size. Defaults to group size when inside a group.

props.name: elevation
props.description: Resting shadow depth for floating (FAB-style) toggle buttons, mirroring Button. `none` is the default flat button; `low`/`med`/`high` map to the shadow token scale. Applies inside a ToggleButtonGroup as well — grouped children retain their own elevation.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the button is disabled.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Whether the button shows a loading spinner.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon element. When provided without children, button becomes icon-only with tooltip from label.

props.name: isIconOnly
props.description: When true, renders as a square icon-only button with `label` as the aria-label and an automatic tooltip from the label.

props.name: pressedIcon
props.description: Icon shown when pressed. Falls back to icon if not provided.

props.name: children
props.description: Visible content. If omitted with icon, button becomes icon-only.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Tooltip text shown on hover.

props.name: value
props.description: Value identifier when used inside ToggleButtonGroup. Required in groups.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

bestPractices.text: Use a filled or colored icon for the pressed state so users can see the current state at a glance: an outline star vs a solid star, for example.
Keep the label identical between pressed and unpressed states. Let the visual treatment (icon, weight, background) communicate the change.
Wrap related toggles in a ToggleButtonGroup with an accessible label so screen readers announce them as a connected set.
Don't use a ToggleButton for one-time actions like "Submit" or "Delete"; those are regular Buttons, not toggles.
Don't mix ToggleButtons with regular Buttons inside the same group; use only ToggleButtons in a ToggleButtonGroup.
Don't use a ToggleButton for on/off settings that persist across sessions; use a Switch instead, which better communicates "setting" semantics.

accessibility.name: Text label
accessibility.description: The label must have at least 4.5:1 contrast with the button background when selected and unselected. For Hover and Pointer down, measure the final background after the overlay is applied.

accessibility.name: Essential icon or spinner arc
accessibility.description: An icon-only ToggleButton must have at least 3:1 contrast between its icon and button background. The moving spinner arc must also meet 3:1. An icon beside a visible label does not need its own check.

accessibility.name: Selected state indicator
accessibility.description: The selected background must reach 3:1 only when users need it to tell selected from unselected. Label weight or a changed icon can also show selection.

accessibility.name: Visible control boundary
accessibility.description: The button edge needs 3:1 contrast only when users need it to see the control. A visible label or icon can show the control instead.

accessibility.name: Keyboard focus indicator
accessibility.description: The focus outline must have at least 3:1 contrast with the area around the button. Check both selected and unselected states.

accessibility.name: Disabled appearance
accessibility.description: Disabled controls do not need to meet these contrast ratios.

anatomy.name: Icon
anatomy.description: A leading icon that represents the toggle action, like a star for favorite or bold "B" for formatting.

anatomy.name: Pressed icon
anatomy.description: An alternate icon shown when pressed: typically a filled version of the default icon to reinforce the active state.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: The visible text or accessible name. For icon-only toggles, used as the aria-label and auto-tooltip.

anatomy.name: Spinner
anatomy.description: Replaces the icon during async operations triggered by pressedChangeAction.

components.name: ToggleButtonGroup
components.description: Groups toggle buttons for exclusive (single) or multi-select behavior. Uses discriminated union on type for type-safe value/onChange. Under the touch presentation a press tracks like a menu: press a toggle and slide across the others, and the highlight follows. Only the toggle you lift on toggles, and lifting outside the group toggles nothing. With a finger, each toggle's target grows toward 44 px, up to half the gap to a neighbour, without the toggles growing.

props.name: children
props.description: ToggleButton children. Give each member a value; the group owns its pressed state and ignores its isPressed, onPressedChange, and pressedChangeAction props. Member activation calls the group’s onChange without starting a member Action transition.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the group (aria-label).

props.name: type
props.description: Selection mode. Single allows one active button, multiple allows many.

props.name: value
props.description: Currently selected value(s). Type depends on selection mode.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when selection changes.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Layout direction of the button group.

props.name: size
props.description: Default size for buttons in the group. Individual buttons can override.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether all buttons in the group are disabled.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

components.name: Token
components.description: Token is a small, inline element for representing discrete pieces of associated data, like tags, categories, or selections. Use it to label content, show active filters, or represent removable items like selected recipients in a compose field.

props.name: label
props.description: Text label displayed inside the token.

props.name: size
props.description: The size of the token.

props.name: color
props.description: Color variant of the token.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon rendered before the label.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the token is disabled; reduces opacity and blocks interactions.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: Callback fired when the remove button is clicked. When provided, an X button is rendered inside the token.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler. When provided, the token renders as a <span> container with an invisible <button> inside for accessibility.

props.name: href
props.description: Link URL. When provided, the token renders as an <a> element. The destination follows the shared navigation rule described on the Link `href` prop.

props.name: description
props.description: Accessible description applied via aria-description on the root element.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content rendered after the label and before the remove button.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label using a screen-reader-only clip technique; the label remains accessible.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

bestPractices.text: Use color to distinguish categories (for example, green for "Active", red for "Blocked", blue for "In Review") so users can scan status at a glance.
Provide an onRemove callback when tokens represent user selections that can be undone, like filters or multi-select values.
Add a leading icon when it helps identify the token type faster, like a person icon for user tokens or a tag icon for labels.
Keep labels short: one to three words. Tokens truncate with ellipsis when the text overflows.
Labels keep their character order under right-to-left, so `@alice`, `C++` and `example.com` read as written; a right-to-left label still reads right to left.
Don't use tokens for primary actions or navigation; use Button or Link instead. Tokens are for displaying metadata, not triggering workflows.
Don't hide the label unless the icon alone is universally understood. A color dot without text is ambiguous.
Don't mix too many colors in one token group. Stick to two or three meaningful colors so the palette stays scannable.

anatomy.name: Icon
anatomy.description: A leading icon that identifies the token type, like a user avatar or category symbol.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: The visible text. Also used as the accessible name when isLabelHidden is true.

anatomy.name: End content
anatomy.description: Trailing content after the label, like a count badge or status dot.

anatomy.name: Remove button
anatomy.description: An X button that appears when onRemove is provided, letting users dismiss the token.

components.name: Tokenizer
components.description: Tokenizer is a multi-select input that lets users search, select, and manage multiple items displayed as removable chips. Use it when users need to build a set of selections from a searchable data source, like adding team members, applying tags, or choosing filters.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the input.

props.name: searchSource
props.description: Data source providing search and bootstrap methods. `search(query, context)` may call `context.update(items)` to show matches it already has before it returns; the value it returns is the final list, and every list after the first for a query keeps the shown rows first and adds new rows after them.

props.name: value
props.description: Array of currently selected items.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when selection changes. The change argument includes the affected item and type ('add' | 'create' | 'remove' | 'reorder'). Additions and removals (including Backspace on an empty input) are announced to screen readers via a polite live region.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Input placeholder text. Only shown when no tokens are selected.

props.name: maxEntries
props.description: Maximum number of selections allowed. Input is hidden when the limit is reached.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Show a clear-all button for bulk removal of all tokens.

props.name: renderToken
props.description: Custom render function for selected tokens. Default renders Token with label and onRemove.

props.name: renderItem
props.description: Custom render function for dropdown items. Default renders TypeaheadItem.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the input and all token interactions. The input keeps its tab stop: it is announced as disabled (aria-disabled), is read-only, and opens and picks nothing. With tokenOverflowBehavior="unfocusedLayer", the placeholder of the collapsed field keeps that tab stop.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: The HTML name attribute for form submissions. Renders one hidden input per selected item id.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the tokenizer is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the input focusable via aria-disabled (input stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled Tokenizer in Tooltip, so the reason is attached to the field itself.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status object with type and message for error/warning/success states.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip reveals the message in an info-tip button.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text displayed below the label.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Marks the field as required.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Shows an optional indicator on the label.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text shown on the label.

props.name: hasEntriesOnFocus
props.description: Show bootstrap results on focus before typing. After a pick from that list, the input keeps focus and the list stays open with the next choice active, while another choice remains.

props.name: maxMenuItems
props.description: Maximum number of search results to display. The hasCreate entry is offered on top of them, so a menu can show one more than this.

props.name: menuWidth
props.description: Fixed dropdown width in pixels. The menu never shrinks below its anchor width.

props.name: minQueryLength
props.description: Minimum query length before the search source is queried. Below it no search runs, and the menu stays closed — unless hasCreate is set, in which case the "Create ..." entry is still offered, being derived from the typed text rather than fetched for it.

props.name: emptySearchText
props.description: Content shown when the query matched nothing. Takes a ReactNode, so the dead end can carry a link or a create row. Announced in a polite live region as the text it renders, read from the DOM; aria-hidden parts stay out of both, and content that renders no text announces nothing. null counts as not given, like undefined, and falls through to the default; pass an empty string to render nothing.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Auto-focus the input on mount.

props.name: size
props.description: Input and token size. Inside an InputGroup the group's size applies instead.

props.name: debounceMs
props.description: Debounce delay in ms before triggering search. Set to 0 for synchronous sources, and for a source that shows local matches through `context.update` and delays its own server request.

props.name: hasCreate
props.description: Allow users to create new tokens from free-text input. When true, a "Create" option appears in the dropdown for typed text that doesn't match existing results. The onChange change type is 'create' for these items.

props.name: onChangeQuery
props.description: Callback fired when the search query text changes.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon to display at the start of the input, before any tokens; pass a built-in meaning such as 'search' (see `astryx docs icons`), an icon component, or an icon element.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content to display at the end of the input row. Useful for buttons, result counts, or other controls.

props.name: handleRef
props.description: Imperative handle exposing focus(), blur(), open() and close(). open() and close() drive the inline menu; the sheet presentation ignores them.

props.name: menu
props.description: What the menu shows. role 'listbox' (default) is the result list; its optional render({listbox, query, isBusy, isEmptySearch, close}) places information such as a header or a hint around it, and anything a person acts on stays a result so the arrow keys reach it. role 'dialog' shows render({query, close}) in a dialog named by label that takes focus; Escape, an outside press or close() returns focus to where it was when the menu opened. Astryx owns the layer either way. Switching from listbox to dialog keeps the menu open: call handleRef.open() from onChange. The sheet presentation keeps its own sheet and ignores it.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the inline menu opens or closes. It reports changes only; drive the menu with handleRef. Not called by the sheet presentation.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: tokenOverflowBehavior
props.description: Controls how tokens overflow when the container is too narrow.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Fires when focus enters the tokenizer input.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Fires when focus leaves the tokenizer input.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

bestPractices.text: Write a placeholder that tells users what they can search for, such as "Search people..." or "Add tags...", so the input is not a blank mystery.
Set maxEntries when the number of selections should be bounded, like limiting a review to 5 approvers.
Use hasCreate for free-form tagging where users need to enter values that do not exist in the search source.
Show validation status with the status prop so users know immediately when a selection is missing or invalid.

Use inside InputGroup only when the tokenizer needs a short prefix or suffix addon as part of one decorated input surface; the grouped row stays single-line, so keep selections few (maxEntries) or use tokenOverflowBehavior to summarize them.
Don't use Tokenizer for single-item selection; use Typeahead instead. Tokenizer is for building sets of two or more items.
Avoid applying custom colors to individual tokens inside a Tokenizer; use the default token style for visual consistency across the set.
Don't hide the label; every Tokenizer needs a visible label so users understand what they are selecting. Use isLabelHidden only when surrounding context makes the purpose obvious.
Wrap a disabled Tokenizer in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: The visible text above the input describing what the user is selecting. Also used as the accessible name.

anatomy.name: Token chips
anatomy.description: Removable chips representing each selected item. Each chip shows a label and a remove button.

anatomy.name: Search input
anatomy.description: The text input where users type to search the data source. Hides when maxEntries is reached.

anatomy.name: Dropdown menu
anatomy.description: The search results list that appears below the input as the user types.

anatomy.name: Spinner
anatomy.description: Loading indicator shown at the end of the field while a search is in flight.

anatomy.name: End content
anatomy.description: A trailing slot after the input for action buttons, counts, or other controls.

anatomy.name: Clear button
anatomy.description: A button that removes all selected tokens at once. Shown when hasClear is true and tokens are present.

anatomy.name: Status icon
anatomy.description: Error, warning, or success icon at the end of the field. With statusVariant tooltip it is a button that reveals the status message.

components.name: Toolbar
components.description: Toolbar is a horizontal bar with left, center, and right areas. Use it for contextual actions within a content area (above a table, inside a card, or in a panel), not as a page-level header. Set the size once on the toolbar and all buttons, inputs, and tabs inside it match automatically.

bestPractices.text: Put secondary actions like "Back" on the left, and primary actions like "Save" on the right.
Make temporary toolbars like bulk selection visually distinct so users can tell they're contextual, for example with a background color or border.
Visually separate the toolbar from the content below it, with a divider, a background variant, or both.

Use Toolbar as a card header when the header has interactive actions like filter or add; it gives you slot layout, keyboard navigation, and size cascading. If the header is just a title with no actions, a LayoutHeader or Section is enough.
Put too many actions in one toolbar; move less common items into a MoreMenu.
Set size on individual child buttons; set it once on the toolbar and it cascades automatically.
Use Toolbar for app-wide navigation like main menu links or sign out; use TopNav or LayoutHeader for that.

anatomy.name: Outer chrome
anatomy.description: Section-owned container that supplies the toolbar surface, padding, and selected divider edges.

anatomy.name: Toolbar
anatomy.description: Named toolbar row that owns toolbar semantics and the start, optional center, and end layout.

components.name: Tooltip
components.description: A short text hint that appears on hover or focus, anchored to a trigger element. Use it to describe icon-only buttons, show the full text of truncated labels, or provide supplementary context without cluttering the UI.

bestPractices.text: Keep tooltip content concise: aim for under 140 characters of plain text.
Add a tooltip to icon-only buttons and controls that lack a visible label.

Set touchTrigger to tap when the trigger is a button whose only job is revealing the tooltip: touch has no hover, and auto keeps the tap for triggers that perform an action. For an info icon, use InfoTip, which also pins its help on a press.
Place interactive elements like links or buttons inside a tooltip; use HoverCard or Popover instead.
Use tooltips for essential information that users must see to complete a task.

anatomy.name: Tooltip surface
anatomy.description: Painted overlay surface that presents the tooltip.

anatomy.name: Tooltip text
anatomy.description: Tooltip content rendered within the surface.

components.name: TopNav
components.description: TopNav is a horizontal navigation bar for product-level navigation in application headers. Use TopNav for 5 or fewer always-visible navigation items, or minimal navigation paired with search and controls. For complex navigation hierarchies, use a sidebar; to filter content, use tabs or filter buttons instead.

props.name: heading
props.description: Heading slot content (logo, brand): positioned at the left edge of the nav bar.

props.name: startContent
props.description: Start content slot for navigation items or breadcrumbs: positioned after the heading, left-aligned.

props.name: children
props.description: Alias for startContent. Prefer startContent when composing with heading, centerContent, or endContent; children keeps the common React nav-item pattern from silently dropping items.

props.name: centerContent
props.description: Center content slot (tabs, search bar, primary navigation): when provided, switches the layout to three regions that keep it at the middle of the bar while they fit one row; the bar wraps when they do not.

props.name: endContent
props.description: End content slot for search, icons, or user profile: positioned at the right edge.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the navigation landmark, applied as aria-label on the <nav> element.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

bestPractices.text: Include a product logo and name in the heading slot to clearly identify the application.
Limit primary navigation items to 5 or fewer for quick scanning and minimal cognitive load.
Avoid using TopNav to filter page content; use Tabs or filter controls instead.
Avoid deeply nested navigation hierarchies; keep menus to one level of depth.

anatomy.name: Product icon and name
anatomy.description: Identifies the product in the navigation bar.

anatomy.name: Navigation items
anatomy.description: Primary links for product-level destinations.

anatomy.name: More menu
anatomy.description: Overflow menu for additional navigation items.

anatomy.name: Flex area
anatomy.description: Flexible region for search, primary action buttons, or other controls.

components.name: TopNavHeading
components.description: Product/suite/account heading for the TopNav heading slot. Supports smart interaction boundary logic: logo, heading text, superheading/subheading with independent links, and an optional menu popover with automatic chevron indicator.

props.name: logo
props.description: Logo element to display before the heading text. Can be an image, NavIcon, or any ReactNode.

props.name: heading
props.description: Product/app name displayed as the primary heading text.

props.name: headingHref
props.description: Link for the heading text (e.g. product home). When no menu is present and this is the only href, the whole heading becomes one clickable link.

props.name: superheading
props.description: Text above the heading (e.g. suite name). Rendered in a smaller secondary style.

props.name: superheadingHref
props.description: Link for the superheading text (e.g. suite home). When provided alongside a menu, renders as an independent inline link.

props.name: subheading
props.description: Text below the heading (e.g. account context). Rendered in a smaller secondary style.

props.name: subheadingHref
props.description: Link for the subheading text. When provided alongside a menu, renders as an independent inline link.

props.name: headerEndContent
props.description: Content rendered at the trailing edge of the heading row (e.g. a badge or status indicator).

props.name: menu
props.description: Menu content shown in a popover dropdown. When provided, a chevron indicator appears automatically. Interaction boundary is determined by the presence of hrefs: no hrefs means the whole header is the trigger; with hrefs, links are independent and the chevron area is the trigger.

props.name: as
props.description: Custom component to render instead of <a>. Overrides the provider-level default set by LinkProvider. Must accept href, className, style, and children props.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

components.name: TopNavItem
components.description: Navigation link item for use in TopNav startContent: renders as an anchor with hover and selected states.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the nav item. Rendered as visible text by default. When isIconOnly is true, used as aria-label instead.

props.name: href
props.description: Navigation target URL.

props.name: isSelected
props.description: Whether this nav item is currently selected. Sets aria-current="page" and applies highlighted styles.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the nav item is disabled. Sets aria-disabled, drops href/target so the item cannot navigate, and prevents interaction.

props.name: isIconOnly
props.description: Renders the item as a square icon-only element. When true, label becomes the aria-label and visible text is hidden. Requires icon to be set.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon to display before the label.

props.name: children
props.description: Custom content to render instead of the label text.

props.name: as
props.description: Custom component to render instead of <a>. Overrides the provider-level default set by LinkProvider. Must accept href, className, style, and children props.

components.name: TopNavMegaMenu
components.description: Navigation item that displays a full-width mega menu panel on hover. Uses a slots API with items and featured props. TopNavMegaMenuItem renders itself in both desktop and mobile drawer modes. Supports inline collapsible drawer via render mode context.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label for the trigger button.

props.name: items
props.description: Menu items slot: typically TopNavMegaMenuItem components, but accepts any ReactNode.

props.name: featured
props.description: Featured content slot: rendered in the right panel on desktop, below items in the mobile drawer.

props.name: delay
props.description: Delay in milliseconds before showing the menu on hover.

props.name: hideDelay
props.description: Delay in milliseconds before hiding the menu after the mouse leaves.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback fired when the mega menu opens or closes. Useful for coordinating wrapper styles.

components.name: TopNavMegaMenuFeaturedCard
components.displayName: Top Nav Mega Menu Featured Card
components.description: Standard featured card for the TopNavMegaMenu featured slot. Provides a consistent card with optional image, title, description, and CTA link.

props.name: title
props.description: Card title.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text below the title.

props.name: image
props.description: Optional image URL displayed above the body.

props.name: imageAlt
props.description: Alt text for the image. When omitted, the image is explicitly decorative (alt="", role="presentation", aria-hidden), usually correct since the card already has a visible title. Provide it only when the image conveys information beyond the title and description.

props.name: linkLabel
props.description: CTA link text.

props.name: linkHref
props.description: CTA link URL.

props.name: children
props.description: Custom content rendered below the standard body.

components.name: TopNavMegaMenuItem
components.description: An individual item inside an TopNavMegaMenu. Renders itself in both desktop (popover grid) and mobile drawer modes via render mode context.

props.name: title
props.description: Display title for the menu item.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional description text displayed below the title.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon element displayed to the left.

props.name: href
props.description: URL to navigate to when clicked.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Callback when item is clicked.

props.name: hasCloseOnSelect
props.description: Whether picking the item with the keyboard, a finger or a pen closes the mega menu panel and returns focus to its trigger (a mouse pick leaves it open). Set false for an action that reports its result on the item itself.

props.name: as
props.description: Custom component to render instead of <a> for link items. Overrides the provider-level default set by LinkProvider.

components.name: TopNavMenu
components.description: Navigation item that displays a hover-triggered popover menu with rich items containing an icon, title, and optional description.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label for the trigger button.

props.name: items
props.description: Menu items to display in the hover popover. Item href values follow the shared navigation rule described on Link; rejected destinations remain visible without navigation. Picking an item with the keyboard, a finger or a pen closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger (a mouse pick leaves it open); set the item's `hasCloseOnSelect` to false to keep the menu open for an action that reports its result on the item.

props.name: delay
props.description: Delay in milliseconds before showing the menu on hover.

props.name: hideDelay
props.description: Delay in milliseconds before hiding the menu after the mouse leaves.

components.name: TreeList
components.description: An expandable tree structure for displaying hierarchical data with branch connector lines. Use it for file explorers, nested category browsers, or any interface that visualizes parent-child relationships. Under a finger, expanding a row glides the rows below it while its children fade in on the same timing, and a collapse plays it back; pass an `animatedLayout` handle for content after the tree to glide too.

bestPractices.text: Provide meaningful labels and icons for each node to make the hierarchy easy to scan.
Pre-expand important branches so users see key content immediately.

Leaf rows reserve space for a chevron column whenever the tree has any expandable item to line up under; only a fully flat tree (no expandable items at all) renders its rows flush. Rely on this rather than nudging indentation with custom CSS.
Nest more than 4–5 levels deep; flatten the structure or use a different pattern.
Use a tree for flat, non-hierarchical data; use a List instead.

anatomy.name: Tree list
anatomy.description: Container that presents the hierarchical tree.

anatomy.name: Header
anatomy.description: Caller-provided content that visibly names the tree.

anatomy.name: Item
anatomy.description: Painted row for one node in the hierarchy.

anatomy.name: Chevron
anatomy.description: Expand and collapse control rendered for an Item with children.

anatomy.name: Chevron glyph
anatomy.description: Directional symbol rendered by Icon inside a Chevron.

anatomy.name: Item label
anatomy.description: Primary content that identifies an Item.

anatomy.name: Item description
anatomy.description: Secondary text rendered below an Item label.

anatomy.name: Start content
anatomy.description: Caller-provided content rendered before an Item label.

anatomy.name: End content
anatomy.description: Caller-provided content rendered after an Item label.

anatomy.name: Guide
anatomy.description: Connector line that shows parent-child relationships.

components.name: Typeahead
components.description: A searchable input for selecting a single item from a large or dynamic dataset. Results appear as the user types, with support for async data sources, debounced search, and custom item rendering. Use it when the option list is too large for a Selector dropdown.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the input.

props.name: searchSource
props.description: Data source providing search and bootstrap methods. `search(query, context)` may call `context.update(items)` to show matches it already has before it returns; the value it returns is the final list, and every list after the first for a query keeps the shown rows first and adds new rows after them.

props.name: value
props.description: Currently selected item, or null if nothing is selected.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when the selection changes.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Input placeholder text.

props.name: hasEntriesOnFocus
props.description: Show bootstrap results on focus before typing.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Show clear button to deselect the current value.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the input. The field keeps its tab stop: it is announced as disabled (aria-disabled), is read-only, and opens and picks nothing.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the input is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus, and the reason describes the field (activation stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled Typeahead in Tooltip, so the reason is attached to the field itself.

props.name: maxMenuItems
props.description: Maximum number of dropdown items to display.

props.name: minQueryLength
props.description: Minimum query length before the search source is queried. Below it no search runs and the menu stays closed.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status object with type and message for error/warning/success states.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip reveals the message in an info-tip button.

props.name: renderItem
props.description: Custom render function for dropdown items. Default renders TypeaheadItem.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text displayed below the label.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Marks the field as required.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Shows an optional indicator on the label.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text shown on the label.

props.name: emptySearchText
props.description: Content shown when the query matched nothing. Takes a ReactNode, so the dead end can carry a link or a create row. Announced in a polite live region as the text it renders, read from the DOM; aria-hidden parts stay out of both, and content that renders no text announces nothing. null counts as not given, like undefined, and falls through to the default; pass an empty string to render nothing.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Auto-focus the input on mount.

props.name: size
props.description: Input and token size.

props.name: debounceMs
props.description: Debounce delay in ms before triggering search. Set to 0 for synchronous sources, and for a source that shows local matches through `context.update` and delays its own server request.

props.name: onChangeQuery
props.description: Callback fired when the search query text changes.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback when the dropdown opens or closes.

props.name: menu
props.description: What the menu shows. role 'listbox' (default) is the result list; its optional render({listbox, query, isBusy, isEmptySearch, close}) places information such as a header or a hint around it, and anything a person acts on stays a result so the arrow keys reach it. role 'dialog' shows render({query, close}) in a dialog named by label that takes focus; Escape, an outside press or close() returns focus to where it was when the menu opened. Astryx owns the layer either way. Switching from listbox to dialog keeps the menu open: call handleRef.open() from onChange.

props.name: handleRef
props.description: Imperative handle: open() opens the menu (a dialog at once; a listbox shows or loads its results) and close() closes it. There is no controlled open state; onOpenChange reports changes.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon displayed at the start of the input; pass a built-in meaning such as 'search' (see `astryx docs icons`), an icon component, or an icon element.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the element that paints the border and background and holds icons and end controls. Never the native input.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Class name for the visual control box.

props.name: controlStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the visual control box.

bestPractices.text: Provide descriptive placeholder text that hints at what users can search for.
Show suggestions on focus when users benefit from seeing popular or recent options before typing.
Add a search delay for remote data sources to avoid excessive network requests.

For a remote source, show the matches the page already has at once: call `context.update(local)` in `search`, pass `debounceMs={0}`, delay the server request in the source, and return the server answer with the shown rows first.
Use inside InputGroup when the typeahead needs a single-line prefix or suffix addon.
Use for short, static option lists; use Selector for better discoverability.
Use for multi-selection; use Tokenizer instead.
Place multiple Typeaheads adjacent to each other without clear labels differentiating them.
Wrap a disabled Typeahead in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled triggers swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

anatomy.name: Field
anatomy.description: Standalone Field shell that provides the label and optional supporting content; omitted inside InputGroup.

anatomy.name: Input surface
anatomy.description: Painted control surface containing the editable input or the selected token.

anatomy.name: Icon-rendered start icon
anatomy.description: Optional leading icon, by built-in meaning or icon component, rendered through Icon.

anatomy.name: Caller-rendered start content
anatomy.description: Optional arbitrary React content rendered directly at the start of the input surface.

anatomy.name: Selected token
anatomy.description: Token that presents the selected item while the control is not in edit mode.

anatomy.name: Spinner
anatomy.description: Loading indicator shown at the end of the input surface while a search is in flight.

anatomy.name: Clear button
anatomy.description: Shared clear action that removes the selected item when hasClear is enabled.

anatomy.name: Status icon
anatomy.description: Error, warning, or success icon at the end of the input. With statusVariant tooltip it is a button that reveals the status message.

anatomy.name: Popup surface
anatomy.description: The layer the Dropdown opens in, above the page and anchored below the input.

anatomy.name: Dropdown
anatomy.description: Anchored listbox surface containing the current search results.

components.name: TypeaheadItem
components.description: Default dropdown item renderer for typeahead results. Shows label with optional icon, description, and avatar. Exported for use in custom renderItem implementations.

props.name: item
props.description: The search result item to render.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon or avatar to display before the label.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed below the label.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether this item is visually disabled.

props.name: group
props.description: This prop has no effect. Set `item.auxiliaryData.group` on search-source items to group results in Typeahead or BaseTypeahead.

components.name: useAnimatedLayout
components.description: Returns a handle to pass to a component whose size changes, such as TreeList or Collapsible. When that component changes size, it and the content after it inside `containerRef` animate together on one shared motion role. Fixed and stuck sticky elements stay put, the glide never scrolls the area, and Reduce Motion is respected. It applies under every pointer, a mouse included. Without the handle a component keeps its jump: content after it takes its place at once. Content after the change may mix Astryx components and your own elements; none of it opts in.

bestPractices.text: Create one handle per scroll container or panel and pass the same handle to every component in it whose size changes.
Pass the ref you already give ScrollableArea as containerRef; ScrollableArea does not register itself.
Wrap the content after a disclosure in an extra element to make it move; everything after the change inside the container moves on its own.
Animate height yourself alongside it; the glide moves content with a compositor translate and never animates height.

components.name: useAnimator
components.description: Animates one element with the motion Astryx's own components use. Call `animator.animate` to spring an element to new values on the state-change motion, `animator.decay` to fling it with the momentum of a released scroll view, and `animator.set` to move it directly, so a card can follow a finger, snap back and be thrown away. To animate an area's layout as its items change, use `useAnimatedLayout`; for what a component already animates, such as a sheet's detents or a carousel's snapping, use the component's own props. Outside React, use `createAnimator`.

bestPractices.text: Call the animator from event handlers and effects: it lives outside render, so animating never re-renders the component.
Start every `animate` that follows a drag with the release velocity, so the element carries on as it was thrown.
Reach every state an animation shows without the animation too: a key, a button or a menu item that calls the same code.
Keep the animated values in React state: read them with `animator.get()` when you need them.

accessibility.name: Keyboard and assistive technology
accessibility.description: An animator moves an element; it adds no way to act. Give every action an animation stands for a control a keyboard and a screen reader can reach, such as a button that discards a card, and have it call `animate`, which Reduce Motion turns into a fade in place. Keep `decay` for a throw the person made: Reduce Motion keeps the momentum of a coast, as it continues that throw. Keep focus on an element that stays on screen: move it before you fling its element away.

accessibility.name: Reduce Motion
accessibility.description: When the person asks for reduced motion, every call is planned for them. On a touch screen a move or a scale becomes a short opacity cross-fade: the element fades out where it was and fades back in where it lands. With a mouse it lands at once. A decay of `x` and `y` keeps its momentum, as it continues the throw the person made; a decay of `scale`, `rotate` or `opacity` is planned like a move. No option turns this off.

components.name: useAnnounce
components.description: Imperatively announces a message to screen readers through a visually-hidden live region. Use it for state that is only conveyed visually; search result counts, "no results", loading and saved confirmations, validation errors (WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages). The polite and assertive regions are created empty on first use and stay mounted, which is what makes announcements reliable: most screen readers ignore a live region that is inserted together with its content. Each message is cleared a couple of seconds after it is announced so stale status does not linger in the accessibility tree. A message is delivered where its caller is: from inside an open Astryx modal it goes to a region inside that modal and is heard there with no change to the calling code; a message sent just as the modal is dismissed is delivered through whatever is exposed afterwards rather than lost. A call made outside the modal, even by the component that renders it, uses the page-body region.

bestPractices.text: Reach for this instead of hand-rolling an aria-live div; a region rendered with its content usually does not announce at all.
Keep "polite" for status and result counts; reserve "assertive" for errors and time-sensitive alerts, since it interrupts whatever the screen reader is saying.
Announce the outcome, not the interaction; "12 results" rather than "search ran".
Send a value that keeps changing, such as a result count as the user types, through its own useAnnounce({hasReplace: true}) instance, so input faster than a frame says only the latest count.
Announce content that is already visible and correctly labeled in the DOM; that doubles up for screen reader users.

components.name: useAppShellMobile
components.description: Hook for reading and controlling AppShell mobile navigation state from descendants of AppShell. Use it for custom mobile nav triggers, closing the drawer after route changes, or coordinating AppShell-adjacent mobile experiences with the same breakpoint used by mobile nav.

bestPractices.text: Use inside the AppShell tree when building custom mobile navigation controls, route-aware nav items, or UI that should update at the same breakpoint as AppShell mobile nav.
Prefer MobileNavToggle for the standard hamburger trigger: use this hook when you need custom placement, styling, or extra behavior.
Call closeMobileNav after a custom mobile nav item changes route so the drawer dismisses cleanly.
Use as a general responsive primitive when the UI is not inside AppShell or does not need to align with AppShell mobile nav: use useMediaQuery instead.
Assume it throws outside AppShell. The hook returns safe defaults and no-op callbacks when no provider is present.

components.name: useCalendarConstraints
components.description: Provides date constraint validation for calendar views and custom range pickers. It combines boundary dates, span limits measured from an in-progress range start, and custom rules (such as weekly closures or blackout dates) into an isDateDisabled predicate. Calendar uses it internally to disable day buttons; use it directly when building bespoke scheduling interfaces or range pickers.

bestPractices.text: Pass rangeAnchor only after the user selects an initial range start, so all eligible start dates remain selectable before the first click.
Use dateConstraints for recurring or dynamic rules, such as disabling closed weekdays, past holidays, or sold-out dates.
Perform slow network calls or heavy calculations inside dateConstraints predicates, because isDateDisabled is evaluated synchronously for each day rendered in the grid.

components.name: useCalendarDays
components.description: Builds the day grid for one month: every date to show, including the previous and next months' days that fill the first and last weeks, grouped into weeks, plus localized weekday header names that start on weekStartsOn. It is the layout Calendar uses, for a custom month view such as a compact availability grid or a mini calendar. It returns data only: rendering, selection, keyboard navigation and the grid's accessibility semantics are the caller's.

bestPractices.text: Render dayNames as the header row so the header follows weekStartsOn and the locale together with the grid.
Style days with isOutside differently, for example dimmed, so the filler days read as part of the next or previous month.
Use it to build a date picker that people choose from; use Calendar, which adds selection, keyboard navigation and grid semantics.

components.name: useCalendarNavigation
components.description: Manages visible month state and pagination for calendar components. It provides previous/next month stepping, localized month-year header strings, and pending focus tracking so keyboard arrow navigation seamlessly moves focus across month boundaries into the adjacent month. Use it directly when composing custom calendar headers, pager controls, or dual-month availability pickers.

bestPractices.text: Wire navigateMonth(-1) and navigateMonth(1) to Previous/Next icon buttons to paginate months.
Pass focusedDate and offset (e.g. 1 for horizontal arrow keys, 7 for vertical arrow keys) to navigateMonth so pendingFocus directs keyboard focus to the correct day cell after the month transition.
Hardcode month-year header strings manually; use monthYearLabel which automatically formats according to the active locale and calendar system.

components.name: useChatDictation
components.description: Voice input for a chat composer. It wraps speech recognition with microphone level, start and stop cues, and optional interim text in a ChatComposerInput. Check isSupported before offering the control. A browser without speech recognition reports false and does not listen. Sustained loud speech turns the transcript to upper case.
