bestPractices.text: Pass inputRef when the words should appear in the composer. The hook inserts each final transcript there and still calls onResult.
Disable the control when isSupported is false, and say that this browser cannot take voice input.
Handle onError. It is the only signal that microphone permission was refused.
Call the browser SpeechRecognition API beside this hook. Use useSpeechRecognition only when the composer behavior is not wanted.

components.name: useChatPasteAsToken
components.description: Turns a long plain-text paste into a token chip in a ChatComposerInput. Short pastes are left for the composer to insert. Pass the returned object as pasteAsToken. The default threshold is 200 characters.

bestPractices.text: Keep the same ref on the composer handle and on this hook, so insertToken reaches that input.
Pass pasteAsToken={false} when every paste should stay inline text.
Insert the long paste as characters and also as a token. Returning true tells the composer the paste is already handled.

components.name: useClickableContainer
components.description: Makes a container element clickable while preserving nested interactive element behavior. Solves the "nested interactive elements" problem: when a card is clickable but contains buttons/links, clicking those should NOT trigger the card's action. Detects interactive ancestors between the click target and the container, and ignores text selections. Supports href navigation (including middle-click and Ctrl/Cmd+click for new tabs).

bestPractices.text: Attach onClick, onMouseUp and onPointerDown to the container element: full click handling including middle-click, and no touch pressed state for a press on a nested control.
Use inside ClickableCard or SelectableCard for the standard card interaction pattern.

For a pressable surface without Card chrome, such as a quoted message that jumps on press, compose it yourself: this hook on the surface; `usePressFeedback()` and `interactionOverlayStyles.backgroundColor` (from `@astryxdesign/core/utils`) on the same element for the hover tint and touch press; a native `<button>` (or an `<a>` for a destination) inside `VisuallyHidden` as the named control and interactiveRef; and `focusOutlineStyles.focusWithin` (from `@astryxdesign/core/utils`) on the surface for the shared focus ring, the one ClickableCard draws. The `Core/Hooks/useClickableContainer` story has the full recipe.
Use when the entire container is a single interactive element; just use a <button> or <a> directly.

components.name: useClipboard
components.description: Copy-to-clipboard behavior: the clipboard write, a transient isCopied flag with its own reset timer, and an optional polite screen-reader announcement. Extracted so every copy affordance is a thin control over one implementation instead of re-deriving the timer and announcement. Rapid re-copies restart the reset timer so the confirmation always lasts the full duration, and the timer is cleaned up on unmount. It also copies inside a sandboxed frame that refuses the async Clipboard API, with the browser copy command, inside the reader’s click or key press. CodeBlock and Timestamp build their built-in copy buttons on it; reach for it directly when building a copy affordance that is not a plain icon button (a menu item, a labeled text button, a copy-on-click value chip).

bestPractices.text: Drive the copied confirmation (copy → check icon, label swap) off the returned isCopied flag rather than tracking your own state.
Pass a localized announce message so the copy is spoken by screen readers; swapping the button aria-label alone is not reliably announced.
For the common compact icon copy button, render a ghost IconButton with a "Copy" tooltip and wire onClick to copy(); the tooltip stays "Copy" and the icon flip is the confirmation.
Track a separate copied useState alongside the hook; isCopied already reflects the copied window and resets itself.

components.name: useCollapsible
components.description: Reusable hook that encapsulates the collapsible state machine. Supports three modes: group-controlled (inside CollapsibleGroup), controlled (isOpen + onOpenChange), and uncontrolled (self-managed with defaultIsOpen). Used internally by Card and Section.

bestPractices.text: Use the hook directly when building custom collapsible components that need Astryx collapsible behavior without Collapsible wrapper.
For accordion behavior, wrap items in CollapsibleGroup and pass unique value props.
Pass local isOpen, defaultIsOpen, or onOpenChange expecting them to run for a value-bound group item; the group owns that state and notification path.
Implement your own open/close state when useCollapsible already provides it; the hook handles group coordination automatically.

components.name: useCollator
components.description: Returns the sanctioned locale-aware comparator for custom sorting. The collator is recreated when the provider locale or an option changes.

bestPractices.text: Reuse collator.compare in custom Table comparators and other user-visible string ordering.
Construct Intl.Collator directly or call localeCompare; those bypass the provider-backed locale contract.

components.name: useCombobox
components.description: Tracks the active option of a single-select combobox and handles its keys, while DOM focus stays on the control. It powers Selector and CommandPalette; use it to build a combobox those components do not cover, including one over a single-line text field you render yourself, such as a search field whose results replace a page section, or an “add people” field in a dialog. It renders nothing: you render the field, the listbox and the options, and spread `getFieldProps`, `getListboxProps` and `getOptionProps` onto them, or wire `role`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant` yourself from `onKeyDown` and `getItemId` for a control such as a button.

bestPractices.text: Render each option with `id={getItemId(index)}` and set the control's `aria-activedescendant` only while `isOpen` and `highlightedIndex` points at a rendered option, as CommandPalette does.
For type-to-select without a search field, run useTypeahead's handler first and fall through to this `onKeyDown` when it returns false, as Selector does.
For a field you render, spread the prop getters, and set the active option yourself when a new query changes the options: the first option so Enter picks it, or -1 so Enter stays the field’s.
Announce the number of results through useAnnounce when the options change for a new query (AST-075 DEC-2). When nothing matches, announce the words the field shows for it.
Render controls that are not options, such as a create button or an empty message, inside the listbox; render them beside it.
Move DOM focus onto the options; the active option is announced through `aria-activedescendant` while focus stays on the control.

accessibility.name: Focus stays in the field
accessibility.description: With the prop getters, moving the active option never moves focus out of the field. The field names the active option through `aria-activedescendant` and carries none while no option is active.

accessibility.name: Expanded state follows the list
accessibility.description: While the listbox renders, the field exposes `aria-expanded="true"` and `aria-controls` naming it. Otherwise it exposes `aria-expanded="false"` and references nothing.

accessibility.name: Roles
accessibility.description: The field is a `combobox` with `aria-autocomplete="list"`. The list is a `listbox` of `option`s with `aria-selected="true"` on the active one. You name the field and the listbox.

accessibility.name: Keys
accessibility.description: While the list shows, ArrowDown and ArrowUp move the active option and wrap; Enter picks an active option and only then stops the field’s own Enter; Escape, whatever modifier is held, hides the list without closing an enclosing dialog or popover on the same press. While it is hidden, ArrowDown shows it when there are options. An open field with no options still takes Escape, which closes the list, so render an empty message while it is open. Home, End, other chords such as Shift+Enter, and every other key reach the field.

accessibility.name: Input method
accessibility.description: No key moves, picks or hides while an input method is composing text.

accessibility.name: Pointer
accessibility.description: Moving the pointer over an option makes it active without moving focus; pressing an option picks it, and the field keeps focus through the press.

accessibility.name: Result count
accessibility.description: Yours to announce: compose useAnnounce (AST-075 DEC-2) so each new query announces the number of options, or that there are none, once and politely. For none, announce the words the field shows.

components.name: useContainerReveal
components.description: A headless hover/focus reveal primitive. Gives a container a scoped trigger that reveals (or conceals) content inside it when the container is hovered or receives keyboard focus: the classic "row actions appear on hover" pattern. The reveal is CSS-only: no hover state lives in React and hovering never triggers a re-render. The caller authors no StyleX for the reveal itself; the hook hands out the container and content styles, and a nested container shadows its ancestor, so nested containers never leak hover/focus into one another. Accessible by construction: revealed content is visually hidden at rest with position and opacity (never display:none), so it stays mounted, keeps its place in the tab order, and is announced to assistive technology; it reveals on :focus-within so keyboard users see it when tabbing in, stays visible under a coarse primary pointer (never gated behind hover there), and honors prefers-reduced-motion.

bestPractices.text: Destructure getContainerProps and getContentRevealProps; spread getContainerProps() on the container (via mergeProps with your own stylex.props) and getContentRevealProps() on the content to reveal.
Use for secondary affordances: reveal-on-hover row actions (edit/copy/remove on list or table rows) and overlay controls on a card or media tile (e.g. Thumbnail's remove button).
Gate the reveal with isEnabled when a consumer prop decides whether content is revealed on hover or always shown; it can change at any time.
Pass isLayoutPreserved for absolutely-positioned or overlay content to reserve its box and avoid layout shift when it appears.
Set a hoverDelay (100-250ms) on rows in a long list, so a cursor travelling across the list does not light up every row it passes; keyboard and touch still reveal immediately.

Reach for forceState when something other than the pointer owns the interaction (a drag, a scroll or motion gate, an open row menu), and forceVisibility when just one element should ignore the container.
Reach past the API into the hook's private custom properties (--_reveal-opacity and friends) to suppress a reveal; use forceState / forceVisibility, which survive a rename.
Use it to hide content that must always be discoverable; keep essential actions visible instead of gating them behind hover.

components.name: useDevWarning
components.description: Fires a dev-only "Component: message" console warning once per mount while the condition holds. It is the render-safe way for a component to flag misuse: warning straight from the render body repeats on every render, and gating it with state adds a re-render, so this uses a ref and an effect instead. For a warning outside a component, use the imperative devWarn utility.

bestPractices.text: Say what is wrong and what the builder should do instead; the message is the whole value of the warning.
Warn about combinations the types cannot express, such as two mutually exclusive props being set together.
Use it for anything a user could see or for runtime error handling; it is stripped from production builds.

components.name: useDirection
components.description: Reads the current text direction during render. Reach for this hook as a last resort when render-time direction is strictly required (such as canvas drawing that cannot use CSS logical properties). In order of preference, always favor: CSS logical properties (margin-inline, inset-inline); shared mirror styles for directional icons (CSS scaleX); and DOM reads for keyboard or gesture logic.

bestPractices.text: Prefer CSS logical properties and directional CSS mirroring before using useDirection.
Use useDirection when drawing on an HTML canvas or calculating non-CSS layout coordinates where the start edge depends on text direction.
Use useDirection to conditionally swap margins, paddings, or inline alignments that can be solved with CSS logical properties.

components.name: useDragToSnapPoints
components.description: Lets a drag move an element along one axis and settles it on snap points when the finger lifts, the way an iOS sheet settles on its detents: on the nearest snap point to where it is, on the next one in its direction after a quick flick, and back where it started when the finger was moving back. The settle continues the release's velocity. For a bottom sheet, use BottomSheet's `snapPoints`; for a scrolling row, Carousel's `hasSnap`. Outside React, use `createDragToSnapPoints`.

bestPractices.text: Offer the same positions without a drag: buttons or keys that call `settleTo`.
Keep the settled index in state from `onSettle`, and render what the position means from it.
Use it for a sheet or a carousel: their own props already settle the way people expect.

accessibility.name: Keyboard and assistive technology
accessibility.description: A drag is one way in, never the only one. Give each snap point a control a keyboard and a screen reader can reach, such as Expand and Collapse buttons, and call `settleTo` from it. When a position changes what the element shows, announce the change.

accessibility.name: Reduce Motion
accessibility.description: When the person asks for reduced motion, the settle after a touch drag becomes a short cross-fade into the snap point, as does any settle on a device whose primary pointer is coarse, such as a tablet; after a mouse or pen drag elsewhere it lands at once. `settleTo` fades on such a device and lands at once with a fine primary pointer. While the finger is down, the element still follows it.

components.name: useEntryAnimation
components.description: Returns a StyleX style for animating an element on mount. Only animates when the element is dynamically inserted after the initial page paint; elements rendered on page load are not animated. Uses Astryx motion tokens (duration, easing) for consistent animation timing. Server-rendered elements hydrate without the entry style and never animate; elements mounted after hydration animate.

bestPractices.text: Use for conditionally rendered elements like validation messages, toasts, or expanding sections.
Spread the returned style into stylex.props() alongside other styles.
Use for elements that should be visible on initial page load; they will not animate.

components.name: useFocusTrap
components.description: Traps focus within a container element following the WAI-ARIA dialog focus trap pattern. Listens to focus events on the document and redirects focus back into the container if a Tab from inside it moves focus out. Handles both Tab and Shift+Tab wrapping. A Tab pressed while focus is outside the container is left to the page, so an open non-modal surface never takes over the focus order of the page. When the trap deactivates or unmounts, focus is restored to the element that was focused before activation, unless focus was already moved elsewhere or never entered the trap (so popups that keep focus on their trigger, like comboboxes, are unaffected). Mouse clicks outside the container are not intercepted; use a light-dismiss handler for that.

bestPractices.text: Call focusFirst() when opening a dialog/modal to move focus into the trapped region.
Provide an onEscape callback to close the dialog when Escape is pressed.
Rely on the built-in focus restoration on close; only add your own onHide focus handling when you need to send focus somewhere other than the previously-focused element.
Use on non-modal content like tooltips or dropdowns; those need light-dismiss, not focus trapping.

components.name: useGridFocus
components.description: Manages keyboard navigation within a 2D grid following the WAI-ARIA grid pattern. Supports arrow keys for cell-to-cell navigation, Home/End for row boundaries, Ctrl+Home/Ctrl+End for grid boundaries, and Page Up/Down for custom callbacks (e.g., month navigation in calendars). Boundary navigation callbacks allow cross-grid navigation.

bestPractices.text: Use for calendar date grids: wire onPageUp/onPageDown to month navigation and onNavigateBefore/onNavigateAfter for cross-month arrow key navigation.
Attach both gridRef and handleKeyDown to the grid container element.
For roving-tabindex grids (e.g. Calendar), set hasRovingTabIndex: true and attach handleFocus to the container onFocus; seed one focus target with tabindex=0 and the hook repairs and moves it.
Use for simple linear lists; prefer useListFocus for 1D navigation.

components.name: useHotkeys
components.description: Registers global keyboard shortcuts with a single window keydown listener per hook instance. Handlers live in a ref, so re-renders never re-subscribe. Skips events from typing targets (input, textarea, select, contenteditable) unless allowInInputs, skips defaultPrevented events, and calls preventDefault() on match. SSR-safe.

bestPractices.text: Use for app-level shortcuts like command palettes (mod+k), help overlays ("?"), and navigation keys.
Pair with the Kbd component to display the same combo you register; both resolve "mod" per platform identically.
Use isDisabled to suspend shortcuts while a modal or wizard owns the keyboard, instead of unmounting the hook.
Use for focus-scoped keyboard navigation inside a widget; use useListFocus or useGridFocus instead.

components.name: useHoverCard
components.description: Headless hook for hover-triggered floating cards. Builds on useLayer with hover/focus intent detection, configurable delays, safe hover behavior, and accessible aria-describedby linking. Use for rich previews on hover when you need full control over the trigger or rendered content.

bestPractices.text: Use for rich content previews such as user profiles, entity summaries, and link previews.
Prefer the HoverCard component for standard trigger-content pairs; use the hook for custom trigger patterns.
Use for simple text hints: use Tooltip or useTooltip instead.

components.name: useIcon
components.description: Resolves a built-in meaning to a React node through the nearest Theme, so a custom component draws the same success, warning or error icon that Astryx components draw and follows a theme that overrides it. Resolution reads the nearest Theme's icons (outside any Theme, the registered theme the document root names), then registerIcons() overrides, then the built-in default. The node is returned as is, with no size or color wrapper: the built-in icons are 1em squares in currentColor, so they follow the surrounding text. A function entry is read at {size: 'md'}. Render <Icon icon={name} /> instead when the icon needs another size, a color or a label.

bestPractices.text: Use it in a custom component that places the icon for a built-in meaning itself, so a Theme that overrides the icon changes the component too.
Render <Icon icon={name} /> when the icon needs a size other than md, a color, or an accessible label.
Import a specific icon library glyph for a meaning that a theme should control, such as a success or error state.

components.name: useImageMode
components.description: Detects whether an image is predominantly dark or light by sampling pixels via OffscreenCanvas. Uses APCA perceptual lightness (sRGB linearization + power curve) for accurate detection, especially on saturated colors. Runs entirely off the paint path: no visible canvas, no layout thrash. Supports regional sampling for detecting luminance where text overlays will appear. Returns null while loading and falls back gracefully on CORS or network errors.

bestPractices.text: Pair with MediaTheme to automatically adapt text color over dynamic background images.
Use the region option to sample only the area where text overlays will appear for more accurate results.
Use for images that change rapidly (e.g., video frames); each src change triggers a new fetch and analysis.

components.name: useImperativeAlertDialog
components.description: Hook for showing an alert dialog without managing open state. Call alert.show(options) to open and alert.hide() to close. Render alert.element in your JSX tree.

props.name: show
props.description: Show the alert dialog with the given options. Options are the same as AlertDialog props minus isOpen/onOpenChange.

props.name: hide
props.description: Hide the alert dialog.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Whether the dialog is currently open.

props.name: element
props.description: The dialog element: render this in your JSX tree.

components.name: useImperativeDialog
components.description: Hook for showing a dialog without managing open state. Call dialog.show(content, options) to open and dialog.hide() to close. Render dialog.element in your JSX tree.

props.name: show
props.description: Show the dialog with the given content. Options are the same as Dialog props minus isOpen/onOpenChange/children.

props.name: hide
props.description: Hide the dialog.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Whether the dialog is currently open.

props.name: element
props.description: The dialog element: render this in your JSX tree.

components.name: useIndicatorFocusRing
components.description: Draws the standard focus ring on the indicator of a control whose real input is visually hidden; a checkbox or radio focuses an opacity-0 input, so the ring has to appear on the picture beside it. The ring is painted imperatively on the indicator's own element, which is the only element whose border-radius can shape it, and only on :focus-visible, so pointer clicks stay quiet. Owning it here means a theme-supplied indicator cannot ship a control with no visible focus (WCAG 2.4.7) by ignoring a prop.

bestPractices.text: Wrap only the indicator in the ref'd element; a wrapper holding label text would ring the whole row.
Spread focusProps on the element that contains the hidden input, not on the input itself.
Ask a themeable indicator to draw its own focus ring; a replacement that ignores the prop leaves the control with no visible focus.

components.name: useInputContainer
components.description: Makes an input container wrapper clickable, delegating focus to the inner input/textarea when the user clicks non-interactive areas (icons, padding, status indicators). Built on top of useClickableContainer, so nested interactive elements (clear buttons, calendar toggles, links) are handled safely; clicking them does NOT steal focus from the input. Automatically detects input type: text-like inputs receive .focus(), while other types (checkbox, radio, file) receive .click().

bestPractices.text: Use inside input wrapper components (TextInput, NumberInput, TimeInput, TextArea) to make the full container area clickable.
Attach both onClick and onMouseUp to the wrapper div for full interaction handling.
Use on bare inputs without a wrapper; there is no benefit if the input already fills the full clickable area.

components.name: useInputStatusIcon
components.description: Builds the on-field status affordance for a bordered input and its accessibility wiring, so every input in the family behaves the same for a given status. The attached variant renders a plain glyph and leaves the text to the message box; the detached variant renders nothing here, because the message box already carries its own icon; the tooltip variant renders a real focusable button whose tooltip is reachable by keyboard, pointer, touch and assistive tech. Use it when building a bordered input, not for field-level messaging.

bestPractices.text: Render statusIcon inside the input container and merge describedBy into the control's aria-describedby list.
Let it decide when nothing should render; pass isInGroup and the variant through rather than branching at the call site.
Use it to convey the status by icon alone; the tooltip variant is the only one that carries the message, so the others still need a message box.

components.name: useInteractiveRole
components.description: Resolves what a polymorphic component should render as, in one place: href wins, then onClick, then an interactive trigger context supplied by a parent (Popover, DropdownMenu and friends), then inert. Use it in any component that is sometimes a link, sometimes a button, and sometimes plain content; Token, Thumbnail, Item and ClickableCard all do. Because context is part of the resolution, a component built on it becomes a valid trigger for new surfaces without changing.

bestPractices.text: Switch on the returned role to pick the element, and render an anchor only for "link" so keyboard and middle-click behavior come from the platform.
Pass isDisabled through rather than dropping the href yourself; the hook already keeps disabled links out of the tab order.
Add another ad-hoc href/onClick precedence check in a component; new trigger contexts are added here so every consumer inherits them.

components.name: useKeyboardHint
components.description: Shows an ephemeral "← → to navigate" hint anchored to the focused item the first time a roving-tabindex composite (Toolbar, TabList, SegmentedControl, etc.) receives keyboard focus. It teaches sighted keyboard users that arrow keys move within the group. The hint renders arrow keys with Kbd in the top layer (popover="manual") and is CSS-anchor-positioned to the focused element, so overflow containers never clip it. It stays until the first arrow press, Escape, or blur, and does not re-show for that instance. Escape closes only the hint, through the shared layer dismissal stack, and keeps focus where it is. Toolbar, TabList, and SegmentedControl wire this in automatically; reach for the hook directly only when building a custom roving-tabindex widget.

bestPractices.text: Compose the returned onFocus/onKeyDown with your existing focus handlers rather than replacing them: call onKeyDown first (it only dismisses, never prevents), then your navigation handler.
Render hintElement as the last child of the composite container; it is position:fixed in the top layer and aria-hidden, so it never affects layout or the accessibility tree.
Match orientation to the arrow keys your widget actually responds to so the hint shows the correct icons.
Use for single controls or widgets without roving-tabindex navigation; the hint only makes sense where arrows move focus within a group.

components.name: useLayer
components.description: Core positioning hook for rendering overlay content using CSS Anchor Positioning and the Popover API. Use it as the foundation for custom popovers, hover cards, tooltips, and fixed-position layers when higher-level components are not enough. Both modes use theme body text defaults and end ancestor surface/group membership as a whole, including group-owned state. Explicit props and unrelated contexts remain unchanged. Apply intentional formatting through render styles or content, and establish complete content-local providers inside the rendered layer.

bestPractices.text: Use context mode for anchor-positioned overlays relative to a trigger element, and fixed mode for manually positioned overlays at specific coordinates.
Build on higher-level components like Popover, HoverCard, and Tooltip for common overlay patterns.

Rely on the Popover API top layer to escape ancestor clipping and stacking, and host the layer near its trigger rather than in the body so it inherits the trigger's theme cascade and keeps a natural focus order.
Implement ARIA patterns directly in a Layer unless you also own the full accessibility behavior.

components.name: useLightbox
components.description: State management and accessible trigger wiring for Lightbox. Eliminates boilerplate for managing open state and current index. Returns trigger props with button role, tabIndex={0}, aria-haspopup="dialog", and keyboard activation handlers, along with a pre-wired Lightbox element that handles dismissal, next/previous navigation, and focus restoration.

bestPractices.text: Spread getTriggerProps(index) onto image or thumbnail elements to give them accessible button semantics and keyboard activation.
Render lightbox.element once in your component JSX tree alongside the triggers.
Manage separate isOpen or index state alongside useLightbox; the hook already tracks both.
Add custom click or keydown handlers to open the lightbox when using triggerProps or getTriggerProps.

components.name: useLinkComponent
components.description: Resolves which component renders a link, so a custom component's links follow the app's router the same way Astryx's own links do. The order is the as argument, then the nearest LinkProvider's component, then a native anchor. Render the returned component with href (and to, for a router that reads it). Before rendering it checks both destinations under the Link href rule: a rejected destination renders an anchor with no destination, and a custom router is never invoked with it. A custom component receives to={href} unless to is passed explicitly.

bestPractices.text: Use it for links inside a custom component, so a LinkProvider wired to the router reaches them without a prop on every link.
Pass as='a' for a destination the router cannot handle, such as a file download or a page outside the app.
Import the router's link directly in a shared component; the component then ignores LinkProvider and the destination check.

components.name: useLinkify
components.description: Finds URLs, email addresses and custom patterns in plain text and returns React nodes with a Link for each match; the links respect LinkProvider for client-side routing. Use it wherever user- or tool-authored plain text should grow safe, styled links without pre-parsing it into markup: activity feeds, comment threads, description fields. Custom patterns turn project-specific references (issue numbers like #123, ticket IDs) into links by supplying a regex plus an href builder — e.g. an issue tracker pattern that maps captures onto its URL scheme. When matches overlap, the earliest one wins, and at the same start a custom pattern wins over the built-in ones, so a custom #123 pattern coexists with URL detection in the same string.

bestPractices.text:
Render the returned nodes directly inside a text container (

{nodes}

); the hook already interleaves the unmatched plain text.
Wrap the app (or the region) in LinkProvider so detected links route client-side instead of full-page navigating.
Give a custom pattern the global flag (g). Without it the scan never advances, and when the text contains a match the render never finishes.
Pre-parse the text into your own markup before linkifying — the hook exists so the plain string can be rendered as-is with links composed in.

components.name: useListFocus
components.description: Manages keyboard navigation within a linear list following WAI-ARIA menu/listbox/toolbar patterns. Supports arrow key navigation (vertical, horizontal, or both), Home/End for boundaries, optional wrap-around, RTL, and Escape to close. Opt into hasRovingTabIndex for composite widgets (toolbars, segmented controls, tab strips) that own a single tab stop. Suitable for dropdown menus, toolbars, and any 1D focusable list.

bestPractices.text: Set orientation to 'horizontal' for toolbars and tab bars, 'vertical' for dropdown menus.
Provide an onEscape callback for menus/dropdowns to return focus to the trigger.
Enable hasRovingTabIndex (and hasCaretGuard when the widget can contain text inputs) for toolbar-style composites that should be a single tab stop.
Use for 2D grid navigation; prefer useGridFocus for grids and calendars.

components.name: useLocale
components.description: Reads the authoritative Astryx locale. Use it to thread the provider locale into pure formatting helpers and sibling-package APIs; do not derive a second locale from navigator.language or a hardcoded literal.

bestPractices.text: Pass the returned locale to pure Astryx helpers or package APIs that require an explicit locale.
Use navigator.language or a hardcoded display locale as a fallback; InternationalizationProvider is the locale source.

components.name: useLongPress
components.description: Detects a single-finger press-and-hold and reports where it happened, so touch users can reach affordances that a pointer gets from right-click. iOS Safari never synthesizes a contextmenu event on long-press, which makes this the only touch route into a cursor-positioned surface such as ContextMenu. The press cancels on movement, lift, multi-touch or unmount. The hold is timed on the touch events’ own timestamps: when a busy page handles the lift late, a finger held for the full delay still reports its long press, before the lift acts.

bestPractices.text: Use the reported point to position the surface you open, so it appears under the finger.
Pair it with the pointer contextmenu handler rather than replacing it; this hook only covers touch.
Use it for the primary action of a control; press-and-hold is undiscoverable as the only way to do something.

components.name: useMediaQuery
components.description: SSR-safe media query hook that subscribes to window.matchMedia changes. Returns whether the given media query matches. Always returns false on first render for SSR compatibility. Where `window.matchMedia` is missing, it returns its server default and never throws.

bestPractices.text: Use for responsive layout switching based on viewport width, color scheme, or motion preferences.
Prefer Astryx responsive tokens and component props over manual breakpoint logic when possible.
Use for server-rendered content that must match on first paint; the hook always returns false initially.

components.name: useMenuPress
components.description: The press model of macOS and iOS menus, for any pointer: the row under the pointer when it is RELEASED is the row that acts, the highlight follows the pointer while it is held, a mouse opens the menu on press and can drag straight into it, and a finger or a pen opens it while still down: as it presses with no delay given, picking a row only after moving 10 px, or else once it is held for the delay. The pointer is tracked at document level by pointerId, so a finger that slid off the row it landed on is still followed; the click the browser reports at the end of a touch, aimed at the row where the touch began, is swallowed so nothing acts twice. DropdownMenu, ContextMenu, DropdownMenuSubMenu, Selector and the menu bottom sheet already mount it; reach for it directly only when building a menu-like surface of your own.

bestPractices.text: Pass a selector for ENABLED rows only, so a disabled row or a divider under the pointer clears the highlight instead of lighting up.
Let the default highlight move focus in a menu; supply onHighlight only for a listbox that must keep focus on its combobox and highlight through aria-activedescendant.

Declare touch-action on the menu root: pinch-zoom when its rows fit, pan-y pinch-zoom when it scrolls, so the browser — not the hook — decides when a finger is scrolling, and a two-finger pinch still zooms the page.
Act on a row from its own pointerdown or pointerup handler as well; the hook already activates the row under the release, and a second path acts twice.
Read a row click with detail 0 as a keyboard activation; the hook dispatches its pointer activation with detail 0 too. Use isMenuPressActivation() to tell them apart.

components.name: useMergedRefs
components.description: Combines multiple object or callback refs into one stable callback ref. Use it when a component must forward a consumer ref while also attaching internal refs. Unlike calling mergeRefs during render, the callback identity stays stable across unrelated rerenders, so React does not detach and reattach the element.

bestPractices.text: Use useMergedRefs when one element must receive both a forwarded ref and one or more internal refs.
Call mergeRefs directly in a JSX ref prop; that creates a new callback on every render and forces unnecessary detach and attach work.

components.name: useMultiCombobox
components.description: Tracks the active option of a multi-select combobox and handles its keys, while DOM focus stays on the control. It powers MultiSelector; unlike useCombobox, toggling an option keeps the list open, and rows can carry an action cell. It renders nothing and sets no attributes: the caller renders the control and the list, and wires the ARIA attributes from what it returns.

bestPractices.text: Render each option with `id={getItemId(index)}` and pass `activeDescendantId` as the control's `aria-activedescendant`.
Use `isGrid` only when rows carry a control next to the option; give each action cell `id={getActionCellId(index)}`.
Announce the number of results through useAnnounce when the options change for a new query.
Close the list after each toggle; a multi-select stays open so several options can be picked in a row.

components.name: useOutlineFromDOM
components.description: Builds outline items from the headings already in the page. Use it when the article is not a Markdown string, and pass the items to Outline. The list updates when headings are added, removed, renamed, or given a new id. A null ref returns an empty list.

bestPractices.text: Put an id on every heading the outline should list. A heading with no id, or with no text, is omitted.
Point the ref at the article, not the page, so headings outside the article stay out of the outline.
Expect the hook to invent ids. It only reads the ids the headings already have.
Use it for a Markdown string. useOutlineFromMarkdown follows the same parser and slugs as Markdown.

components.name: useOutlineFromMarkdown
components.description: Extracts the headings of a Markdown string for an Outline next to the rendered document. It uses the parser and heading slugs that Markdown uses, so in a complete document each item links to its heading, and fenced code never counts as a heading. The result is memoized on the source and the options. Outside React, use parseOutlineFromMarkdown.

bestPractices.text: Pass the same string, plugin list and finality to Markdown and this hook, so items match the rendered headings once the content is complete.
Declare the plugin list outside the component or memoize it. A new array on each render recomputes the outline.
For several documents on one page, install one createMarkdownHeadingLinks per document with headingIdPrefix, so their ids do not collide.
Write the items by hand or find headings with a regular expression. They drift from the rendered ids.
Expect every item to have a target while content streams. Markdown reveals text gradually and trims unfinished syntax, so a heading can be absent or have another id until the content is complete.

Expect an item to link to a heading that cites a Markdown sources entry. The hook does not receive sources, so the ids differ: for '# Intro [ref]', Markdown renders intro and the hook returns intro-ref.
Expect an item for a nested heading, such as one in a blockquote. Only root headings become items.

components.name: useOverflow
components.description: Measures children rendered in a hidden container to determine how many fit in the available width without flickering. Uses ResizeObserver to react to container and measured-child size changes. The measurement container should hold all items plus an optional overflow indicator element (identified by a data-overflow-indicator attribute).

bestPractices.text: Render all items into the measureRef container (hidden) and only the first visibleCount items into the containerRef container (visible).
Include an overflow indicator (e.g., "+N more" button) as the last child of the measurement container with a data-overflow-indicator attribute.
Use for vertical overflow; this hook measures horizontal width only.

components.name: useOverlay
components.description: Adds overlay behavior to a container you already render, such as a Card or a custom media frame, without the wrapper Overlay adds. Spread containerRef and containerProps on the container, then render element (or renderOverlay(children)) once inside it. The scrim is absolutely positioned, so it covers the nearest positioned ancestor: the container itself, or a positioned section inside it such as an image area. Visibility is CSS-driven from the container's :hover and :focus-within, so with showOn 'hover' a keyboard user reveals the content by moving focus into the container. On a device with a mouse or trackpad, content that a hover or focus reveal hides stays in the tab order, so Tab reaches an action in it and focus reveals the scrim. On a touch-primary device a hover overlay stays inert until a tap. A revealed scrim takes pointer input over the area it covers, so keep any other control in the container outside the scrim, or use a top or bottom strip and keep the control in the part the strip leaves uncovered.

bestPractices.text: Use showOn 'hover' for actions on media cards: it also reveals on keyboard focus within the container.
Give an overlay action a label that names what it does. With a mouse or trackpad, Tab reaches it while the overlay is hidden, and focus reveals the overlay.
Use the Overlay component when you do not already have a container element to attach to.

Put information people need to choose the item, such as its title or price, only in a hover or focus overlay; on a touch device a hover overlay shows only after a tap, and a focus overlay does not show.

components.name: usePanGesture
components.description: Reports a drag on an element as values, for a surface the product moves itself: a card that follows the finger, a drawer pulled by its handle. A finger, a mouse and a pen all drive it. A mouse or pen drag that starts on selectable text selects that text, and the pan reports nothing. Give that text `user-select: none`. The drag claims its touch at UIKit’s 10 pt, as `UIPanGestureRecognizer` does, so a tap stays a tap, and a press or a long press is never reported as a pan. With `axis`, a scroll across that axis that starts on the element stays the page’s; without it, the pan takes a drag in any direction, so a finger’s scroll that starts on the element moves the element instead of the page. A trackpad scroll still scrolls the page. The hook is a thin layer over `createPanGesture`, the same API for code without React. A drag has no keyboard or assistive-technology path of its own: whatever the drag does needs another way to do it, such as buttons or arrow keys (WCAG 2.5.7). The pan moves nothing itself, so Reduce Motion applies to the motion you drive from it: honor the user’s reduced-motion setting in the animation that moves the element. Where a component already offers the behavior, use its prop instead: BottomSheet’s `snapPoints`, Carousel’s `hasSnap`.

bestPractices.text: Move the element from `translation` added to where it was when the drag began, so it moves with the finger from the moment the drag claims it.
At `ended`, hand `velocity` to the animation that settles the element, so a flick carries on at the speed it was released.
Give every drag another way to do the same thing from a keyboard and from assistive technology, such as buttons, arrow keys or a menu.
Use a component's own prop when it covers the job: BottomSheet's `snapPoints` for a sheet, Carousel's `hasSnap` for paging.
Hold the drag offset in a large component’s state: each `changed` event renders the component that holds it.
Recognize taps or long presses with it; `useLongPress` and the components’ own press handling own those.

accessibility.name: Keyboard and assistive technology
accessibility.description: A drag has no keyboard or assistive-technology path of its own: whatever the drag does needs another way to do it, such as buttons, arrow keys or a menu.

accessibility.name: Reduce Motion
accessibility.description: The pan moves nothing itself, so Reduce Motion applies to the motion you drive from it: a settle or a throw goes to its end without travel when the person asks for reduced motion.

components.name: usePopover
components.description: Headless hook for click-triggered popovers with focus trapping. Combines useLayer with useFocusTrap, auto-focus, light dismiss, Escape handling, and an optional hidden close button for accessible dialog-like popover behavior. Every painted surface emits the canonical popover target. A custom composition needing a distinct stable seam should pass and document its own surfaceTarget.

bestPractices.text: Use for interactive content such as menus, pickers, forms, and command panels that need focus management.
Prefer the Popover component for standard trigger-content pairs; use the hook for custom trigger patterns.
Do not add your own focus return: the hook returns focus as the popover closes, to the opener or a stand-in, and has no option to turn that off.
Use popover as the broad canonical surface target.
When a custom composition needs its own theme refinement, pass and document an owned surfaceTarget such as selector-popup. It refines the Popover surface rather than creating another anatomy part.
Use for non-interactive hover previews: use useHoverCard or useTooltip instead.

components.name: usePowerSearchConfig
components.description: Memoizes a PowerSearch configuration built from typed field definitions and returns it along with an applyFilters function for client-side filtering. Automatically maps field types (string, number, boolean, date, enum, etc.) to their canonical operators and provides an efficient predicate evaluator to filter datasets.

bestPractices.text: Declare field definitions as const outside the component or memoize them so usePowerSearchConfig only recalculates when needed.
Pass the returned config to PowerSearch and use applyFilters to compute the filtered data rows for a Table or List.
Recreate field definitions inline on every render without as const or memoization.

components.name: usePressFeedback
components.description: The touch press model every Astryx pressable uses, for a local component that paints its own press. Under a finger, CSS `:active` paints on the touch itself and can outlive the start of a scroll; the press model instead tracks the touch the way UIKit tracks a control: it highlights as the finger lands (after the content-touch delay inside a scroller, where a flick paints nothing), a quick tap answers at the lift, and a scroll that takes the touch cancels it with no fade. One document-level controller does this for every marked element (installed by the first pressable to mount, removed by the last to unmount), so calling the hook adds no listener or state to your element. On a desktop a mouse press is still your `:active` rule: keep it, and drop it under `@media (pointer: coarse)` the way the built-in components do. That query reads the primary pointer, so on a phone or tablet it also drops `:active` for a connected mouse, trackpad or keyboard; the controller paints those presses there (at once, faded at the release), so nothing goes unanswered.

bestPractices.text: Spread the result on the element whose background paints the press and compose one of `interactionOverlayStyles` on it; the composed style is the instant onset, the hold and the fade, and it is themed through `--color-overlay-pressed`.

Let the composed style own the press on every pointer: it keeps `:active` for a desktop mouse and drops it under `@media (pointer: coarse)`, where the controller paints every press (a finger through the press model, a mouse or Space key at once). A rule of your own that paints `:active` would paint under a finger too, on the touch and through a scroll.
Add a pointer listener or React state to the element to track the press; the controller already writes the attribute, and per-element listeners are what a long list cannot afford.
Call it for a control rendered by an Astryx component; those are marked already, and the innermost marked element takes the press.

components.name: useResizable
components.description: Hook for adding drag-to-resize behavior to layout regions. Supports single-region and multi-region configurations with snap points, collapsible panels, localStorage persistence, and cascade resize ordering.

bestPractices.text: Use percent(40, {min: pixel(333)}) for a 40% size with a 333px floor, or percent(10, {max: pixel(400)}) for a 10% size with a 400px ceiling. The options argument is required and carries a floor XOR a ceiling.
A structured default is an initial choice only; a structured minSize or maxSize remains live. State, persistence, callbacks, resize(), paint, and ARIA all use resolved pixel numbers.

Import percent and Table’s same pixel binding from @astryxdesign/core/Resizable/utils when constructing configuration in a Server Component; the root package exposes one pixel symbol and one percent symbol without collision.
Use with Layout or AppShell sidebar for resizable navigation panels.
Set autoSaveId to persist user-chosen sizes across page reloads.
Set minSize too small; content becomes unreadable. Prefer collapsible for panels that can hide entirely.

components.name: useScrollableArea
components.description: Adds canonical axis-aware scroll behavior to structure owned by the caller. An axis is effective only when its computed overflow is scroll-capable and geometry exceeds the shared 1px tolerance. Both viewport and content boxes are observed.

bestPractices.text: Pass already-resolved props and refs through both prop getters, then spread each returned object once.
Use viewport keyboard ownership only when the viewport itself should enter the tab order; provide a concise accessible label.

Use contentOrViewport to delegate forward Tab entry to the first sequential native link or button when it preserves native scroll keys. Inputs, composite widgets, and nested scroll areas retain the named viewport stop. Shift+Tab from the delegated first child skips the viewport; pointer and programmatic focus stay on it.

Use content keyboard ownership when your integration already supplies keyboard access to the full scroll range. Automatic delegation checks current content at each keyboard entry without continuously tracking its focusability.
Pass caller `xstyle` through `getViewportProps`; the getter composes it with fitting clip, active overflow, and Sticky containment.
Give a viewport-owned tab stop a visible focus indicator; compose `focusOutlineStyles.focusVisible` (or an equivalent) into the viewport `xstyle`, as ScrollableArea does.
Attach only the viewport getter. A real observed content box is required for live overflow changes.
Declare overflow through caller props on the viewport; the getter owns overflow declarations and strips conflicting inline values.

components.name: useScrollLock
components.description: Locks page scroll while active and keeps the page where it is. The page gets overflow: hidden (on the root, or on body when its own overflow is the one the viewport uses), which stops wheel, keyboard and scrollbar scrolling, and overscroll-behavior-y: none on the root and body, which stops the overscroll bounce while the lock holds. Where the primary pointer is coarse (phones and tablets), a one-finger pan that would scroll the page is cancelled, because iOS Safari scrolls an overflow: hidden page under a finger; pans that a scroller inside the overlay can take, drags on a native range input, pinch-zoom, and one-finger drags on a pinch-zoomed page (which pan the zoomed view) still work. The scroll offset never changes, so nothing jumps when the lock starts or ends, and iOS Safari keeps its toolbar as it was. Where the hidden scrollbar takes layout space (desktop), the hook holds its gutter open with scrollbar-gutter: stable, so the page, including any position: fixed chrome, does not shift sideways.

bestPractices.text: Use when opening full-screen modals or dialogs to prevent background content from scrolling.
Pass the same boolean that controls dialog visibility (e.g., isOpen) as the isLocked parameter.
Use for non-modal overlays like popovers or tooltips; users should be able to scroll away from those.

components.name: useScrollOverflow
components.description: Tracks scroll overflow state for a horizontally scrollable container. Returns a ref callback and state booleans that update as the user scrolls, the container resizes, or its content changes (a child added, removed or resized, or a new gap or padding). Uses scroll event listeners, ResizeObserver and MutationObserver for reactive updates. Tolerance of 1px is applied to avoid sub-pixel false positives.

bestPractices.text: Use to show/hide scroll navigation buttons or fade edges on carousels and horizontal lists.
Apply the scrollRef to a container with overflow-x: auto or overflow-x: scroll.
Use for vertical scroll tracking; this hook only measures horizontal overflow.

components.name: useSnapPaging
components.description: Gives a Carousel iOS paging on native snap's stops: pass the value as hasSnap={useSnapPaging()}. Under a finger and on a trackpad swipe, a flick moves one view, or one item with {pages: 'item'}, and the row rests on an item's start edge. A mouse wheel keeps native snapping. Only a carousel given the value loads the paging code.

bestPractices.text: Use it for a row read one view at a time, such as onboarding screens or a photo strip, where a fast flick must not skip past the next view.
Pass {pages: 'item'} when several items show at once and each flick should move only one of them.
Use it for a row people scan quickly; plain hasSnap keeps native momentum, which can pass several items in one swipe.

components.name: useSpeechRecognition
components.description: A headless speech-recognition control. It does not write into a composer. Read the transcript from interimTranscript and onResult, and draw your own UI from isListening and volume. Check isSupported first. useChatDictation adds composer interim text and start and stop cues on top of this hook.

bestPractices.text: Hide or disable the control when isSupported is false.
Use onResult for the committed transcript. interimTranscript changes while the person is still speaking.
Use this hook to fill a ChatComposerInput. useChatDictation owns that interim text.

components.name: useStreamingText
components.description: Smooths bursty streamed text into a steady character-by-character reveal using requestAnimationFrame. Decouples arrival rate from display rate. Advances on word and syntax boundaries to avoid slicing mid-markdown or mid-word, preventing visual glitches with markdown renderers. Animation timing derives from Astryx motion tokens via useTheme when available, with sensible fallbacks outside a theme provider. Snaps to full text when isStreaming becomes false.

bestPractices.text: Pass the accumulated text (not individual chunks) as targetText; the hook handles incremental reveal internally.
Set isStreaming to false when the stream completes to snap to the final text.
Use speed='instant' for non-animated contexts like search results or when reduced motion is preferred.
Use for static text that does not change; the hook adds unnecessary overhead for non-streaming content.

components.name: useSyntaxTheme
components.description: Reads syntax colors for a canvas or other drawing that cannot use the CSS variables SyntaxTheme sets. Call it under a SyntaxTheme. It returns null when that provider is absent, so the caller can skip drawing.

bestPractices.text: Render the drawing under the same SyntaxTheme that colors the surrounding code.
Check for null before reading token. The hook returns null with no SyntaxTheme above it.
Copy syntax colors into the canvas by hand. They drift from the active syntax theme.

components.name: useTableColumnResize
components.description: Hook that returns a TablePlugin adding draggable resize handles to column header borders. T is the row type; TypeScript cannot infer it from the config, so it defaults to Record<string, unknown>, which a Table with typed rows rejects: pass it, as in `useTableColumnResize<Walk>(…)` for `<Table<Walk>>`. Supports pointer + keyboard (WAI-ARIA window splitter) resizing, RTL, per-column min/max widths, and proportional-column preservation (resizes the neighbor so the table stays full-width). Commits widths on release.

props.name: columnWidths
props.description: Controlled pixel-width overrides keyed by column key. When a key is present it overrides the column's declared width.

props.name: onColumnResizeEnd
props.description: Called when a resize completes (pointerup / Enter). Receives a map of every column key whose width changed; merge it into your columnWidths state.

props.name: minWidth
props.description: Global minimum column width in pixels during resize. Overrides per-column defaults when set.

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: Global maximum column width in pixels during resize.

props.name: columns
props.description: Column definitions, needed to derive per-column min widths and detect proportional vs pixel columns for neighbor/last-column resize behavior.

components.name: useTableColumnSettings
components.description: Headless column visibility and ordering management for Table. T is the row type; TypeScript cannot infer it from the config, so it defaults to Record<string, unknown>, which a Table with typed rows rejects: pass it, as in `useTableColumnSettings<Walk>(…)` for `<Table<Walk>>`. When the column keys have a narrower type than string (a union, or keys that useTableColumnSettingsState infers from its columns), pass both: `useTableColumnSettings<Walk, WalkColumnKey>(…)`. Provides filtered columns, toggle helpers, and pre-built MultiSelector options for a column picker UI.

props.name: columns
props.description: All available columns with metadata for the settings UI. Each entry has key, label, optional isAlwaysVisible and group.

props.name: activeColumnKeys
props.description: Currently active column keys, in display order. Only columns with keys in this array are shown.

props.name: onChangeActiveColumnKeys
props.description: Called when active columns change (toggle, reorder).

props.name: defaultColumnKeys
props.description: Default column set for "Reset to default". When omitted, reset shows all columns.

components.name: useTableColumnSettingsState
components.description: Headless column visibility and ordering state management for Table. Manages which columns are active, provides toggle and reset operations, and produces a config object that feeds directly into useTableColumnSettings. Renderer-agnostic and pairs with any column picker UI.

bestPractices.text: Pass columnSettingsConfig directly to useTableColumnSettings and give the resulting plugin to Table.
Mark essential identifier columns (like name or ID) with isAlwaysVisible: true so users cannot accidentally hide them.
Mutate activeColumnKeys array directly; use toggleColumn, showAllColumns, or resetToDefault.

components.name: useTableColumnsVirtualization
components.description: Returns an opaque capability for Table column windowing. Pass the capability to Table.virtualization and keep the complete data, columns, explicit stable idKey and plugins on Table. Columns keep their declared widths: an overflowing Table renders at its minimum width, and the window uses the width each column has there. Pinned columns from useTableStickyColumns always mount; only the columns between the pinned runs window, with a few overscan columns on each side. When the Table's scroll area is at least as wide as the Table's minimum width, every column mounts. A focused cell keeps its column mounted while it scrolls out of view, until focus leaves the Table or moves to another cell. Changing column order, widths, visibility or pinning keeps the first visible column and its scroll offset. Supported tables have one header row, flat rows, no cell that spans columns and single-line content; explicit wrapping, arbitrary custom renderers, non-flat rows, invalid identity, a caller-provided scrollWrapper or a min-width wider than the column floors render every column. To window rows and columns together, pass both capabilities as a list: Table.virtualization={[rows, columns]}. Mounted cells keep native table semantics and full-table column positions; unmounted columns are not promised screen-reader discovery. Keep the capability on the Table for its whole life: adding or removing it remounts the table, which resets focus and scroll position. Changing initialViewportWidth does not remount it.

props.name: initialViewportWidth
props.description: The inline viewport width in CSS pixels that the first window plans for, on the server and before the viewport is measured. It does not size the Table: after mount, the measured width of the Table's scroll area sets the window. Table accounts for its pinned columns.

components.name: useTableFiltering
components.description: Table plugin that adds inline column filters with popover or inline controls. T is the row type; TypeScript cannot infer it from the config, so it defaults to Record<string, unknown>, which a Table with typed rows rejects: pass it, as in `useTableFiltering<Walk>(…)` for `<Table<Walk>>`. Pairs with useTableFilterState for managed state. Supports text, select, multi-select, date, and number filter types via PowerSearch field definitions. The plugin renders the filter controls only; it does not remove rows. Filter the data yourself (toSearchFilters with applyFilters from usePowerSearchConfig) and pass the result to Table. When no row matches, Table shows its emptyState prop.

props.name: filters
props.description: Current filter state: map from column key to filter value.

props.name: onFilterChange
props.description: Called when the user changes a filter value. null clears the filter.

props.name: variant
props.description: Display variant for filter controls.

props.name: searchConfig
props.description: Defines the filter fields. A column sets `filter: '<field key>'` to show the control for that field. Build it with usePowerSearchConfig or createPowerSearchConfig; PowerSearch can use the same config.

components.name: useTableFilterState
components.description: Managed state hook for table filtering. Returns filters (the current filter map), onFilterChange, and clearAll (clears every filter, for example from a "Clear filters" button in the Table emptyState). Pass filters and onFilterChange to useTableFiltering.

props.name: initialState
props.description: Optional initial filter state map.

components.name: useTableGroupedRows
components.description: Hook that groups a flat data array into collapsible section rows. Each distinct groupBy value becomes a full-width section-header row with a chevron toggle, the group label, and a member count; collapsing hides that group's data rows while keeping the header visible. The disclosure state lives on the chevron button, not the native table row. Mirrors useTableTreeState: the consumer owns the collapsedGroups set and the hook returns {data, plugin, idKey}: pass them to Table as data, plugins, and idKey respectively. Grouping runs on the rows you hand it, so with pagination the order is filter, sort, slice, then group: sort by the group key first and the user's keys second, so a section's rows stay contiguous and each page appends to the bottom of the table instead of splicing rows in above the reader. A page that ends on a row count still cuts mid-section, and the heading then counts what has loaded rather than what exists: "6" quietly becoming "10". Where the full result set is in hand, carry the cut forward to the end of the section it lands in: every rendered section is then whole and its count is a total.

props.name: data
props.description: The flat data to group.

props.name: groupBy
props.description: Derive the group key for a row. Rows with the same key share a section.

props.name: collapsedGroups
props.description: Set of currently-collapsed group keys.

props.name: onToggleGroup
props.description: Called with a group key when its header is toggled.

props.name: renderGroupHeader
props.type: (groupKey: string, count: number, collapsed: boolean) => ReactNode
props.description: Custom renderer for a group header's content (right of the chevron). Defaults to `<groupKey> (<count>)`.

props.name: getRowKey
props.description: Stable key for a real row. Falls back to a positional key when omitted.

props.name: groupOrder
props.description: Explicit group ordering; groups not listed keep first-seen order after these.

components.name: useTableInfiniteScroll
components.description: Call useTableInfiniteScroll<T>({hasMore, isLoading, onLoadMore}) and pass the result to <Table plugins={{infiniteScroll: plugin}} />. T is the row type; TypeScript cannot infer it from the config, so it defaults to Record<string, unknown>, which a Table with typed rows rejects: pass it, as in `useTableInfiniteScroll<Walk>(…)` for `<Table<Walk>>`. Keep accumulated rows in your own state. onLoadMore must return a Promise<void> that settles when the batch work completes. A fulfilled request finishes after settlement and a subsequent committed isLoading=false; a true loading phase is not required. Visible short batches can automatically request again in a later task, so update hasMore when the source is exhausted. A resolved request that appends no rows must not incorrectly claim endless more data. Throws, rejections and invalid non-Promise results pause automatic loading; the manual Button can retry once controlled loading is false. The hook does not render product errors or cancel transport. For a new dataset, key and remount the component owning both the hook and its Table, not only the Table child; prevent stale responses from committing caller data yourself. Children mode and unsupported row models do not load and emit a deduplicated development warning. Body modifiers must declare compatible rowModel: flat. Observation uses the Table scroll area while the Table windows its rows, and the browser viewport otherwise, with zero look-ahead and no ancestor discovery. Without IntersectionObserver, the same manual command works.

props.name: hasMore
props.description: Whether the source can provide another batch. False removes loading chrome and observation. Only a focused removed command hands focus to the shared Table viewport, without scrolling.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Caller-controlled loading. Blocks requests while true. The outstanding request latch also keeps the Button busy through Promise settlement and the next false commit.

props.name: onLoadMore
props.description: Fetch and append the next batch, returning its completion Promise. Rows, cursors, errors and stale-response suppression stay caller-owned. Callback identity changes do not reset pending work or failure pause.

components.name: useTablePagination
components.description: Call useTablePagination with a config object containing page state and callback. T is the row type; TypeScript cannot infer it from the config, so it defaults to Record<string, unknown>, which a Table with typed rows rejects: pass it, as in `useTablePagination<Walk>(…)` for `<Table<Walk>>`. Pass the returned plugin to Table via the plugins prop.

props.name: page
props.description: Current page number (1-based).

props.name: onPageChange
props.description: Called when the page changes.

props.name: totalItems
props.description: Total number of items across all pages. Used to calculate total page count.

props.name: totalPages
props.description: Total number of pages. Use when you know the page count but not item count.

props.name: hasMore
props.description: Whether more pages exist. Use for cursor-based pagination where the total is unknown.

props.name: pageSize
props.description: Number of items per page.

props.name: onPageSizeChange
props.description: Called when the user changes the page size. Shows a page size dropdown when provided with pageSizeOptions.

props.name: pageSizeOptions
props.description: Available page size options. Shows a page size selector when provided.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual variant for the pagination controls.

props.name: position
props.description: Where to render pagination controls relative to the table.

props.name: align
props.description: Horizontal alignment of the pagination controls.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the pagination nav landmark. With position='both' the two navs get distinct names (the label suffixed as '(top)' and '(bottom)') so same-type landmarks stay unique (axe landmark-unique).

components.name: useTableRowExpansion
components.description: Hook that returns a TablePlugin which expands a full-width detail panel below a row, rendered by the consumer via renderExpanded(item). Adds a leading chevron column and a right-click "Expand/Collapse row" action; the consumer owns the expandedKeys set. The panel spans the row but starts its content at the first column, past the chevron, so detail lines up with the labels above it; the inset follows the table density. Use it for master-detail rows (order details, forms, charts, nested tables). For hierarchical data where child rows reuse the parent columns, use useTableTreeData + useTableTreeState instead.

props.name: expandedKeys
props.description: Set of currently-expanded row keys. Consumer-owned.

props.name: onToggle
props.description: Called with a row key when its expansion is toggled (chevron click or context-menu action).

props.name: getRowKey
props.description: Derive a stable unique key from a row item.

props.name: getRowLabel
props.description: Derive a human-readable row identity for the chevron accessible name. Astryx combines it with localized expand/collapse wording. Omit it, or return blank text, to keep the generic "Expand row" and "Collapse row" labels.

props.name: renderExpanded
props.description: Render the detail content shown in a full-width panel below the row when it is expanded. Receives the row item.

props.name: getIsItemExpandable
props.description: Control which rows are expandable. Non-expandable rows show no chevron, no context-menu action, and never render a panel. Defaults to all rows expandable.

props.name: panelVariant
props.description: Background behind the detail panel. 'transparent' (default) paints nothing: the panel is the row's continuation and takes whatever surface the table sits on, so a Card shows through and a striped table's zebra reads on unchanged. 'muted' washes it, marking it as commentary rather than another row of data — reach for it in a bare table with no card, dividers or striping, where nothing else makes that distinction. The wash is a low-alpha near-black, so it is close to invisible over a dark card: 'muted' is largely a light-theme effect.

props.name: hasRowClickExpansion
props.description: Toggle a row by clicking anywhere on it, not only on its chevron. A pointer-only convenience layered over the chevron, which stays the accessible control for keyboard and assistive tech. Clicks on interactive cell content (buttons, links, form controls) or on a text selection do not toggle, and non-expandable rows stay inert.

props.name: animatedLayout
props.description: A handle from useAnimatedLayout. With it, opening or closing a panel glides the rows after it (and the content after the table) to their new places instead of jumping, the opening panel plays in on the same motion, and each row's divider moves with it. Under Reduce Motion the rows fade in place on a touch screen and change at once with a mouse; in a table with column lines (dividers columns or grid, which do not move yet) they change at once. Without it, rows jump.

components.name: useTableRowIndex
components.description: Hook that returns a TablePlugin which prepends a right-aligned, monospaced row-number column, starting at 1 by default. Without data, Table supplies row positions; with data, ordinary numbers follow that array. Windowed rows use the parent Table logical position directly; nondefault startFrom values use full rendering.

props.name: data
props.description: Optional: the array whose order the numbers follow. Omit it to number rows from the positions Table gives them.

props.name: getRowKey
props.description: Optional key extractor used with data, returning a unique string per row. When provided, rows match data by the returned string; otherwise by reference identity. Memoize with useCallback for a stable plugin identity.

props.name: label
props.description: Header label for the index column.

props.name: startFrom
props.description: First index value.

components.name: useTableRowStatus
components.description: Hook that returns a TablePlugin which prepends a narrow column signaling per-row status. Return {status, label} for a semantic success, warning, or error: Table resolves the matching glyph and tone through the active theme. Return {color, icon?, label} for a custom marker: every color is paint-only, an omitted icon renders the stable 8px dot, and an explicit icon renders that caller-selected glyph. Named custom icons keep their released Icon color mapping; raw CSS custom icons inherit the caller's exact paint instead of the previous primary fallback. Existing callers require no source migration. label is required and becomes the accessible image name plus supplemental hover tooltip; return null for no indicator. The column header is visually blank but carries a screen-reader-only localized name ("Row status", i18n key @astryx.table.rowStatus.columnHeader). Memoize getStatus with useCallback for a stable plugin identity.

props.name: getStatus
props.type: (item: T) => ({ status: 'success' | 'warning' | 'error'; color?: never; icon?: never; label: string } | { status?: never; color: 'accent' | 'success' | 'error' | 'warning' | 'red' | 'orange' | 'green' | 'yellow' | 'blue' | 'gray' | string; icon?: IconName; label: string }) | null
props.description: Derive either a semantic outcome or a custom marker. {status, label} accepts the closed success/error/warning vocabulary and resolves its glyph and tone through the active theme. {color, icon?, label} preserves the stable custom-marker path: color always selects paint, no icon renders an 8px dot, and icon renders the explicit caller glyph. Even color values named success/error/warning remain dots without icon. Valid icon names: close, chevronDown, chevronLeft, chevronRight, chevronsLeft, chevronsRight, check, success, error, warning, info, calendar, clock, externalLink, menu, moreHorizontal, search, upload, arrowUp, arrowDown, arrowsUpDown, funnel, eyeSlash, viewColumns, copy, checkDouble, wrench, stop, microphone. The branches are exclusive, label is required and announced via role="img", and null leaves the row status cell empty. Memoize with useCallback for a stable plugin identity.

components.name: useTableRowsVirtualization
components.description: Returns an opaque capability for fixed-height flat-row Table windowing. Pass the capability to Table.virtualization and keep the complete data, columns, explicit stable idKey and plugins on Table. Sizes are positive finite CSS pixels. The Table scrolls inside the height its parent gives it and fills all of it. Give the Table's parent a height, fixed or relative, or a flex child, so windowing can bound the rows; with no height every row renders. Make the Table the parent's only child, or a flex child with min-height: 0 beside a heading or toolbar. Supported rows use single-line content; explicit wrapping, non-flat rows or invalid identity use ordinary full rendering. What stays windowed: a column without renderCell (its default cell renders the row's value as single-line text) and the row-number (useTableRowIndex, counting from 1) and selection (useTableSelection) columns. A column with a custom renderCell turns windowing off for the whole table, because Table cannot check that the cell keeps the fixed row height; it renders every row and warns in development, naming the column. A useTableRowStatus column, or a useTableRowIndex column that counts from another number, turns windowing off too. To window a table, put the text a column shows in the row data and leave renderCell off that column. Windowing uses the Table-owned scroll wrapper; a caller-provided scrollWrapper takes diagnostic full-render fallback. Mounted rows retain native table semantics and full-table positions; unmounted rows are not promised screen-reader discovery.

props.name: rowHeight
props.description: Total body-row pitch in CSS pixels, including existing density padding and collapsed borders. Must fit text and supported controls without reducing their size. When every row measures taller, as with enlarged text or zoom, the Table windows at the measured height and warns in development; rows of unequal height render every row.

props.name: initialViewportHeight
props.description: The viewport height in CSS pixels that the first window plans for, on the server and before the viewport is measured. It does not size the Table: the Table scrolls inside the height its parent gives it, and after mount the measured viewport sets the window. Table accounts for its headers and chrome.

components.name: useTableSelection
components.description: Hook that returns a TablePlugin implementing row selection with checkboxes, select-all, and aria-selected. Uses React Context for independent checkbox re-renders.

props.name: getIsItemSelected
props.description: Returns whether the given item is currently selected.

props.name: onSelectItem
props.description: Called when a row checkbox is toggled. isSelected is the new desired state.

props.name: onSelectAll
props.description: Called when the select-all header checkbox is toggled.

props.name: getIsAllSelected
props.description: Returns whether all selectable items are currently selected.

props.name: getIsIndeterminate
props.description: Returns whether selection is partial (some but not all). Renders the select-all checkbox in indeterminate state.

props.name: getIsItemSelectable
props.description: Returns false for a row that can never be selected (no checkbox, an empty selection cell), unlike getIsItemEnabled, which shows a disabled checkbox. Use it for rows such as a read-only system row. This hook does not change select-all: your onSelectAll and getIsAllSelected must skip these rows. useTableSelectionState does this for you.

props.name: getIsItemEnabled
props.description: Returns false for a selectable row whose checkbox shows but is disabled and keeps its checked state, unlike getIsItemSelectable, which removes the checkbox. Use it for rows that are selectable in other conditions, such as a locked or busy row. This hook does not change select-all: your onSelectAll must not add or remove these rows. useTableSelectionState does this for you.

props.name: getRowLabel
props.description: Derives a human-readable identity for a row; the row checkbox's hidden label becomes `Select ${getRowLabel(item)}` so screen readers announce which row each checkbox selects. Falls back to "Select row" when omitted.

props.name: hasRowHighlight
props.description: Paints checked rows with the accent wash. Set false when the surrounding UI already uses row background to mean something else (a row open in a detail panel, say).
